summary.en: Germanic tribes led by Arminius ambushed and destroyed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus. The defeat ended Augustus's plans to push the frontier to the Elbe, leaving the Rhine as the lasting boundary of Roman power.
summary.zh: 阿米尼乌斯率领的日耳曼部落伏击并全歼瓦卢斯统率的三个罗马军团。此役使奥古斯都放弃将边界推进至易北河的计划，莱茵河由此成为罗马势力的长期边界。

sources.title: Tacitus, Annals I.60–62
Cassius Dio, Roman History LVI.18–24
Britannica: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest

events.note: Month (September 9 CE) is known but not the exact days; the battlefield is identified with the Kalkriese archaeological site (Wikidata coordinates), which most but not all scholars accept.

summary.en: A few thousand Han loyalists under Liu Xiu broke a vastly larger Xin army besieging Kunyang. The rout doomed Wang Mang, whose capital Chang'an fell to rebels later that year.
summary.zh: 刘秀率数千汉军冲破围攻昆阳的新莽大军，王莽主力溃散，同年长安被起义军攻破，王莽被杀。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

资治通鉴 卷39 汉纪三十一 淮阳王更始元年

summary.en: The sisters Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị led the Lạc lords of the Red River delta in revolt against the Han governor of Jiaozhi and ruled for about three years from Mê Linh, until the Han general Ma Yuan crushed the rising in 43.
summary.zh: 征侧、征贰姐妹率领红河三角洲的雒将起兵反抗东汉交趾太守，以麊泠为中心自立约三年，43年被东汉将领马援镇压。

sources.title: Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han), "Biography of Ma Yuan" and "Treatise on the Southern Man"
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Trưng sisters' rebellion

name.en: Founding of the White Horse Temple

summary.en: Traditionally regarded as China's first Buddhist temple, founded outside Luoyang under Emperor Ming after envoys returned from the west with the monks Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna.
summary.zh: 相传汉明帝遣使西行求法，迎摄摩腾、竺法兰至洛阳，于城西建白马寺，被视为中国第一座佛寺。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
杨衒之《洛阳伽蓝记》卷4 白马寺
Britannica: White Horse Temple

events.note: The founding date of 68 is traditional.

summary.en: Roman legions under Titus besieged Jerusalem during the First Jewish–Roman War. The city fell in late summer 70 and the Second Temple was destroyed, a turning point for Judaism and for Jewish life in Judaea.
summary.zh: 第一次犹太-罗马战争期间，提图斯率罗马军团围攻耶路撒冷。公元70年夏末城破，第二圣殿被毁，成为犹太教历史和犹地亚犹太人生活的转折点。

sources.title: Josephus, The Jewish War, Books V–VI
Encyclopaedia Britannica: First Jewish Revolt
Wikipedia: Siege of Jerusalem (70 CE)

summary.en: Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii, Herculaneum and neighbouring towns under ash and pyroclastic flows. Pliny the Younger's letters describe the disaster, in which his uncle Pliny the Elder died; the buried cities became key archaeological sites.
summary.zh: 维苏威火山喷发，火山灰和火山碎屑流掩埋了庞贝、赫库兰尼姆及周边城镇。小普林尼的书信记录了这场灾难，其舅父老普林尼在救援中遇难；被掩埋的城市后来成为重要的考古遗址。

sources.title: Pliny the Younger, Letters VI.16 and VI.20
Britannica: Mount Vesuvius
Britannica: Pompeii

events.note: Wikidata gives 24 October 79, supported by a charcoal inscription found at Pompeii in 2018; the manuscript tradition of Pliny's letter gives 24 August. The year is undisputed.

wiki.en: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD
wiki.zh: 西元79年維蘇威火山爆發

name.en: Battle of Ikh Bayan and the Yanran inscription
name.zh: 稽落山之战与燕然勒石

summary.en: General Dou Xian crushed the Northern Xiongnu at Mount Jiluo and had Ban Gu compose a victory inscription carved on Mount Yanran in the Khangai range, rediscovered in Mongolia in 2017.
summary.zh: 窦宪大破北匈奴于稽落山，登燕然山命班固作铭刻石记功；该摩崖石刻于2017年在蒙古国杭爱山发现。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
范晔《后汉书》卷23 窦宪传

summary.en: On Emperor Hadrian's orders, Roman legions began building a stone and turf barrier about 118 km long across northern Britain, from the Tyne to the Solway Firth. It marked and controlled the empire's north-western frontier for most of the next three centuries.
summary.zh: 罗马军团奉哈德良皇帝之命，在不列颠北部自泰恩河至索尔威湾修筑长约118公里的石土城墙。此后近三百年间，它大体标志并管控着帝国的西北边疆。

sources.title: Historia Augusta, Life of Hadrian 11.2
Britannica: Hadrian's Wall
UNESCO: Frontiers of the Roman Empire

events.note: Construction began c. 122 and the main work was completed c. 128; both dates are approximate.

name.zh: 迦腻色伽即位（罗巴塔克铭文）

summary.en: The Bactrian-language Rabatak inscription, found in northern Afghanistan in 1993, records Kanishka’s royal genealogy and the first year of his era, when Kushan authority reached cities of the Ganges plain. Most scholars now place that year near 127 CE.
summary.zh: 1993年在阿富汗北部发现的大夏语罗巴塔克铭文记载了迦腻色伽的王统世系及其纪元元年，当时贵霜势力已达恒河平原诸城。今多数学者将该元年定在公元127年前后。

sources.title: N. Sims-Williams & J. Cribb, “A new Bactrian inscription of Kanishka the Great”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 4 (1996)
Harry Falk, “The yuga of Sphujiddhvaja and the era of the Kuṣāṇas”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 7 (2001)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kanishka
Wikidata Q2382049

events.note: Kanishka’s accession has been placed anywhere between 78 and 144 CE; 127 follows Falk (2001) and is now the majority view. The inscription itself gives only regnal year 1.

summary.en: At Luoyang the astronomer Zhang Heng built the Houfeng Didong Yi, a bronze vessel said to drop a ball from a dragon's mouth toward the direction of a distant earthquake.
summary.zh: 太史令张衡在洛阳制成候风地动仪，据载地震时对应方向的龙口吐丸，可感知远方地震。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
范晔《后汉书》卷59 张衡传

summary.en: Simon bar Kokhba led a Jewish uprising in Judaea against Hadrian, provoked in part by plans to refound Jerusalem as the Roman colony Aelia Capitolina. Its suppression, ending at Betar, devastated Judaea, and the province was renamed Syria Palaestina.
summary.zh: 西蒙·巴尔·科赫巴领导犹地亚犹太人反抗哈德良，起因之一是罗马计划把耶路撒冷重建为殖民城市爱利亚加比多连。起义最终在贝塔尔被镇压，犹地亚遭到重创，行省更名为叙利亚-巴勒斯坦。

sources.title: Cassius Dio, Roman History 69.12–14
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Second Jewish Revolt
Wikipedia: Bar Kokhba Revolt

summary.en: Zhang Jue's Taiping Dao movement rose across eastern China in 184. The main armies were crushed within a year, but the emergency powers granted to regional commanders opened the way to warlordism.
summary.zh: 张角以太平道起事于巨鹿，八州并起。主力当年即被镇压，但余部延续二十年，地方将帅坐大，开启军阀割据。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
范晔《后汉书》卷71 皇甫嵩传
资治通鉴 卷58 汉纪五十 光和七年

events.note: Wikidata ends the rebellion in 205 (remnant risings); the main outbreak was 184, as in Jiangshan-map.

image.file: Three Brothers during the Yellow Turban Rebellion.jpg

summary.en: Dong Zhuo's seizure of Luoyang in 189 reduced the Han emperors to puppets; Cao Cao later controlled Emperor Xian from Xu, and in 220 his son Cao Pi accepted the abdication and founded Wei.
summary.zh: 189年董卓入洛废立，汉帝沦为傀儡；曹操迎献帝都许挟天子以令诸侯，220年曹丕受禅建魏，东汉亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Cao Cao defeated the far larger army of Yuan Shao by burning its grain depot at Wuchao, gaining control of north China.
summary.zh: 曹操奇袭乌巢焚毁袁绍粮草，以少胜多大败袁军，奠定统一北方的基础。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: The allied fleets of Sun Quan and Liu Bei, led by Zhou Yu, burned Cao Cao's armada on the Yangtze near Wulin, halting his drive south and setting the stage for the Three Kingdoms.
summary.zh: 孙权、刘备联军由周瑜指挥，黄盖火攻，于乌林焚毁曹操战船，阻止其南下，奠定三国鼎立格局。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
陈寿《三国志》卷54 吴书九 周瑜传
资治通鉴 卷65 汉纪五十七 建安十三年

summary.en: Liu Bei invaded Wu to avenge Guan Yu and recover Jingzhou; the Wu commander Lu Xun waited, then burned the Shu camps strung along the gorges at Yiling, and Liu Bei withdrew to Baidicheng.
summary.zh: 刘备为报关羽之仇、夺回荆州而伐吴，陆逊坚守待机，于夷陵火烧连营，刘备败退白帝城。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
陈寿《三国志》卷58 吴书十三 陆逊传
资治通鉴 卷69 魏纪一 黄初三年

events.note: The campaign began in 221 (Wikidata date) and the decisive fire attack came in 222 (Jiangshan-map date).

name.en: Battle of Hormozdgan (founding of the Sasanian Empire)
name.zh: 霍尔木兹甘之战（萨珊王朝建立）

summary.en: Ardashir, a Persian vassal king from Fars, defeated and killed the Parthian king Artabanus IV. The victory ended nearly five centuries of Arsacid rule and founded the Sasanian Empire, which rivalled Rome for four hundred years.
summary.zh: 法尔斯的波斯藩王阿尔达希尔击败并杀死安息国王阿尔达班四世。此战结束了阿萨息斯王朝近五百年的统治，建立了此后与罗马抗衡四百年的萨珊王朝。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Hormizdagan
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Sasanian dynasty
al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. V (trans. Bosworth)

events.note: The battlefield has not been located; the date 28 April 224 is the conventional reconstruction.

summary.en: From Hanzhong, Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang launched five campaigns against Wei through the Qinling passes. Supply problems and Sima Yi's defensive strategy stalled them, and he died in camp at Wuzhang Plains in 234.
summary.zh: 蜀相诸葛亮以汉中为基地，越秦岭五次北伐曹魏。粮运艰难，司马懿坚壁不战，234年病逝五丈原军中。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

资治通鉴 卷71–72 魏纪三、四

summary.en: While regent Cao Shuang escorted the Wei emperor to the Gaoping tombs, Sima Yi seized Luoyang and then executed Cao Shuang's faction, putting the Sima clan in control of Wei.
summary.zh: 曹爽奉魏帝谒高平陵之际，司马懿闭城发动政变，诛曹爽一党，司马氏自此掌握曹魏朝政。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Shapur I defeated a Roman army near Edessa and captured Emperor Valerian, the first Roman emperor taken prisoner by a foreign enemy. Shapur commemorated the triumph in rock reliefs and in his trilingual inscription at Naqsh-e Rostam.
summary.zh: 沙普尔一世在埃德萨附近击败罗马军队，俘虏皇帝瓦勒良——这是第一位被外敌俘获的罗马皇帝。沙普尔在纳克什-鲁斯塔姆以浮雕和三语铭文纪念此役。

sources.title: Shapur I, inscription on the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht (ŠKZ), Naqsh-e Rostam
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Shapur I
Wikipedia: Battle of Edessa

events.note: Usually dated 260; some scholars prefer 259.

summary.en: Wei armies under Zhong Hui and Deng Ai invaded Shu; while Jiang Wei held Jiange, Deng Ai crossed the mountains by the Yinping trail and reached Chengdu, where Liu Shan surrendered.
summary.zh: 钟会、邓艾分道伐蜀，姜维据守剑阁，邓艾偷渡阴平直抵成都，后主刘禅出降，蜀汉亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Six Jin columns attacked Wu, and Wang Jun's fleet sailed down the Yangtze from Sichuan to Jianye, where Sun Hao surrendered in 280, reunifying China for the first time since the Han.
summary.zh: 西晋六路伐吴，王濬楼船自益州顺江而下直抵建业，280年孙皓出降，结束三国分裂。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: A succession of Jin princes, beginning with Empress Jia's coup, fought for control of the weak Emperor Hui. The civil wars devastated the north and drew Xiongnu and other frontier troops into Chinese politics.
summary.zh: 贾后乱政后，宗室诸王为控制晋惠帝相继混战十六年，中原残破，匈奴等内迁部族借机起兵。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: According to Armenian tradition, King Tiridates III was converted by Gregory the Illuminator and made Christianity the religion of his kingdom, the first state to adopt it officially. The cathedral of Etchmiadzin was founded at the royal city of Vagharshapat.
summary.zh: 据亚美尼亚传统，国王梯里达底三世受启蒙者格列高利感化而皈依，并定基督教为国教，使亚美尼亚成为第一个正式奉基督教为国教的国家。埃奇米阿津大教堂建于王城瓦加尔沙帕特。

sources.title: Agathangelos, History of the Armenians
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tiridates III
Wikipedia: Christianization of Armenia

events.note: Traditional date 301; many historians prefer c. 314.

summary.en: Han-Zhao forces under Liu Yao and Wang Mi stormed Luoyang, captured Emperor Huai and burned the city, triggering a mass migration of northern elites south of the Yangtze.
summary.zh: 汉赵刘曜、王弥攻陷洛阳，俘晋怀帝，焚掠宫城，引发中原士族大规模南迁（衣冠南渡）。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《资治通鉴》 卷87 晋纪九 永嘉五年六月

房玄龄等《晋书》卷5 孝怀帝纪 永嘉五年

summary.en: Meeting in Milan, the emperors Constantine I and Licinius agreed to grant religious freedom throughout the empire and to restore confiscated property to Christians. The policy ended state persecution and opened the way for Christianity's rise to imperial favour.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁一世与李锡尼在米兰会晤，同意在帝国境内给予宗教自由，并归还被没收的基督徒财产。这一政策终结了官方迫害，为基督教获得帝国青睐铺平了道路。

sources.title: Lactantius, De mortibus persecutorum 48
Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History X.5
Britannica: Edict of Milan

events.note: The agreement was reached at Milan in February 313; the surviving text is a rescript issued by Licinius at Nicomedia in June 313.

summary.en: The accession of Chandragupta I at Pataliputra, linked in Gupta coinage to his marriage alliance with the Licchavis, became the epoch of the Gupta era used in inscriptions across northern India for centuries.
summary.zh: 旃陀罗笈多一世在华氏城即位，笈多钱币将此与其和离车族的联姻相联系；这一年成为笈多纪元的起点，此后数百年间北印度碑铭普遍采用。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gupta dynasty
Wikidata Q28174068

events.note: The era’s epoch is reckoned as 319–320 CE; Wikidata dates the broader “Gupta era” period from 318.

summary.en: Emperor Constantine convened bishops from across the empire at Nicaea in Bithynia. The council rejected Arianism, issued the original Nicene Creed and set common rules such as the method of dating Easter. It is counted as the first ecumenical council.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁皇帝召集帝国各地主教在比提尼亚的尼西亚开会。会议否定阿里乌派，颁布最初的《尼西亚信经》，并统一了复活节日期的推算等规定，被视为第一次大公会议。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Council of Nicaea
Eusebius, Life of Constantine, Book III
Wikipedia: First Council of Nicaea

summary.en: Constantine I formally dedicated his rebuilt city on the site of Byzantium as a new imperial residence, Constantinople. It became the capital of the eastern Roman, later Byzantine, empire for more than eleven centuries.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁一世在拜占庭旧址上重建城市，并正式将其奉献为新的帝国驻地——君士坦丁堡。此后一千一百余年，它一直是东罗马即拜占庭帝国的首都。

sources.title: Chronicon Paschale, year 330
Socrates Scholasticus, Ecclesiastical History I.16
Britannica: Istanbul

events.note: QID is the historical city of Constantinople, whose inception Wikidata gives as 330.

summary.en: Wang Xizhi hosted some forty literati at the Orchid Pavilion near Shanyin (Shaoxing) for the spring purification festival and wrote the preface to their poems, later revered as the supreme work of Chinese calligraphy.
summary.zh: 王羲之与谢安等四十余人修禊于会稽山阴兰亭，作《兰亭集序》，被后世尊为“天下第一行书”。

summary.en: Gothic forces, mainly Tervingi under Fritigern joined by Greuthungi cavalry, destroyed an eastern Roman army near Adrianople; Emperor Valens was killed. The disaster left the Goths settled inside the empire and is often seen as a turning point in the late Roman crisis.
summary.zh: 以弗里提格伦为首的哥特人（主要为特尔温吉部，并有格鲁森尼骑兵增援）在阿德里安堡附近歼灭东罗马军队，瓦伦斯皇帝阵亡。此役使哥特人得以定居帝国境内，常被视为罗马晚期危机的转折点。

sources.title: Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae XXXI.12–13
Britannica: Battle of Adrianople

events.note: Date is secure; the exact battlefield, some kilometres north of Adrianople (Edirne), is unknown—coordinates follow Wikidata's approximation.

summary.en: Fu Jian's huge Former Qin army, attempting to conquer the south, was routed at the Fei River near Shouyang by about 80,000 Eastern Jin troops under Xie Xuan; the defeat broke up Former Qin.
summary.zh: 前秦苻坚倾国南下，于寿阳淝水被谢玄所率八万北府兵击溃，前秦随之瓦解，南北对峙之局延续。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: A seven-metre wrought-iron column bearing a Sanskrit eulogy of a king “Chandra”, usually identified with Chandragupta II, it was forged around 400 CE and has resisted corrosion remarkably; it now stands in the Qutb complex in Delhi.
summary.zh: 这根约七米高的熟铁柱刻有赞颂“旃陀罗”王的梵文铭文，一般认为即旃陀罗笈多二世；约铸于公元400年，至今几乎不锈，现立于德里顾特卜建筑群内。

sources.title: R. Balasubramaniam, Delhi Iron Pillar: New Insights (2002)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Iron pillar of Delhi
Wikidata Q543419

events.note: Dated by palaeography to c. 400 CE (Wikidata: 5th century); it was probably moved to Delhi from elsewhere, possibly Udayagiri, centuries later.

summary.en: The monk Mesrop Mashtots, supported by King Vramshapuh and Catholicos Sahak, devised a 36-letter alphabet for Armenian. It launched the translation of the Bible and a native literature that anchored Armenian identity.
summary.zh: 修士梅斯罗布·马什托茨在国王弗拉姆沙普和大主教萨哈克支持下，为亚美尼亚语创制了36个字母。由此开始了《圣经》翻译和本土文学创作，奠定了亚美尼亚民族认同。

sources.title: Koriun, The Life of Mashtots
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Saint Mesrop Mashtots
Wikipedia: Armenian alphabet

events.note: c. 405 following Koriun; exact year debated.

name.en: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths

summary.en: Visigoths under Alaric I entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time in about 800 years that the city had fallen to a foreign enemy. The shock across the Roman world prompted Augustine to write The City of God.
summary.zh: 阿拉里克一世率领的西哥特人攻入罗马城并劫掠三日，这是近八百年来罗马首次落入外敌之手。此事震动整个罗马世界，促使奥古斯丁写下《上帝之城》。

sources.title: Orosius, Seven Books of History against the Pagans VII.39
Augustine, De civitate Dei, Book I
Britannica: Alaric

image.file: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths on 24 August 410 by JN Sylvestre 1890.jpg

summary.en: King Jangsu of Goguryeo raised a 6-metre stone stele near the capital Gungnae (modern Ji'an) to commemorate his father Gwanggaeto. Its roughly 1,800 characters record the dynasty's origins and Gwanggaeto's campaigns and are a key source for early relations between Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla and Wa.
summary.zh: 高句丽长寿王在国内城（今集安）附近立起高约六米的石碑，纪念其父广开土王。碑文约一千八百字，记述王室起源与广开土王的征战，是研究高句丽、百济、新罗与倭早期关系的重要史料。

sources.title: Gwanggaeto Stele inscription (414)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Gwanggaeto Stele

summary.en: Founded under the Gupta king Kumaragupta I, Nalanda grew into Asia’s foremost Buddhist monastic university, drawing scholars such as Xuanzang and Yijing, until it declined after attacks around 1200.
summary.zh: 那烂陀寺创建于笈多王鸠摩罗笈多一世时期，发展为亚洲首屈一指的佛教寺院大学，玄奘、义净等皆曾来此求学，约1200年遭攻击后衰落。

sources.title: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji (Records of the Western Regions), tr. Samuel Beal (1884)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara at Nalanda, Bihar
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nalanda
Wikidata Q216243

events.note: The c. 427 founding date is conventional, resting on seals naming Kumaragupta I (r. c. 415–455) and on Xuanzang’s account.

summary.en: A coalition of Romans under Flavius Aetius and Visigoths under Theodoric I fought Attila's Hunnic army in north-eastern Gaul. Theodoric fell, but Attila withdrew, ending his invasion of Gaul.
summary.zh: 罗马统帅埃提乌斯与西哥特国王狄奥多里克一世的联军，在高卢东北部迎战阿提拉的匈人大军。狄奥多里克阵亡，但阿提拉被迫撤退，其入侵高卢的行动就此终止。

sources.title: Jordanes, Getica 36–41
Britannica: Battle of Châlons

events.note: The site is unknown—placed by sources between Châlons-en-Champagne and Troyes; the day (20 June, per Wikidata) is a modern reconstruction. Wikidata's English label is 'Battle of the Maureaco Fields'.

image.file: De Neuville - The Huns at the Battle of Chalons.jpg

summary.en: The fourth ecumenical council, meeting at Chalcedon across the Bosporus from Constantinople, defined Christ as one person in two natures. Many Christians in Egypt, Syria and Armenia rejected it, producing the lasting split between Chalcedonian and Oriental Orthodox churches.
summary.zh: 第四次大公会议在君士坦丁堡对岸的迦克墩召开，确定基督为“一个位格、两种本性”。埃及、叙利亚和亚美尼亚的许多基督徒拒绝这一定义，形成迦克墩派与东方正统教会之间的长期分裂。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Council of Chalcedon
R. Price & M. Gaddis (trans.), The Acts of the Council of Chalcedon (2005)
Wikipedia: Council of Chalcedon

name.zh: 阿旃陀石窟（伐迦陀迦时期）

summary.en: Under the Vakataka king Harisena, Buddhist patrons cut most of Ajanta’s richly painted caves within a few decades, adding to an earlier group of the 2nd–1st centuries BCE. The murals are the finest surviving ancient Indian paintings.
summary.zh: 在伐迦陀迦王诃利犀那统治时期，佛教施主于数十年间开凿了阿旃陀的大部分彩绘石窟，与公元前2至前1世纪的早期洞窟相接续。其壁画是现存最精美的古印度绘画。

sources.title: Walter M. Spink, Ajanta: History and Development, vol. 1 (2005)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Ajanta Caves
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ajanta Caves
Wikidata Q184427

events.note: Spink’s short chronology (c. 460–480) is influential but debated; Wikidata’s start date (c. 2nd century BCE) refers to the earliest caves.

image.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Soman assumed (based on copyright claims).

name.zh: 罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯被废黜

summary.en: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. The date conventionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire, though its decline had been long and gradual.
summary.zh: 日耳曼将领奥多亚克在拉文纳废黜少年皇帝罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯，并将帝国徽章送往君士坦丁堡。这一年通常被视为西罗马帝国灭亡的标志，尽管其衰落是一个漫长渐进的过程。

sources.title: Anonymus Valesianus, pars posterior 8.38
Britannica: Odoacer
Peter Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire (2005)

wiki.en: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

name.zh: 迦叶波一世营建狮子岩

summary.en: King Kashyapa I of Anuradhapura moved his court to this granite monolith, crowning it with a palace and surrounding it with frescoes, water gardens and a lion gateway; after his fall it became a Buddhist monastery.
summary.zh: 阿努拉德普勒王迦叶波一世将宫廷迁至这块花岗岩巨石，在其顶部建宫殿，四周饰以壁画、水园和狮爪门；其败亡后此地改为佛教寺院。

sources.title: Culavamsa, ch. 39 (tr. Wilhelm Geiger, 1929)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Ancient City of Sigiriya
K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (1981)
Wikidata Q272153

events.note: Kashyapa’s reign (c. 477–495) is dated from the Culavamsa chronicle.

name.en: Emperor Xiaowen moves the capital to Luoyang

summary.en: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei moved his court from Pingcheng to Luoyang and imposed Chinese dress, language and surnames on the Xianbei aristocracy as part of his sinicisation reforms.
summary.zh: 北魏孝文帝自平城迁都洛阳，推行改汉服、说汉语、改汉姓等汉化改革。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Clovis I, king of the Franks, was baptised a Catholic Christian by Bishop Remigius at Reims. Choosing Nicene Christianity rather than the Arianism of other Germanic kings won him the support of the Gallo-Roman church and population.
summary.zh: 法兰克国王克洛维一世在兰斯由主教雷米吉乌斯施洗，皈依天主教。他选择尼西亚派而非其他日耳曼诸王所信奉的阿里乌派，因而赢得高卢—罗马教会与民众的支持。

sources.title: Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks II.31
Britannica: Clovis I

events.note: Gregory of Tours' chronology implies c. 496; modern historians place the baptism anywhere between 496 and 508. Wikidata has no date.

name.zh: 阿耶波多著《阿耶波多历书》

summary.en: Writing at Kusumapura (Pataliputra) aged 23, Aryabhata set out place-value computation, an accurate value of π, a sine table and the daily rotation of the Earth, shaping Indian mathematical astronomy for a millennium.
summary.zh: 阿耶波多23岁时在拘苏摩补罗（华氏城）写成此书，阐述位值计算、精确的圆周率、正弦表以及地球自转之说，影响印度数理天文学达千年之久。

sources.title: Kim Plofker, Mathematics in India (2009)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Aryabhata I
Wikidata Q3518429

summary.en: Neglected northern frontier garrisons of Northern Wei rose under Poliuhan Baling at Woye. The revolts brought warlords such as Erzhu Rong, Gao Huan and Yuwen Tai to power and split the empire.
summary.zh: 北魏北边六镇军民因地位沦落而起事，破六韩拔陵首倡于沃野镇。尔朱荣、高欢、宇文泰由此崛起，北魏终至分裂。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
魏收《魏书》卷9 肃宗纪 正光五年
资治通鉴 卷149 梁纪五 普通五年

events.note: Jiangshan-map dates the outbreak to 523 (Huaihuang mutiny); Poliuhan Baling's rising at Woye, Wikidata's start, is dated 524 in the Zizhi Tongjian.

summary.en: A powerful earthquake, followed by fire, destroyed much of Antioch, one of the great cities of the Eastern Roman Empire. Chroniclers reported about 250,000 deaths, probably an exaggeration but a sign of immense devastation.
summary.zh: 一场强烈地震及随后的大火摧毁了东罗马帝国大城安条克的大部分地区。编年史家记载死者约25万人，虽可能夸大，但足见灾难之惨烈。

sources.title: John Malalas, Chronographia, Book 17
E. Guidoboni, Catalogue of Ancient Earthquakes in the Mediterranean Area up to the 10th Century (1994)
Wikipedia: 526 Antioch earthquake

summary.en: Justinian I dedicated the rebuilt church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus. Its vast dome made it the largest church in Christendom for nearly a thousand years.
summary.zh: 查士丁尼一世为君士坦丁堡重建的圣索菲亚大教堂举行献堂礼，该教堂由特拉勒斯的安提米乌斯和米利都的伊西多尔设计。其巨大的穹顶使之在近千年间都是基督教世界最大的教堂。

sources.title: Procopius, Buildings I.1
Britannica: Hagia Sophia

events.note: Wikidata's start date (23 February 532) is when rebuilding began; this record marks the dedication of 27 December 537.

summary.en: Bubonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, reached the Mediterranean through Egypt in 541 and struck Constantinople in 542, killing a large share of its population. Recurring waves until the mid-8th century weakened the Byzantine Empire and its neighbours.
summary.zh: 由鼠疫杆菌引起的腺鼠疫于541年经埃及传入地中海世界，542年侵袭君士坦丁堡，造成大量人口死亡。此后直至8世纪中叶的反复流行，削弱了拜占庭帝国及其邻邦。

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars II.22–23
Lester K. Little (ed.), Plague and the End of Antiquity: The Pandemic of 541–750 (2007)

events.note: Wikidata spans all waves (541–750); endYear here marks the first wave. Placed at Constantinople, the best-documented outbreak (542).

summary.en: The defector Hou Jing rebelled against Liang, besieged Jiankang's palace city and starved Emperor Wu to death. The war ruined the Yangtze delta until Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian destroyed him.
summary.zh: 东魏降将侯景叛梁，围攻建康台城，梁武帝饿死。江南残破，至552年王僧辩、陈霸先平之。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
姚思廉《梁书》卷56 侯景传
资治通鉴 卷161–164 梁纪

summary.en: Yang Jian, regent for a child emperor of Northern Zhou, took the throne as Emperor Wen of Sui, built the new capital Daxing beside old Chang'an and issued the Kaihuang code; in 589 he conquered Chen.
summary.zh: 北周外戚杨坚受禅称帝建隋，营建大兴城，颁《开皇律》，确立三省六部制，589年灭陈统一。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

《隋书》 卷28 志第二十三 百官下 高祖官制

summary.en: The last and most destructive war between Rome and Persia. Khosrow II's armies took Syria, Jerusalem and Egypt, but Heraclius counter-attacked through the Caucasus, won near Nineveh in 627 and forced peace, leaving both empires exhausted on the eve of the Arab conquests.
summary.zh: 罗马与波斯之间最后也是最具破坏性的战争。霍斯劳二世的军队夺取叙利亚、耶路撒冷和埃及，但希拉克略经高加索反攻，627年在尼尼微附近获胜并迫使波斯议和，两大帝国在阿拉伯征服前夕均已精疲力竭。

sources.title: J. Howard-Johnston, The Last Great War of Antiquity (2021)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Heraclius
Wikipedia: Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628

events.note: Plotted near Nineveh, site of the decisive battle of 627.

summary.en: A set of moral and political injunctions for officials, drawing on Confucian and Buddhist ideals, which the Nihon Shoki attributes to Prince Shōtoku in 604. It stresses harmony, reverence for Buddhism and obedience to the sovereign.
summary.zh: 据《日本书纪》记载，圣德太子于604年制定了这一针对官员的道德与政治训诫，融合儒家与佛教思想，强调“以和为贵”、崇敬佛法、服从君主。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seventeen-article constitution
Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Seventeen-article constitution

events.note: Known only from the Nihon Shoki (720); its date and Shōtoku's authorship are debated by historians.

name.en: Construction of the Sui Grand Canal

summary.en: Emperor Yang linked Luoyang to the Huai and Yangtze by the Tongji Canal (605), to Zhuojun near Beijing by the Yongji Canal (608), and to Hangzhou by the Jiangnan Canal (610), creating China's north-south artery.
summary.zh: 隋炀帝相继开通济渠（605）、永济渠（608）、江南河（610），以洛阳为中心北抵涿郡、南达余杭，贯通南北水运。

summary.en: Islamic tradition holds that Muhammad, meditating in the cave of Hira on a mountain above Mecca, received the first verses of the Qur'an through the angel Gabriel. Muslims regard this as the beginning of his prophethood.
summary.zh: 据伊斯兰传统，穆罕默德在麦加附近山上的希拉山洞中静修时，经天使吉卜利勒（加百列）接受了《古兰经》最初的经文。穆斯林视此为其使命的开端。

sources.title: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad, 1955)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Muhammad
Wikipedia: Muhammad's first revelation

events.note: Traditional date c. 610.

summary.en: Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok lured a large Sui expeditionary force deep into the peninsula and destroyed it as it retreated across the Salsu (probably the Cheongcheon River). The disaster crippled Emperor Yang's campaigns against Goguryeo.
summary.zh: 高句丽将领乙支文德诱使隋朝远征大军深入，并在其撤退渡过萨水（一般认为即清川江）时予以重创。此役使隋炀帝征讨高句丽的战争严重受挫。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Suishu (Book of Sui, 636), annals of Emperor Yang
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Battle of Salsu

events.note: Wikidata gives no coordinates; the Salsu is usually identified with the Cheongcheon River near Anju, and Sui troop numbers in the sources are probably exaggerated.

summary.en: After Emperor Yang was killed at Jiangdu, Li Yuan, who had risen at Taiyuan and taken the capital, accepted the abdication of the puppet Emperor Gong and proclaimed the Tang dynasty at Chang'an.
summary.zh: 隋炀帝江都遇弑后，太原起兵入据长安的李渊迫隋恭帝禅位，于长安称帝建唐。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《资治通鉴》 卷185 唐纪一 武德元年三月；五月

《大唐创业起居注》 卷三 武德元年五月

summary.en: Harsha’s southward advance was halted on the Narmada by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, a victory celebrated in the Aihole inscription of 634; the river became the frontier between their realms.
summary.zh: 戒日王南下的攻势在讷尔默达河畔被遮娄其王补罗稽舍二世阻止，634年的艾霍莱铭文颂扬此胜；此后该河成为两国的分界。

sources.title: Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II (634 CE), Epigraphia Indica vol. 6
Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Wikidata Q115809322

events.note: Dated variously 618–619 or c. 630s; the exact battlefield on the Narmada is unknown, so the coordinates are approximate.

summary.en: Facing hostility in Mecca, Muhammad and his followers migrated to Yathrib, thereafter called Medina, where he founded the first Muslim community. The year of the migration later became the epoch of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.
summary.zh: 因在麦加受到敌视，穆罕默德与追随者迁往叶斯里卜（此后称麦地那），建立了第一个穆斯林社团。迁徙之年后来成为伊斯兰教历（希吉拉历）的纪元。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hijrah
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. Guillaume)
Wikipedia: Hijrah

summary.en: At the wells of Badr, a small Muslim force from Medina defeated a larger army of the Quraysh of Mecca. The victory, in the second year after the Hijra, greatly strengthened Muhammad's position in Arabia.
summary.zh: 在白德尔水井旁，麦地那的一支小规模穆斯林队伍击败了人数更多的麦加古莱什军队。这场发生在希吉拉后第二年的胜利大大巩固了穆罕默德在阿拉伯半岛的地位。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Badr
al-Waqidi, Kitab al-Maghazi
Wikipedia: Battle of Badr

summary.en: Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers, Crown Prince Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, at the Xuanwu Gate of the palace in Chang'an; within two months his father abdicated in his favour.
summary.zh: 秦王李世民在长安宫城玄武门伏兵杀太子建成、齐王元吉，两月后唐高祖传位，李世民即位为唐太宗。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《资治通鉴》 卷191 唐纪七 武德九年六月
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷2 太宗本纪上 武德九年
资治通鉴 卷191 唐纪七 武德九年

name.en: Tang defeat of the Eastern Turks at Yinshan

summary.en: Li Jing's surprise attack in the Yin Mountains destroyed the Eastern Turkic Khaganate and captured Illig Qaghan. The steppe chiefs then hailed Taizong as "Heavenly Khagan".
summary.zh: 李靖率军夜袭阴山，大破东突厥，擒颉利可汗。西北诸部尊唐太宗为“天可汗”。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《资治通鉴》 卷193 唐纪九 贞观四年
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷67 李靖传
资治通鉴 卷193 唐纪九 贞观四年

summary.en: The Chinese monk Xuanzang studied at Nalanda, met King Harsha at Kannauj and toured the subcontinent before returning to Chang’an with hundreds of texts; his Records of the Western Regions (646) is a key source for 7th-century India.
summary.zh: 唐僧玄奘在那烂陀寺求学，于曲女城会见戒日王，并遍游南亚次大陆，后携数百部经典返回长安；其《大唐西域记》（646年）是研究7世纪印度的重要史料。

sources.title: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji (Records of the Western Regions), tr. Samuel Beal (1884)
Huili, A Biography of the Tripitaka Master of the Great Ci’en Monastery
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Xuanzang
Wikidata Q1146069

events.note: The QID is the Records (completed 646); the travel dates (c. 630–645) come from that text and Huili’s biography.

summary.en: Muhammad entered Mecca with a large army almost without bloodshed. The idols around the Kaaba were removed and most of the Quraysh accepted Islam, making Mecca the religious centre of the new faith.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德率大军几乎兵不血刃地进入麦加。克尔白周围的偶像被清除，古莱什人大多皈依伊斯兰教，麦加从此成为这一新宗教的中心。

sources.title: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (trans. Guillaume)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Muhammad
Wikipedia: Conquest of Mecca

events.note: Wikidata gives 629; Muslim sources date it to Ramadan 8 AH, i.e. January 630 CE, which is used here.

summary.en: Within a century of Muhammad's death, Arab Muslim armies under the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphs conquered the Sasanian Empire, Byzantine Syria and Egypt, North Africa, Iberia and parts of Central Asia, creating one of the largest empires in history and reshaping the region's religions and languages.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德去世后不到一个世纪，四大哈里发和倭马亚王朝的阿拉伯穆斯林军队征服了萨珊帝国、拜占庭的叙利亚和埃及、北非、伊比利亚及中亚部分地区，建立起历史上最大的帝国之一，深刻改变了该地区的宗教与语言。

label.zh: 梅尔夫；伊嗣俟三世之死

sources.title: H. Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)
al-Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan
Wikipedia: Early Muslim conquests

events.note: Wikidata dates the overall process 622–750; here the start is 632, when expansion beyond Arabia began. Point is Wikidata's generic coordinate.

summary.en: Over six days by the Yarmouk River, a Rashidun army commanded by Khalid ibn al-Walid destroyed a large Byzantine force. The defeat ended Byzantine rule in Syria and opened the Levant to Muslim rule.
summary.zh: 在雅尔穆克河畔历时六天的战斗中，哈立德·本·瓦利德指挥的正统哈里发军队歼灭了一支庞大的拜占庭军队。此役终结了拜占庭对叙利亚的统治，黎凡特由此归于穆斯林。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of the Yarmuk River
H. Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)
Wikipedia: Battle of the Yarmuk

summary.en: An Arab army under Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas defeated the Sasanian general Rostam Farrokhzad in several days of fighting near al-Hira. The victory opened Mesopotamia and the Sasanian capital Ctesiphon to the Muslims.
summary.zh: 赛义德·本·阿比·瓦卡斯率领的阿拉伯军队在希拉附近经数日激战击败萨珊将领鲁斯塔姆。此役为穆斯林打开了美索不达米亚和萨珊首都泰西封的大门。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XII (trans. Friedmann)
Wikipedia: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah

events.note: Wikidata and most modern works give November 636; some sources date it to 637.

summary.en: Emperor Taizong sent Princess Wencheng to Rasa (Lhasa) as consort of the Tibetan emperor Songtsen Gampo, sealing an alliance; tradition credits her with bringing Buddhist images and Chinese crafts to Tibet.
summary.zh: 唐太宗以宗室女文成公主嫁吐蕃赞普松赞干布，唐蕃和亲；相传公主携佛像与工艺入藏。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《资治通鉴》 卷196 唐纪十二 贞观十五年正月
《旧唐书》 卷196上 列传第一百四十六上 吐蕃上
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷196上 吐蕃传上 贞观十五年

events.note: The Wikidata item is the princess herself; no separate item exists for the marriage.

image.artist: The original uploader was TibetInfopage at German Wikipedia.

summary.en: Arab forces defeated the last major Sasanian field army near Nahavand in the Zagros. Muslim chroniclers called it the "victory of victories"; afterwards Persian resistance fragmented and Yazdegerd III fled east.
summary.zh: 阿拉伯军队在扎格罗斯山区的纳哈万德附近击败萨珊最后一支主力野战军。穆斯林史家称之为“胜利中的胜利”；此后波斯抵抗分崩离析，伊嗣俟三世东逃。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Nahavand
al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XIII
Wikipedia: Battle of Nahavand

events.note: Dated 642 (some sources 641). Wikidata's coordinates duplicate al-Qadisiyyah; plotted here at Nahavand town.

summary.en: After the overthrow of the Soga clan in 645, Prince Naka no Ōe and Nakatomi no Kamatari launched reforms under Emperor Kōtoku modelled on Tang China: land and people were declared the sovereign's, and a centralised bureaucracy and tax system were planned from the new palace at Naniwa.
summary.zh: 645年苏我氏被推翻后，中大兄皇子与中臣镰足在孝德天皇治下仿效唐朝推行改革，宣布土地与人民归于天皇，并以难波新宫为中心筹划中央集权的官僚与税制。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Taika Reform

events.note: The wording of the 646 reform edict in the Nihon Shoki was probably revised later; the real pace of reform is debated.

name.en: Goguryeo–Tang War and fall of Pyongyang
name.zh: 唐与高句丽战争及平壤陷落

summary.en: After repeated Tang invasions from 645, an allied Tang–Silla army besieged Pyongyang in 668 and captured King Bojang, ending Goguryeo after some seven centuries. Tang set up the Protectorate General to Pacify the East in its former capital.
summary.zh: 唐朝自645年起多次进攻高句丽，668年唐与新罗联军围攻平壤，俘获宝藏王，高句丽灭亡。唐朝随后在平壤设立安东都护府。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Goguryeo–Tang War

name.en: Battle of Hwangsanbeol and fall of Baekje
name.zh: 黄山伐之战与百济灭亡

summary.en: Baekje general Gyebaek made a last stand against the Silla army of Kim Yu-sin at Hwangsanbeol while a Tang fleet landed in the west. The Baekje capital Sabi fell soon after and King Uija surrendered.
summary.zh: 百济将领阶伯在黄山伐迎战金庾信率领的新罗军，最终战死，同时唐朝水军在西海岸登陆。不久百济都城泗沘陷落，义慈王投降。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Battle of Hwangsanbeol

events.note: Battlefield location near Nonsan is approximate (Wikidata gives none).

summary.en: A Yamato fleet sent to restore Baekje was destroyed by Tang and Silla naval forces at the mouth of the Baekgang (Geum River). The defeat ended Baekje restoration hopes and led Japan to fortify its western coasts.
summary.zh: 倭国派遣水军援助百济复国，在白江口（今锦江入海口）被唐朝与新罗联军击败。此役终结了百济复国的希望，也促使日本在西部沿海修筑防御工事。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
Jiu Tangshu (Old Book of Tang, 945), "Biography of Liu Rengui" and "Account of Baekje"
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Battle of Baekgang

summary.en: Having helped Tang destroy Baekje and Goguryeo, Silla turned on its ally when Tang tried to rule the peninsula directly. Victories at Maeso fortress (675) and Gibeolpo (676) forced Tang to withdraw, leaving Silla master of the peninsula south of the Taedong River.
summary.zh: 新罗协助唐朝灭百济与高句丽后，因唐欲直接统治半岛而与之反目。675年买肖城之战与676年伎伐浦海战获胜后，唐军撤退，新罗控制了大同江以南的半岛。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Silla–Tang War

summary.en: Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, was killed at Karbala with members of his family and companions by an army sent by the Umayyad governor of Kufa. His martyrdom on 10 Muharram (Ashura) is central to Shia Islam and commemorated every year.
summary.zh: 先知穆罕默德的外孙侯赛因·本·阿里及其家人、追随者在卡尔巴拉被倭马亚王朝库法总督派出的军队杀害。他于穆哈兰月十日（阿舒拉日）的殉难是什叶派信仰的核心，每年都被隆重纪念。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: al-Husayn ibn Ali
al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XIX (trans. Howard)
Wikipedia: Battle of Karbala

name.en: Kedukan Bukit inscription: rise of Srivijaya
name.zh: 格杜干武吉碑：室利佛逝兴起

summary.en: This Old Malay inscription found at Palembang records a sacred expedition by Dapunta Hyang with an army of thousands in 683, commonly read as the founding of the Srivijaya polity that soon dominated the Strait of Malacca.
summary.zh: 在巨港发现的这块古马来语碑铭，记载了683年达本达·希扬率数万大军进行的神圣远征，通常被解读为室利佛逝政权的建立；此后不久它便称霸马六甲海峡。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce: A Study of the Origins of Śrīvijaya (Cornell University Press, 1967)
Wikipedia: Kedukan Bukit inscription

events.note: Interpretation of the expedition as a "founding" is debated; the inscription is dated Śaka 605 (683 CE).

name.en: Wu Zetian proclaims the Zhou dynasty

summary.en: Having ruled through her sons for years, Empress Wu took the throne herself as emperor of a new Zhou dynasty, with Luoyang as the "Divine Capital" – the only woman to reign as emperor in Chinese history.
summary.zh: 武则天在临朝称制多年后自立为帝，改国号为周，以洛阳为神都，成为中国历史上唯一的女皇帝。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷6 则天皇后本纪 天授元年
资治通鉴 卷204 唐纪二十 天授元年

summary.en: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik completed the Dome of the Rock on the Haram al-Sharif (Temple Mount) in Jerusalem. It is the oldest surviving major Islamic monument; its mosaic inscription is dated 72 AH (691–692).
summary.zh: 倭马亚哈里发阿卜杜勒-马利克在耶路撒冷的尊贵禁地（圣殿山）建成圆顶清真寺。它是现存最古老的大型伊斯兰建筑，其马赛克铭文纪年为希吉拉历72年（691—692年）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dome of the Rock
O. Grabar, The Dome of the Rock (2006)
Wikipedia: Dome of the Rock

name.zh: 大马士革倭马亚清真寺建成

summary.en: Caliph al-Walid I built the Great Mosque of Damascus on the site of a Roman temple and the church of St John the Baptist. Its mosaics and layout became a model for later congregational mosques.
summary.zh: 哈里发瓦利德一世在罗马神庙和施洗者约翰教堂的旧址上修建大马士革大清真寺。其马赛克装饰和布局成为后世聚礼清真寺的典范。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Great Mosque of Damascus
F. B. Flood, The Great Mosque of Damascus (2001)
Wikipedia: Umayyad Mosque

summary.en: Empress Genmei moved the court to Heijō-kyō (Nara), a grid-planned capital modelled on Tang Chang'an. It gave its name to the Nara period and, apart from 740–745, remained the capital until 784.
summary.zh: 元明天皇将都城迁至仿照唐长安城棋盘式规划的平城京（今奈良）。奈良时代因此得名，除740至745年外，此地一直为都城，直至784年。

sources.title: Shoku Nihongi (797)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Heijō-kyō

name.zh: 倭马亚王朝征服伊比利亚

summary.en: Berber and Arab forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa, defeated King Roderic at the Guadalete in 711 and within a few years overran most of the Visigothic kingdom. The conquest created al-Andalus, Muslim-ruled Iberia, which survived in part until 1492.
summary.zh: 塔里克·伊本·齐亚德率领柏柏尔人和阿拉伯人从北非渡海，711年在瓜达莱特河击败国王罗德里克，数年内攻占西哥特王国大部。这次征服建立了安达卢斯，穆斯林在伊比利亚的统治部分延续至1492年。

sources.title: Chronicle of 754 (Mozarabic Chronicle)
Roger Collins, The Arab Conquest of Spain, 710–797 (1989)
Britannica: al-Andalus

events.note: Coordinates and date are those of the opening Battle of Guadalete (Wikidata Q504172); the span 711–726 follows Wikidata.

wiki.en: Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula

summary.en: The Arab commander Muhammad ibn al-Qasim took the port of Debal, defeated King Dahir and occupied Sindh and Multan, bringing the lower Indus valley into the caliphate.
summary.zh: 阿拉伯将领穆罕默德·本·卡西姆攻克德巴尔港，击败达希尔王，占领信德和木尔坦，将印度河下游纳入哈里发国。

sources.title: Chach Nama (13th-century Persian history of the conquest)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim
Wikidata Q112182472

summary.en: Ō no Yasumaro presented the Kojiki, Japan's oldest surviving chronicle, to Empress Genmei. It narrates the creation myths and the genealogy of the imperial line up to Empress Suiko.
summary.zh: 太安万侣向元明天皇献上《古事记》，这是现存最古老的日本史书，记述了创世神话及至推古天皇为止的皇室谱系。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kojiki compiled
Donald L. Philippi (trans.), Kojiki (University of Tokyo Press, 1968)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Kojiki

image.artist: Ken'yu (賢瑜), Koten Hozonkai (古典保存会)

summary.en: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeated an Umayyad army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, governor of al-Andalus, between Poitiers and Tours. The victory checked Muslim raids north of the Pyrenees and strengthened the Carolingian family's power.
summary.zh: 查理·马特率领的法兰克军队在普瓦捷与图尔之间击败安达卢斯总督阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·加菲基率领的倭马亚军队。此役遏制了穆斯林越过比利牛斯山向北的袭扰，并巩固了加洛林家族的权势。

sources.title: Continuations of the Chronicle of Fredegar
Chronicle of 754 (Mozarabic Chronicle)
Britannica: Battle of Tours

events.note: Traditionally 10 October 732 (Wikidata); a minority argue for 733. The site between Tours and Poitiers is uncertain; coordinates follow Wikidata (Moussais-la-Bataille).

summary.en: A movement launched in Khorasan by Abu Muslim in the name of the Prophet's family overthrew the Umayyads. After victory on the Great Zab in 750 the Abbasids took power, shifting the caliphate's centre from Syria to Iraq.
summary.zh: 阿布·穆斯林以先知家族之名在呼罗珊发动起义，推翻倭马亚王朝。750年大扎卜河之战获胜后阿拔斯家族掌权，哈里发国的中心由叙利亚移至伊拉克。

label.zh: 迈尔万二世在埃及被杀

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Abbasid caliphate
al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings, vol. XXVII (trans. Williams)
Wikipedia: Abbasid revolution

events.note: Open revolt began 9 June 747 (25 Ramadan 129 AH); Wikidata gives 746.

summary.en: According to the Samguk yusa, the Silla minister Kim Dae-seong began the artificial granite grotto of Seokguram on Mount Toham in 751, together with Bulguksa temple below. Its seated Buddha is a masterpiece of East Asian Buddhist sculpture.
summary.zh: 据《三国遗事》记载，新罗宰相金大城于751年在吐含山开始营建人工花岗岩石窟石窟庵，并同时修建山下的佛国寺。窟内本尊坐佛是东亚佛教雕塑的杰作。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seokguram grotto built
Iryeon, Samguk yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, c. 1281)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple
Wikipedia: Seokguram

events.note: The 751 start and 774 completion follow the Samguk yusa.

summary.en: Emperor Shōmu's colossal bronze Vairocana Buddha at Tōdai-ji, the head temple of the provincial temple network, was ceremonially "eye-opened" in 752 before monks from across Asia.
summary.zh: 圣武天皇下令铸造的东大寺卢舍那大佛于752年举行开眼供养法会，来自亚洲各地的僧侣参加。东大寺是全国国分寺体系的总寺。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji consecrated
Shoku Nihongi (797)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
Wikipedia: Tōdai-ji

summary.en: Frontier general An Lushan rose at Fanyang, took both Tang capitals and proclaimed a Yan dynasty. Emperor Xuanzong fled to Sichuan; Tang, with Uyghur help, needed eight years to suppress the rebels, and never regained its former strength.
summary.zh: 节度使安禄山、史思明自范阳起兵，攻陷两京，僭号大燕；玄宗奔蜀。唐借回纥兵历八年始平定，盛唐由此转衰。

label.en: End of the rebellion at Mozhou

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
资治通鉴 卷217 唐纪三十三 天宝十四载
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷200上 安禄山传

summary.en: Caliph al-Mansur founded his round capital, Madinat al-Salam ("City of Peace"), on the west bank of the Tigris. Baghdad grew into the largest city of the Islamic world and a centre of trade, learning and government for five centuries.
summary.zh: 哈里发曼苏尔在底格里斯河西岸兴建圆形新都“和平之城”。巴格达发展为伊斯兰世界最大的城市，五百年间一直是商业、学术和政治中心。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Baghdad
al-Ya'qubi, Kitab al-Buldan
Wikipedia: Round City of Baghdad

summary.en: Chancellor Yang Yan replaced the per-capita grain, labour and cloth levies with taxes on land and property collected in summer and autumn, a basic shift in Chinese fiscal practice.
summary.zh: 宰相杨炎废租庸调，改按户等资产与田亩于夏秋两季征税，是中国赋税制度的重大转变。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷118 杨炎传
资治通鉴 卷226 唐纪四十二 建中元年

summary.en: From the raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793 until the mid-11th century, Scandinavian seafarers raided, traded and settled from Ireland to the Volga. They founded the Kingdom of Jórvík, Normandy and the settlement of Iceland, and helped shape the early Rus' state.
summary.zh: 自793年袭击林迪斯法恩修道院起至11世纪中叶，斯堪的纳维亚航海者从爱尔兰到伏尔加河一带劫掠、贸易与定居。他们建立了约克维京王国和诺曼底，定居冰岛，并参与塑造了早期罗斯国家。

label.zh: 罗斯人袭击君士坦丁堡
留里克入主诺夫哥罗德（传说）

label.en: Harald Hardrada falls at Stamford Bridge
label.zh: 哈拉尔德·哈德拉达战死斯坦福桥

summary.en: Emperor Kanmu moved the court from Nagaoka to the new grid-planned capital of Heian-kyō, modern Kyoto. It remained the imperial capital until 1869 and gave its name to the Heian period.
summary.zh: 桓武天皇将朝廷从长冈京迁至新建的棋盘式都城平安京，即今京都。此后直到1869年这里一直是天皇所在的都城，平安时代亦由此得名。

summary.en: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day. The act revived a western imperial title, deepened the alliance between the papacy and the Franks, and strained relations with Byzantium.
summary.zh: 圣诞节当天，教宗利奥三世在圣伯多禄大殿为法兰克国王查理曼加冕为“罗马人的皇帝”。此举复兴了西方的帝号，加深了教廷与法兰克人的同盟，也使与拜占庭的关系趋于紧张。

summary.en: The Shailendra dynasty of central Java raised Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist monument: a stepped mandala of nine platforms with over 2,600 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues, built around 780–830.
summary.zh: 中爪哇的夏连特拉王朝建造了世界上最大的佛教建筑婆罗浮屠：一座九层阶梯式曼荼罗，拥有两千六百多块浮雕和五百零四尊佛像，约建于780至830年间。

summary.en: Tang and Tibet swore a peace treaty at Chang'an (821) and again at Rasa (822); the bilingual text was carved on a pillar erected before the Jokhang in 823, where it still stands.
summary.zh: 唐蕃先盟于长安（821），再盟于逻些（822），823年将汉藏双语盟文刻碑立于大昭寺前，至今尚存。

summary.en: The Abbasid palace library known as the Bayt al-Hikma became associated with translating Greek, Persian and Indian works into Arabic. Under al-Ma'mun, scholars such as al-Khwarizmi worked in Baghdad, part of a translation movement that underpinned medieval science.
summary.zh: 阿拔斯宫廷图书馆“智慧宫”与把希腊、波斯和印度典籍译成阿拉伯文的事业密切相关。马蒙在位时，花剌子密等学者在巴格达从事研究，这场翻译运动奠定了中世纪科学的基础。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Bayt al-Hikmah

summary.en: The three surviving sons of Louis the Pious divided the Carolingian Empire: Charles the Bald took West Francia, Louis the German East Francia, and Lothair I a middle kingdom with the imperial title. The partition foreshadowed the later division between France and Germany.
summary.zh: 虔诚者路易的三个儿子瓜分加洛林帝国：秃头查理得西法兰克，日耳曼人路易得东法兰克，洛泰尔一世得中法兰克并保有皇帝称号。这次分割预示了日后法兰西与德意志的分野。

sources.title: Annals of Saint-Bertin, entry for 843
Nithard, Histories
Britannica: Treaty of Verdun

summary.en: Emperor Wuzong ordered the closure of more than 4,600 Buddhist monasteries and the return of over 260,000 monks and nuns to lay life, seizing temple lands and bronze; Manichaeism and Nestorian Christianity were also suppressed.
summary.zh: 唐武宗下诏拆毁佛寺四千六百余所，勒令僧尼二十六万余人还俗，没收寺田铜像；摩尼教、景教亦遭禁。

name.en: Zhang Yichao founds the Guiyi Army

summary.en: Zhang Yichao led the people of Shazhou (Dunhuang) in expelling the Tibetan garrison and restored Gua, Sha and other Hexi prefectures to Tang allegiance; the court named his regime the Guiyi ("Return to Allegiance") Army.
summary.zh: 张议潮率沙州军民驱逐吐蕃守将，收复瓜、沙等河西诸州归唐，唐廷置归义军，以其为节度使。

summary.en: The Shivagrha inscription of 856 records the completion of a great Shiva temple, identified with Prambanan, by the Sanjaya-line ruler of Mataram. Its soaring towers to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma are Java's largest Hindu monument.
summary.zh: 856年的湿婆屋碑铭记载了马打兰古国桑贾亚系君主建成一座宏伟的湿婆神庙，即普兰巴南。其供奉湿婆、毗湿奴与梵天的高塔是爪哇最大的印度教建筑群。

summary.en: Salt smugglers Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao led a peasant war that swept from Shandong to Guangzhou and back; Huang Chao captured Chang'an in 881 and proclaimed Qi. The rebellion left Tang power in the hands of regional warlords.
summary.zh: 王仙芝、黄巢以私盐贩起事，转战南北远至广州；881年黄巢入长安称帝建齐。唐室自此名存实亡，藩镇坐大。

name.en: Later Three Kingdoms and Goryeo reunification
name.zh: 后三国时代与高丽统一

summary.en: As Silla weakened, rebel states Later Baekje and Taebong (Later Goguryeo) arose. Wang Geon, who founded Goryeo in 918, accepted Silla's surrender in 935 and defeated Later Baekje at Illicheon in 936, reuniting the peninsula.
summary.zh: 新罗衰落后，后百济与泰封（后高句丽）相继崛起。918年建立高丽的王建于935年接受新罗归降，936年在一利川击败后百济，重新统一朝鲜半岛。

summary.en: To win Khitan support against Later Tang, Shi Jingtang ceded sixteen prefectures around Youzhou (Beijing) and Yunzhou (Datong) to the Liao, giving the steppe empire a foothold south of the Great Wall for four centuries.
summary.zh: 石敬瑭为借契丹兵灭后唐，割幽、云等十六州予辽，自此中原失去长城屏障达四百余年。

summary.en: Ngô Quyền planted iron-tipped stakes in the bed of the Bạch Đằng River and lured a Southern Han fleet over them at high tide; as the tide fell the ships were impaled and destroyed. The victory ended a millennium of Chinese rule in northern Vietnam.
summary.zh: 吴权在白藤江河床中埋下包铁木桩，趁涨潮引诱南汉舰队驶入，退潮时敌船触桩搁浅而被歼灭。此役结束了中国对越南北部近千年的统治。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)

name.en: Chenqiao Mutiny and founding of Song

summary.en: At Chenqiao post station north of Kaifeng, troops of the Later Zhou palace army draped a yellow robe on their commander Zhao Kuangyin; he returned to the capital, accepted the child emperor's abdication and founded the Song.
summary.zh: 后周殿前都点检赵匡胤于陈桥驿被部下黄袍加身，回师开封受禅，建立宋朝。

summary.en: Grand Prince Vladimir I of Kyiv accepted Byzantine Christianity, was baptised and had the people of Kyiv baptised in the Dnieper. The conversion tied the Rus' to the church and culture of Constantinople, shaping the later Orthodox identity of Ukraine, Belarus and Russia.
summary.zh: 基辅大公弗拉基米尔一世接受拜占庭基督教并受洗，随后令基辅民众在第聂伯河中受洗。这次皈依使罗斯与君士坦丁堡的教会和文化紧密相连，塑造了日后乌克兰、白俄罗斯和俄罗斯的东正教认同。

sources.title: Russian Primary Chronicle, entries for 987–988
Britannica: Saint Vladimir I

events.note: 988 is the Primary Chronicle's date; Vladimir's own baptism may have taken place at Chersonesos in Crimea, and some historians date it 987–989.

summary.en: After a Liao invasion reached Chanzhou on the Yellow River, Emperor Zhenzong, urged on by Kou Zhun, agreed peace: Song paid annual silk and silver, and the two empires kept the peace for over a century.
summary.zh: 辽萧太后与圣宗南下至澶州，寇准力劝宋真宗亲征，双方议和：宋岁输辽银绢，宋辽此后百余年无大战。

summary.en: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady-in-waiting at the Heian court, wrote this long prose narrative of the life and loves of the "Shining Prince" Genji. It was circulating by 1008 and is often called the world's first novel.
summary.zh: 平安宫廷女官紫式部创作了这部描写“光源氏”一生与情爱的长篇物语。至1008年该书已在宫中流传，常被誉为世界上第一部长篇小说。

summary.en: Rajaraja I dedicated this granite Shiva temple at Thanjavur, whose 66-metre vimana was among the tallest buildings of its age; its inscriptions record the Chola state’s revenues, staff and endowments.
summary.zh: 罗阇罗阇一世在坦贾武尔建成这座花岗岩湿婆神庙，其66米高的主塔在当时世界上数一数二；庙中铭文记录了朱罗王朝的税收、人员与捐赠。

name.en: Lý Thái Tổ moves the capital to Thăng Long

summary.en: In his Edict on the Transfer of the Capital, Lý Thái Tổ moved the court from Hoa Lư to the site of the old Tang citadel of Đại La, renaming it Thăng Long ("Ascending Dragon"), the future Hanoi.
summary.zh: 李太祖颁布《迁都诏》，将朝廷从华闾迁至唐代大罗城旧址，并改名升龙（意为“腾飞之龙”），即后来的河内。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)

summary.en: In Tus, Ferdowsi completed the Shahnameh ("Book of Kings"), an epic of some 50,000 couplets recounting Iran's myths and history down to the Arab conquest. Written in Persian with few Arabic loanwords, it became Iran's national epic.
summary.zh: 菲尔多西在图斯完成《列王纪》，以约五万联诗句讲述伊朗从神话时代到阿拉伯征服的历史。全诗以少用阿拉伯借词的波斯语写成，成为伊朗的民族史诗。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Shah-nameh
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Ferdowsi
Wikipedia: Shahnameh

events.note: Wikidata dates the work c. 1000; the final version is dated 1010 in the poem itself.

summary.en: The Song state took over the privately issued jiaozi notes of Sichuan merchants and set up an official Jiaozi bureau at Yizhou (Chengdu), creating the world's first government paper currency.
summary.zh: 北宋于益州（成都）设交子务，将四川商人私发的交子收归官办，成为世界上最早的官方纸币。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

name.zh: 朱罗王朝远征室利佛逝

summary.en: Rajendra Chola I’s fleet raided the Srivijaya maritime realm, sacking ports in Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula including Kadaram (Kedah) and capturing its king; the Tanjore inscription of 1030–31 lists the places taken.
summary.zh: 拉金德拉一世的舰队袭击海上强国室利佛逝，洗劫苏门答腊和马来半岛诸港，包括羯荼（吉打），并俘获其国王；1030—1031年的坦贾武尔铭文列出了所攻占之地。

summary.en: Avicenna (Ibn Sina) completed al-Qanun fi al-Tibb, a five-book synthesis of Greek and Islamic medicine written in Hamadan and Isfahan. Translated into Latin in the 12th century, it remained a standard medical textbook in Europe and the Islamic world for centuries.
summary.zh: 伊本·西那在哈马丹和伊斯法罕写成五卷本《医典》，集希腊与伊斯兰医学之大成。12世纪译为拉丁文后，数百年间一直是欧洲和伊斯兰世界的标准医学教科书。

summary.en: Climaxing some seventeen raids into India, Mahmud crossed the Thar desert, took the Somnath temple on the Gujarat coast and carried off its treasure; the episode became a contested symbol in later memory.
summary.zh: 马哈茂德前后约十七次入侵印度，此役穿越塔尔沙漠，攻陷古吉拉特海岸的索姆纳特神庙并掠走其财宝；此事在后世记忆中成为争议性的象征。

sources.title: Romila Thapar, Somanatha: The Many Voices of a History (2004)

summary.en: The Tangut leader Li Yuanhao declared himself emperor of Great Xia at Xingqing (Yinchuan), introduced a Tangut script, and fought Song to a standstill before the Qingli peace of 1044.
summary.zh: 党项首领李元昊于兴庆府称帝，国号大夏，创制西夏文；与宋连年交战，1044年订庆历和议。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Papal legates led by Cardinal Humbert laid a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar of Hagia Sophia, and the patriarch replied in kind. The mutual excommunications came to symbolise the lasting split between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
summary.zh: 以枢机主教洪贝尔为首的教宗使节将绝罚君士坦丁堡宗主教米海尔·色路拉里乌斯的诏书置于圣索菲亚大教堂祭坛上，宗主教随即予以反绝罚。这次相互绝罚成为罗马天主教与东正教长期分裂的象征。

sources.title: Britannica: Schism of 1054
Henry Chadwick, East and West: The Making of a Rift in the Church (2003)

events.note: The rupture was a long process; 1054 is its conventional symbolic date.

summary.en: Duke William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold II near Hastings, opening the Norman conquest of England. William was crowned at Westminster on Christmas Day 1066, and a new French-speaking aristocracy transformed English government, language and architecture.
summary.zh: 诺曼底公爵威廉在黑斯廷斯附近击败并杀死英格兰国王哈罗德二世，开启诺曼征服。威廉于1066年圣诞节在威斯敏斯特加冕，说法语的新贵族阶层由此深刻改变了英格兰的政治、语言和建筑。

sources.title: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (MSS D and E), entry for 1066
William of Poitiers, Gesta Guillelmi

summary.en: Emperor Shenzong backed Wang Anshi's reforms – state loans to farmers, hired labour service, militia and trade measures – to enrich the state. Opponents led by Sima Guang reversed them in 1085–86, opening decades of factional strife.
summary.zh: 宋神宗任用王安石推行青苗、免役、保甲、市易等新法以富国强兵；1085年后司马光等尽废新法，新旧党争延续数十年。

summary.en: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan routed the Byzantine army near Manzikert, north of Lake Van, and captured Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes. The Byzantine civil strife that followed let Turkish groups settle across Anatolia, beginning its gradual Turkification.
summary.zh: 塞尔柱苏丹阿尔普·阿尔斯兰在凡湖以北的曼齐刻尔特附近大败拜占庭军队，俘虏皇帝罗曼努斯四世。此后拜占庭陷入内乱，突厥部众得以遍布安纳托利亚，开启了该地区逐步突厥化的进程。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Manzikert

summary.en: After nineteen years of work, Sima Guang presented the 294-chapter Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, a chronicle from 403 BCE to 959 CE, to Emperor Shenzong.
summary.zh: 司马光历时十九年编成294卷编年体通史《资治通鉴》，起战国三家分晋（前403）迄五代（959），进呈宋神宗。

name.en: Founding of the University of Bologna

summary.en: Bologna's law school, traditionally dated to 1088, grew from teachers of Roman law into a university organised by student associations. Often regarded as the oldest university in continuous operation, it became a model for others across Europe.
summary.zh: 博洛尼亚的法学院按传统说法创立于1088年，由讲授罗马法的教师群体发展为由学生团体组织的大学。它通常被视为持续办学至今最古老的大学，并成为欧洲各地大学的典范。

summary.en: Answering Pope Urban II's call at Clermont in 1095, armies of western knights marched through Constantinople and Anatolia, took Antioch in 1098 and captured Jerusalem in July 1099. The crusade founded Latin states in the Levant.

summary.zh: 响应教皇乌尔班二世的号召，西欧军队穿越安纳托利亚和叙利亚，先后攻占尼西亚、安条克，最终夺取耶路撒冷，建立了埃德萨、安条克、耶路撒冷以及稍后的的黎波里等十字军国家。

summary.en: Crusader forces stormed Jerusalem, then held by the Fatimids, on 15 July 1099 after a five-week siege. The capture was followed by a massacre of many Muslim and Jewish inhabitants, and Godfrey of Bouillon became the first ruler of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
summary.zh: 经五周围攻，十字军于1099年7月15日攻破法蒂玛王朝控制下的耶路撒冷，随后屠杀了大批穆斯林和犹太居民。布永的戈弗雷成为耶路撒冷王国的首位统治者。

summary.en: King Suryavarman II built Angkor Wat as a temple to Vishnu and probably his own funerary monument. Its five lotus towers, moat and kilometre-long bas-reliefs make it the largest religious monument in the world.
summary.zh: 苏利耶跋摩二世修建吴哥窟，供奉毗湿奴，很可能也是其陵庙。五座莲花状宝塔、护城河与绵延近一公里的浮雕回廊，使其成为世界上最大的宗教建筑。

summary.en: King David IV "the Builder" of Georgia defeated a large Seljuk-led Muslim coalition at Didgori, west of Tbilisi. The victory allowed him to take Tbilisi in 1122 and opened Georgia's golden age.
summary.zh: 格鲁吉亚“建设者”大卫四世在第比利斯以西的迪德戈里击败塞尔柱人领导的穆斯林联军。此役使他于1122年收复第比利斯，开启了格鲁吉亚的黄金时代。

summary.en: Jin armies invaded Song in 1125, besieged Kaifeng twice and took it in early 1127, carrying off the emperors Huizong and Qinzong and thousands of courtiers. Prince Zhao Gou re-established the dynasty at Yingtian as the Southern Song.
summary.zh: 金军1125年分两路南下，两围东京，1127年初攻破开封，掳徽、钦二帝及宗室北去，北宋亡；康王赵构于应天府即位，建立南宋。

summary.zh: 金海陵王完颜亮南侵欲渡长江，文臣虞允文于采石收拾散兵，以车船与霹雳炮击败金军渡江；不久海陵王为部下所杀。

summary.zh: 平氏与源氏两大武士集团之间的内战。1185年平氏水军在坛之浦覆灭，源赖朝由此成为日本最有权势的人物。

summary.en: Saladin trapped and destroyed the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem near the Horns of Hattin above Lake Tiberias, capturing King Guy of Lusignan. Jerusalem surrendered to him on 2 October, prompting the Third Crusade.
summary.zh: 萨拉丁在太巴列湖上方的哈丁角附近围歼耶路撒冷王国军队，俘虏国王居伊。同年10月2日耶路撒冷向他投降，引发了第三次十字军东征。

summary.zh: 阇耶跋摩七世在新建的吴哥城中心修建佛教寺庙巴戎寺，以刻有巨大安详面孔的佛塔群和描绘日常生活及与占婆战争的浮雕而闻名。

summary.en: A Rajput coalition under Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad of Ghor near Taraori in Haryana, wounding the Ghurid ruler and checking his advance into the Ganges plain.
summary.zh: 普里特维拉杰·乔汉率领的拉其普特联军在哈里亚纳的塔拉奥里附近击败古尔王朝的穆罕默德，使其负伤，暂时阻止了他向恒河平原的推进。

summary.en: Minamoto no Yoritomo, already ruling the warrior class from Kamakura, was appointed sei-i taishōgun in 1192. His government created a dual system in which the shogunate controlled military affairs alongside the imperial court in Kyoto.
summary.zh: 已在镰仓统领武士阶层的源赖朝于1192年被任命为征夷大将军。幕府掌握军事与地方治安，与京都朝廷并存，形成公武二元体制。

summary.zh: 古尔的穆罕默德率骑射手卷土重来，在同一战场击溃普里特维拉杰·乔汉，后者被俘遇害，北印度从此向古尔王朝及其后的德里苏丹国敞开。

summary.zh: 古尔王朝征服后，库特布丁·艾巴克在德里第一座聚礼清真寺旁兴建这座带棱纹的砂岩胜利塔，伊勒图特米什续建上层；塔高约73米，是印度最高的中世纪宣礼塔。

summary.en: Facing baronial rebellion, King John of England agreed at Runnymede to a charter limiting royal power and guaranteeing certain legal rights. Though annulled within months, its reissued versions became a foundation of English law and a symbol of constitutional government.

summary.en: From 1231 the Mongols invaded Goryeo repeatedly. The military regime moved the court to Ganghwa Island and resisted for decades while the mainland was ravaged, until Goryeo accepted vassal status in 1259.
summary.zh: 自1231年起蒙古多次入侵高丽。武臣政权将朝廷迁往江华岛，坚持抵抗数十年，本土则惨遭蹂躏，直至1259年高丽接受藩属地位。

summary.en: Sent west by his brother, the Great Khan Möngke, Hulagu destroyed the Nizari Ismaili strongholds of Iran, sacked Baghdad and ended the Abbasid caliphate, then invaded Syria. The campaign founded the Ilkhanate and was checked only at Ain Jalut.
summary.zh: 旭烈兀奉其兄蒙哥大汗之命西征，摧毁伊朗的尼扎里伊斯玛仪派堡垒，攻陷巴格达、终结阿拔斯哈里发政权，随后入侵叙利亚。此次西征建立了伊利汗国，直到阿音札鲁特才被遏止。

summary.zh: 蒙古—元朝先后三次（1258年、1285年、1287—1288年）入侵，虽曾攻占升龙，但都被陈朝击退。陈兴道采取坚壁清野与游击战术，最终在白藤江决战中获胜。

summary.en: After a short siege, Hulagu's Mongol army took Baghdad, sacked the city and executed the last Abbasid caliph, al-Musta'sim. The fall of the caliphal capital, with great loss of life and of libraries, was long remembered as one of the great catastrophes of Islamic history.
summary.zh: 经短暂围攻，旭烈兀的蒙古军攻陷巴格达，洗劫全城并处死末代阿拔斯哈里发穆斯台绥木。哈里发首都的陷落造成大量人员死亡和典籍损毁，长期被视为伊斯兰历史上的重大浩劫之一。

summary.zh: 在巴勒斯坦的耶斯列谷，忽都思和拜巴尔斯率领的埃及马穆鲁克军击败了旭烈兀留在叙利亚的蒙古军。这是蒙古西进遭遇的第一次重大挫败，确立了马穆鲁克王朝对叙利亚的统治。

summary.en: Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty, with Goryeo ships and troops, twice invaded northern Kyushu. Both attacks at Hakata Bay were contained by samurai defenders and walls, and storms—later called kamikaze—wrecked much of the 1281 fleet.

summary.en: Kublai Khan sent a fleet to punish King Kertanegara of Singhasari for mutilating his envoy. Raden Wijaya allied with the Yuan to defeat the usurper Jayakatwang, then turned on and expelled them, founding Majapahit.
summary.zh: 忽必烈派遣舰队惩罚曾黥面元使的新柯沙里国王格尔达纳卡拉。罗登·威查耶先与元军联手击败篡位者查耶卡旺，随后反戈驱逐元军，建立了满者伯夷。

sources.title: Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Pararaton (Book of Kings, 15th–16th c.)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasion of Java

summary.en: Alauddin Khalji’s army met a large Chagatai Mongol force under Qutlugh Khwaja at Kili near Delhi; the Mongols withdrew after heavy fighting, one of several invasions the sultanate repelled around 1300.
summary.zh: 阿拉乌丁·卡尔吉的军队在德里附近的基利迎战忽都鲁·火者率领的察合台蒙古大军，激战后蒙古人撤退；这是约1300年前后德里苏丹国击退的多次蒙古入侵之一。

sources.title: Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Ziauddin Barani, Tarikh-i Firuz Shahi
Wikidata Q19840229

summary.en: Dante Alighieri completed the Commedia, an allegorical poem in three parts—Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso—written in the Tuscan vernacular during his exile. It became a founding work of Italian literature and of the literary Italian language.
summary.zh: 但丁在流亡期间完成了以托斯卡纳方言写成的寓言长诗《神曲》，分为《地狱篇》《炼狱篇》《天堂篇》三部。该作品成为意大利文学和意大利文学语言的奠基之作。

sources.title: Giovanni Boccaccio, Trattatello in laude di Dante
Britannica: The Divine Comedy

events.note: Composed c. 1308–1321; Wikidata gives c. 1320. Paradiso was finished at Ravenna shortly before Dante's death in September 1321.

image.artist: Domenico di Michelino / After Alesso Baldovinetti

summary.en: A series of wars between the Plantagenet kings of England and the Valois kings of France over the French crown and English lands in France. English victories such as Crécy and Agincourt were reversed after Joan of Arc helped relieve Orléans in 1429; by 1453 England held only Calais.
summary.zh: 英格兰金雀花王朝与法兰西瓦卢瓦王朝围绕法国王位及英格兰在法领地展开的一系列战争。英军虽有克雷西、阿金库尔等大捷，但1429年贞德助解奥尔良之围后局势逆转；至1453年英格兰仅保有加来。

sources.title: Jean Froissart, Chronicles
Jonathan Sumption, The Hundred Years War (5 vols., 1990–2023)
Britannica: Hundred Years' War

events.note: Placed at Orléans, the war's turning point (1429).

summary.en: Plague carried on Genoese ships from the Black Sea reached Sicily in October 1347 and swept across Europe within four years, killing perhaps a third to a half of the population. The catastrophe reshaped labour, religion and society across the continent.
summary.zh: 随热那亚船只从黑海传来的鼠疫于1347年10月抵达西西里，四年内席卷欧洲，可能造成三分之一至一半人口死亡。这场浩劫深刻改变了整个欧洲的劳动力、宗教与社会。

sources.title: Giovanni Boccaccio, Decameron, Introduction to the First Day
Ole J. Benedictow, The Black Death 1346–1353: The Complete History (2004)
Britannica: Black Death

events.note: Wikidata dates the pandemic 1346–1352, starting in the Golden Horde; 1347 marks its arrival in Europe (Messina), and it reached Moscow in 1353, so endYear follows Benedictow.

summary.en: Conscripted labourers repairing the Yellow River rose under the White Lotus leaders Han Shantong and Liu Futong at Yingzhou. The red-turbaned armies spread across the Yuan realm; one of their commanders, Zhu Yuanzhang, founded the Ming.
summary.zh: 元末征发民夫治黄河，韩山童、刘福通以白莲教在颍州起事，红巾军遍及各地，其部将朱元璋终建明朝。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
宋濂等《元史》卷42 顺帝本纪五 至正十一年
张廷玉等《明史》卷122 韩林儿传

summary.en: In one of history's largest naval battles, Zhu Yuanzhang's smaller fleet used fire ships to defeat the giant tower ships of his rival Chen Youliang, who was killed; the victory made Zhu master of the Yangtze.
summary.zh: 朱元璋以较小船队用火攻大破陈友谅巨舰于鄱阳湖，陈友谅中箭身亡，朱元璋自此称雄长江中下游。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷1 太祖本纪一

events.note: The Wikidata item dates it 30 Aug–4 Oct 1363.

summary.en: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaimed the Ming dynasty at Yingtian (Nanjing); that summer his generals Xu Da and Chang Yuchun took Dadu, and the last Yuan emperor fled to the steppe.
summary.zh: 朱元璋于应天府称帝建明，同年徐达、常遇春北伐攻克大都，元顺帝北走。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷2 太祖本纪二 洪武元年

summary.en: Monks at Heungdeok temple in Cheongju printed this anthology of Seon (Zen) teachings with movable metal type. The surviving volume, held in the Bibliothèque nationale de France, is the oldest extant book printed this way.
summary.zh: 清州兴德寺僧人用金属活字印行这部禅宗语录选集。现存的一卷藏于法国国家图书馆，是世界上现存最早的金属活字印本。

summary.en: General Yi Seong-gye, who had turned his army back at Wihwa Island in 1388 and taken power, deposed the last Goryeo king and was enthroned as King Taejo in Gaegyeong. He renamed the state Joseon and moved the capital to Hanseong (Seoul) in 1394.
summary.zh: 1388年威化岛回军后掌握大权的将军李成桂，于1392年废黜高丽末代国王，在开京即位为太祖。他改国号为朝鲜，并于1394年迁都汉城（今首尔）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Founding of Joseon
Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Joseon

summary.en: Timur crossed the Indus, defeated Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Tughluq outside Delhi and let his army plunder the city for days, leaving the sultanate shattered before he returned to Samarkand with captives and craftsmen.
summary.zh: 帖木儿渡过印度河，在德里城外击败图格鲁克王朝苏丹纳绥尔丁·马哈茂德，纵兵劫掠全城数日，德里苏丹国由此残破；随后他携俘虏和工匠返回撒马尔罕。

sources.title: Sharaf al-Din Ali Yazdi, Zafarnama
Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)
Wikidata Q123179707

events.note: The date is the battle outside Delhi; the sack followed over the next days.

summary.en: Zhu Di, Prince of Yan, rebelled at Beiping against his nephew the Jianwen Emperor, who was stripping the princes of power. After three years of war he took Nanjing and enthroned himself as the Yongle Emperor.
summary.zh: 燕王朱棣不满建文帝削藩，于北平起兵“靖难”，历时三年攻入南京，即位为明成祖。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷5 成祖本纪一

image.artist: 玖巧仔, translated to English by Alex Shih

summary.en: The fugitive Palembang prince Parameswara settled at Malacca around 1400. With Ming recognition and its command of the strait, the port grew into the greatest entrepôt of Southeast Asia and a centre for the spread of Islam.
summary.zh: 流亡的巨港王子拜里米苏拉约在1400年定居马六甲。凭借明朝的册封和对海峡的控制，这座港口发展为东南亚最大的转口贸易中心，也是伊斯兰教传播的中心。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Founding of the Malacca Sultanate
Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals), trans. C. C. Brown (1952)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca Sultanate

events.note: Founding dates between c. 1396 and 1402 are proposed.

summary.en: Timur defeated and captured the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I near Ankara. The Ottoman state nearly disintegrated in the civil war that followed (1402–1413), delaying its expansion and the fall of Constantinople by half a century.
summary.zh: 帖木儿在安卡拉附近击败并俘虏奥斯曼苏丹巴耶济德一世。奥斯曼国家在随后的内战（1402—1413年）中几近瓦解，扩张和攻取君士坦丁堡因此推迟了半个世纪。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Ankara
C. Finkel, Osman's Dream: The History of the Ottoman Empire (2005)
Wikipedia: Battle of Ankara

summary.en: Between 1405 and 1433 the eunuch admiral Zheng He led seven fleets of large treasure ships from Liujiagang through Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean to Hormuz, Arabia and the East African coast, enrolling dozens of states in the Ming tribute order.
summary.zh: 1405至1433年，郑和七次率宝船队自刘家港出发，经东南亚、印度洋远达忽鲁谟斯、阿拉伯与东非，招徕数十国朝贡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: More than two thousand scholars under Xie Jin and Yao Guangxiao compiled the Yongle Encyclopedia in Nanjing: 22,877 chapters copying some seven to eight thousand earlier works. Only about four percent survives.
summary.zh: 解缙、姚广孝主持两千余人在南京编成《永乐大典》二万二千八百余卷，辑录古籍七八千种，今仅存约百分之四。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷147 解缙传

summary.en: The allied armies of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Władysław II Jagiełło and Vytautas crushed the Teutonic Knights; Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen was killed. The defeat began the long decline of the Teutonic Order's state in Prussia.
summary.zh: 波兰王国与立陶宛大公国联军在瓦迪斯瓦夫二世·雅盖沃和维陶塔斯指挥下大败条顿骑士团，大团长乌尔里希·冯·容金根阵亡。此役开启了条顿骑士团国家在普鲁士的长期衰落。

sources.title: Jan Długosz, Annales seu cronicae incliti Regni Poloniae, Book XI
Britannica: Battle of Grunwald

summary.en: Lê Lợi raised a rebellion against Ming occupation at Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa. After a decade of guerrilla war and the destruction of a Ming relief army at Chi Lăng in 1427, the Ming withdrew and Lê Lợi founded the Later Lê dynasty.
summary.zh: 黎利在清化蓝山起兵反抗明朝统治。经过十年游击战，并于1427年在支棱歼灭明朝援军后，明军撤离，黎利建立后黎朝。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Lam Sơn uprising

summary.en: With the Forbidden City completed in 1420, the Yongle Emperor formally made Beijing the principal capital from New Year 1421, leaving Nanjing as the auxiliary capital; Beijing remained the capital until 1928.
summary.zh: 紫禁城于1420年建成，永乐十九年正月明成祖正式迁都北京，以南京为留都；北京此后为都城至1928年。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷7 成祖本纪三 永乐十八年、十九年

events.note: The Wikidata item is the Forbidden City (completed 1420).

summary.en: An Ayutthayan army besieged and took the Khmer capital. The Khmer court soon moved south toward the Phnom Penh area, closing the Angkorian era.
summary.zh: 阿瑜陀耶军队围攻并攻陷高棉都城。高棉王廷随后南迁至金边一带，吴哥时代就此结束。

sources.title: David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya, trans. Richard D. Cushman (Siam Society, 2000)
Wikipedia: Fall of Angkor

events.note: The 1431 date comes from later chronicles; historians see Angkor's decline as gradual and the date as conventional.

summary.en: King Sejong completed a new phonetic alphabet in 1443 and promulgated it in 1446 in the document Hunminjeongeum, "the correct sounds for instructing the people", so that commoners could read and write Korean.
summary.zh: 世宗大王于1443年创制了一套新的表音文字，并于1446年以《训民正音》（意为“教百姓以正确的字音”）颁布，使平民也能读写朝鲜语。

sources.title: Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
UNESCO Memory of the World Register: Hunmin Chongum Manuscript
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Hunminjeongeum

summary.en: Persuaded by the eunuch Wang Zhen to campaign in person, the Zhengtong Emperor was routed by the Oirat leader Esen at Tumu fortress and taken prisoner. Minister Yu Qian enthroned his brother and defended Beijing.
summary.zh: 明英宗听信宦官王振亲征瓦剌，于土木堡被也先击溃俘虏；兵部尚书于谦拥立景泰帝，固守北京。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷10 英宗前纪 正统十四年
张廷玉等《明史》卷170 于谦传

summary.en: After a siege of about seven weeks, the Ottoman army of Sultan Mehmed II stormed Constantinople; the last emperor, Constantine XI Palaiologos, died in the fighting. The conquest ended the Byzantine Empire and made the city the Ottoman capital.
summary.zh: 经过约七周的围攻，苏丹穆罕默德二世的奥斯曼军队攻破君士坦丁堡，末代皇帝君士坦丁十一世·巴列奥略战死。此役终结了拜占庭帝国，该城随后成为奥斯曼帝国的首都。

sources.title: Kritoboulos of Imbros, History of Mehmed the Conqueror
Steven Runciman, The Fall of Constantinople 1453 (1965)
Britannica: Fall of Constantinople

name.zh: 谷登堡《圣经》与活字印刷

summary.en: In Mainz, Johannes Gutenberg's workshop completed the 42-line Latin Bible, the first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type. Printing spread to more than 200 European towns by 1500, transforming the circulation of knowledge.
summary.zh: 约翰内斯·谷登堡在美因茨的作坊完成了四十二行拉丁文《圣经》，这是欧洲首部以金属活字印刷的重要书籍。到1500年，印刷术已传播至欧洲两百多个城镇，彻底改变了知识的传播方式。

sources.title: Albert Kapr, Johann Gutenberg: The Man and His Invention (1996)
Britannica: Gutenberg Bible

events.note: The Bible has no colophon; it is dated c. 1454–55 from a letter of Enea Silvio Piccolomini (March 1455) and a rubricator's note of 1456. Wikidata has no date.

image.file: Gutenberg Bible, Lenox Copy, New York Public Library, 2009. Pic 01.jpg

summary.en: Mehmed II besieged Trebizond, capital of the last Byzantine successor state, and Emperor David Komnenos surrendered in August 1461. Its fall ended the Empire of Trebizond, founded in 1204, and the last Byzantine rule in Anatolia.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德二世围攻最后一个拜占庭继承国的首都特拉布宗，皇帝大卫·科穆宁于1461年8月投降。特拉布宗帝国（建于1204年）随之灭亡，拜占庭在安纳托利亚的统治宣告终结。

sources.title: Kritovoulos, History of Mehmed the Conqueror (trans. C. T. Riggs, 1954)
F. Babinger, Mehmed the Conqueror and His Time (1978)
Wikipedia: Siege of Trebizond (1461)

summary.en: A succession dispute in the Ashikaga shogunate drew the Hosokawa and Yamana coalitions into a decade of fighting that burned much of Kyoto. The shogunate never recovered its authority, opening the Sengoku (Warring States) era.
summary.zh: 足利将军家的继嗣纷争使细川与山名两大阵营在京都激战十年，城市大半焚毁。幕府权威一蹶不振，日本由此进入战国时代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ōnin War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Ōnin War

events.note: Coordinates set on Kyoto, where the fighting took place; the Wikidata point lies about 17 km to the south.

summary.en: After a ten-year war (1482–1492), Emir Muhammad XII surrendered Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia, to Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile. The surrender completed the Christian Reconquista.
summary.zh: 经过十年战争（1482—1492年），埃米尔穆罕默德十二世将伊比利亚最后的穆斯林政权格拉纳达交给阿拉贡的斐迪南二世与卡斯蒂利亚的伊莎贝拉一世，基督教的“收复失地运动”至此完成。

sources.title: L. P. Harvey, Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500 (1990)
Britannica: Granada

events.note: QID is the Granada War; Wikidata's start date for it (1492) conflicts with the standard 1482 start, so only the surrender date is used here.

summary.en: Sailing for the Crown of Castile, Christopher Columbus left Palos with three ships, crossed the Atlantic via the Canary Islands and reached the Bahamas on 12 October 1492. His return in 1493 launched sustained European contact with, and colonisation of, the Americas.
summary.zh: 哥伦布受卡斯蒂利亚王室资助，率三艘船从帕洛斯出发，经加那利群岛横渡大西洋，于1492年10月12日抵达巴哈马。1493年他返航后，欧洲开始与美洲持续接触并殖民美洲。

label.zh: 离开加那利群岛戈梅拉岛
登陆瓜纳哈尼（圣萨尔瓦多岛）

summary.en: Guided across the Arabian Sea from Malindi, the Portuguese fleet anchored near Calicut, the Zamorin’s spice port, completing the first sea voyage from Europe to India and opening the era of European sea power in the Indian Ocean.
summary.zh: 葡萄牙船队在马林迪领航员引导下横渡阿拉伯海，停泊于扎莫林的香料港卡利卡特附近，完成了从欧洲到印度的首次航行，开启了欧洲海上势力进入印度洋的时代。

sources.title: Álvaro Velho (attrib.), Roteiro da primeira viagem de Vasco da Gama (journal of the first voyage)

name.en: Battle of Sharur and the rise of the Safavids
name.zh: 沙鲁尔之战与萨法维王朝兴起

summary.en: Leading Qizilbash Turkmen followers, the teenage Ismail defeated the Aq Qoyunlu at Sharur, entered Tabriz and was proclaimed shah. He made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion, founding the Safavid dynasty that shaped modern Iran.
summary.zh: 少年伊斯玛仪率领红头军土库曼部众在沙鲁尔击败白羊王朝，进入大不里士称沙阿。他定十二伊玛目什叶派为国教，建立了塑造近代伊朗的萨法维王朝。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ismail I
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Safavids
Wikipedia: Battle of Sharur

events.note: Wikidata dates the battle 17 July 1501; other sources place it a few weeks earlier. Coronation at Tabriz followed in 1501.

summary.en: Afonso de Albuquerque stormed Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate at the second attempt; it became the capital of Portuguese India and stayed Portuguese until 1961.
summary.zh: 阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克第二次进攻时从比贾布尔苏丹国手中夺取果阿；此地成为葡属印度首府，直至1961年仍归葡萄牙所有。

sources.title: Sanjay Subrahmanyam, The Portuguese Empire in Asia, 1500–1700 (1993)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Afonso de Albuquerque
