image.file: "Plan de Goa", in Histoire générale des voyages,1750.jpg

summary.en: Afonso de Albuquerque's fleet stormed Malacca after weeks of fighting, driving out Sultan Mahmud Shah. Portugal gained a key base on the spice route, while Muslim traders dispersed to rival ports such as Aceh, Johor and Banten.
summary.zh: 阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克的舰队经数周激战攻占马六甲，苏丹马哈茂德沙出逃。葡萄牙由此获得香料航线上的关键据点，穆斯林商人则分散到亚齐、柔佛、万丹等竞争港口。

sources.title: Brás de Albuquerque, Commentaries of the Great Afonso Dalboquerque (1557; Hakluyt Society trans. 1875–84)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Capture of Malacca (1511)

image.file: Conquista de Malaca, estudo - Ernesto Condeixa (cropped).png

summary.en: The Ottoman sultan Selim I, with artillery and Janissary firearms, defeated Shah Ismail's Qizilbash cavalry at Chaldiran and briefly occupied Tabriz. The battle set a long-lasting Ottoman–Safavid frontier across eastern Anatolia and Mesopotamia.
summary.zh: 奥斯曼苏丹塞利姆一世凭借火炮和近卫军火器，在查尔迪兰击败伊斯玛仪沙阿的红头军骑兵，并一度占领大不里士。此役确立了横贯安纳托利亚东部和美索不达米亚的奥斯曼—萨法维长期边界。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Chaldiran
C. Finkel, Osman's Dream (2005)
Wikipedia: Battle of Chaldiran

name.en: Ottoman–Mamluk War (Ottoman conquest of Syria and Egypt)
name.zh: 奥斯曼-马穆鲁克战争（奥斯曼征服叙利亚与埃及）

summary.en: Selim I turned south after Chaldiran, killing the Mamluk sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri at Marj Dabiq and taking Aleppo, Damascus and Jerusalem, then Cairo in January 1517. The Ottomans gained Syria, Egypt and guardianship of Mecca and Medina.
summary.zh: 查尔迪兰之战后，塞利姆一世挥师南下，在达比格草原击毙马穆鲁克苏丹甘苏赫·古里，夺取阿勒颇、大马士革和耶路撒冷，并于1517年1月攻入开罗。奥斯曼由此获得叙利亚、埃及及麦加和麦地那的守护权。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ottoman Empire
Ibn Iyas, Bada'i al-Zuhur fi Waqa'i al-Duhur
Wikipedia: Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)

events.note: Event point at Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516).

name.zh: 路德发表《九十五条论纲》

summary.en: Martin Luther, a theology professor at Wittenberg, circulated 95 theses disputing the sale of indulgences and sent them to Archbishop Albert of Mainz. Rapidly printed and spread, they sparked the Protestant Reformation that divided Western Christianity.
summary.zh: 维滕贝格大学神学教授马丁·路德提出《九十五条论纲》，抨击出售赎罪券，并寄呈美因茨大主教阿尔布雷希特。论纲经印刷迅速传播，引发了导致西方基督教分裂的宗教改革。

sources.title: Martin Luther, Disputatio pro declaratione virtutis indulgentiarum (1517)
Britannica: Ninety-five Theses
Britannica: Reformation

events.note: Luther's covering letter to Archbishop Albert is dated 31 October 1517; whether he also nailed the theses to the Castle Church door is debated.

summary.en: Ferdinand Magellan, seeking to force the chief Lapulapu to submit to his Christian ally Rajah Humabon of Cebu, landed on Mactan with about 50 men and was killed. The expedition sailed on and completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.
summary.zh: 麦哲伦为迫使酋长拉普拉普臣服于已受洗的宿务王胡马邦，率约五十人登陆麦克坦岛，结果战死。船队继续航行，并于1522年完成首次环球航行。

label.en: Exits the Strait of Magellan into the Pacific (Nov 1520)
label.zh: 驶出麦哲伦海峡进入太平洋（1520年11月）
利马萨瓦岛：首次弥撒（3月31日）

sources.title: Antonio Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (c. 1524), trans. R. A. Skelton (1969)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ferdinand Magellan
Wikipedia: Battle of Mactan

summary.en: Babur’s smaller army, using field guns behind a wagon barricade and flanking cavalry, defeated Sultan Ibrahim Lodi, who died on the field; the victory ended the Delhi Sultanate and founded the Mughal Empire.
summary.zh: 巴布尔兵力较少，以车阵掩护火炮并辅以侧翼骑兵，击败苏丹易卜拉欣·洛迪，后者阵亡；此战终结了德里苏丹国，开创莫卧儿帝国。

sources.title: Babur, Baburnama (tr. Wheeler M. Thackston, 1996)
John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)
Wikidata Q605321

events.note: 21 April 1526 is the Julian date used by most historians; Wikidata stores the proleptic Gregorian equivalent (1 May).

image.file: Battle of Panipat (20 April 1526). Baburnama of 1598.jpg

summary.en: Babur defeated the Rajput confederacy of Rana Sanga of Mewar near Fatehpur Sikri, securing Mughal control of the upper Ganges plain against its strongest rival.
summary.zh: 巴布尔在法塔赫布尔西格里附近击败梅瓦尔的拉纳·桑加所领导的拉其普特联盟，确保了莫卧儿王朝对恒河上游平原的控制。

sources.title: Babur, Baburnama (tr. Wheeler M. Thackston, 1996)
John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)
Wikidata Q4166578

image.file: Babur’s army in battle against the army of Rana Sanga at.jpg
image.artist: "Mirza 'Abd al-Rahim, Khan-i khanan (Mirza 'Abd al-Rahim, Khan-i khanan)"

name.zh: 哥白尼出版《天体运行论》

summary.en: Nicolaus Copernicus's De revolutionibus orbium coelestium was printed in Nuremberg shortly before his death. Placing the Sun near the centre of the universe with Earth orbiting it, the book laid the groundwork for the Scientific Revolution.
summary.zh: 哥白尼的《天体运行论》在纽伦堡付印，出版于他去世前不久。该书提出太阳位于宇宙中心附近、地球绕其运行，为科学革命奠定了基础。

sources.title: Owen Gingerich, The Book Nobody Read (2004)
Britannica: Nicolaus Copernicus

summary.en: Suleiman I and Shah Tahmasp I ended four decades of war with the first formal Ottoman–Safavid peace. The Ottomans kept Baghdad, most of Iraq and eastern Anatolia; Iran kept Azerbaijan, and the South Caucasus was divided.
summary.zh: 苏莱曼一世与塔赫玛斯普一世签订首个正式的奥斯曼—萨法维和约，结束了四十年战争。奥斯曼保有巴格达、伊拉克大部和安纳托利亚东部，伊朗保有阿塞拜疆，南高加索被瓜分。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Peace of Amasya
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Amasya, Peace of
Wikipedia: Peace of Amasya

summary.en: Akbar’s regent Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, the Sur dynasty general who had just seized Delhi; Hemu was struck by an arrow and captured, restoring Mughal rule under the 13-year-old Akbar.
summary.zh: 阿克巴的摄政拜拉姆汗击败刚刚夺取德里的苏尔王朝将领希穆；希穆中箭被俘，莫卧儿王朝在13岁的阿克巴治下得以复兴。

sources.title: Abu'l-Fazl, Akbarnama (tr. H. Beveridge)
John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)
Wikidata Q233414

summary.en: Oda Nobunaga, with a small force, surprised and killed the daimyō Imagawa Yoshimoto, whose much larger army was marching through Owari. The victory launched Nobunaga's rise as a unifier of Japan.
summary.zh: 织田信长以少量兵力奇袭行军经过尾张的今川义元大军，并斩杀义元。此役使信长崛起，开始统一日本的进程。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Okehazama
Jeroen P. Lamers, Japonius Tyrannus: The Japanese Warlord Oda Nobunaga Reconsidered (Hotei, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Wikipedia: Battle of Okehazama

summary.en: An alliance of the Deccan sultanates defeated Vijayanagara’s regent Rama Raya, who was beheaded; the capital at Hampi was then sacked and the empire never regained its power.
summary.zh: 德干诸苏丹国联军击败毗奢耶那伽罗的摄政罗摩·罗阇，并将其斩首；都城亨比随后遭洗劫，帝国从此一蹶不振。

sources.title: Burton Stein, Vijayanagara (New Cambridge History of India I.2, 1989)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Talikota
Wikidata Q1362188

events.note: Some sources give 23 January 1565.

summary.en: The parliament meeting at Lublin turned the personal union of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania into a single Commonwealth with a jointly elected monarch and common Sejm. The new state was one of Europe's largest until its partitions in the late 18th century.
summary.zh: 在卢布林召开的议会将波兰王国与立陶宛大公国的君合国转变为统一的联邦，两国共同选举君主、设立共同议会。这一新国家在18世纪末被瓜分之前，一直是欧洲面积最大的国家之一。

sources.title: Norman Davies, God's Playground: A History of Poland, vol. 1 (1981)
Britannica: Union of Lublin

name.zh: 阿克巴营建法塔赫布尔西格里

summary.en: Akbar raised a red-sandstone capital at Sikri to honour the Sufi Shaikh Salim Chishti, who had foretold the birth of his heir; it hosted his religious debates in the Ibadat Khana before the court left around 1585.
summary.zh: 阿克巴在西格里兴建红砂岩新都，以纪念曾预言其继承人诞生的苏菲长老萨利姆·契斯提；宫廷约1585年迁离之前，阿克巴在此的“礼拜堂”主持宗教辩论。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Fatehpur Sikri
Abu'l-Fazl, Akbarnama (tr. H. Beveridge)
Wikidata Q179046

events.note: Work began in 1569 (Wikidata); the city was proclaimed capital in 1571.

summary.en: After defeating Rajah Sulayman's Maynila, Miguel López de Legazpi proclaimed the Spanish city of Manila, later walled as Intramuros. It became the capital of the Spanish Philippines and the Asian terminus of the Manila galleons to Acapulco.
summary.zh: 米格尔·洛佩斯·德·黎牙实比击败苏莱曼王统治的马尼拉后，宣布建立西班牙马尼拉城，后筑城墙成为王城区（Intramuros）。这里成为西属菲律宾首府和通往阿卡普尔科的马尼拉大帆船贸易的亚洲终点。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Spanish Manila founded
Emma H. Blair & James A. Robertson (eds.), The Philippine Islands, 1493–1898, Vol. 3 (1903)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Intramuros

summary.en: Mughal forces under Man Singh fought Maharana Pratap of Mewar in a narrow Aravalli pass; Pratap withdrew but kept up resistance and became a lasting emblem of Rajput defiance.
summary.zh: 曼·辛格率领的莫卧儿军队在阿拉瓦利山的狭窄山口与梅瓦尔的普拉塔普王交战；普拉塔普虽撤退但坚持抵抗，成为拉其普特人不屈的长久象征。

sources.title: Abu'l-Fazl, Akbarnama (tr. H. Beveridge)
John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)
Wikidata Q3635360

summary.en: Philip II of Spain sent a fleet of about 130 ships to escort an invasion army from Flanders to England. Harried in the Channel, scattered by fireships off Calais and beaten at Gravelines, the Armada fled round Scotland and Ireland, losing many ships to storms.
summary.zh: 西班牙国王腓力二世派出约130艘战舰，意图护送驻佛兰德的军队入侵英格兰。无敌舰队在英吉利海峡遭英舰袭扰，在加来外海被火船冲散，又在格拉沃利讷战败，被迫绕道苏格兰和爱尔兰返航，途中因风暴损失惨重。

sources.title: Garrett Mattingly, The Defeat of the Spanish Armada (1959)
Colin Martin and Geoffrey Parker, The Spanish Armada (1988)
Britannica: Spanish Armada

events.note: Event coordinates follow Wikidata (off Plymouth, the first engagement). English contemporaries used Old Style dates, ten days behind the Spanish (New Style) ones.

image.file: English Ships and the Spanish Armada, August 1588 RMG BHC0262.jpg

summary.en: Guru Arjan built the Harmandir Sahib in the sacred pool of Amritsar and installed the newly compiled Adi Granth there in 1604; rebuilt and gilded under Ranjit Singh, the Golden Temple is Sikhism’s holiest shrine.
summary.zh: 古鲁阿尔琼在阿姆利则圣池中建造哈曼迪尔寺，并于1604年将新编成的《阿迪·格兰特》供奉于此；该寺在兰吉特·辛格时期重建并贴金，即锡克教最神圣的金庙。

sources.title: J. S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (New Cambridge History of India II.3, 1990)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Golden Temple
Wikidata Q180422

events.note: The 1589 foundation follows Wikidata; some accounts place the start in 1581 or 1588.

name.zh: 壬辰倭乱（万历朝鲜战争）

summary.en: Toyotomi Hideyoshi sent some 150,000 troops into Joseon in 1592, aiming ultimately at Ming China. After rapid Japanese advances, Ming intervention, guerrilla resistance and Yi Sun-sin's navy stalled the campaign; a second invasion in 1597 ended with Hideyoshi's death and withdrawal in 1598.
summary.zh: 1592年丰臣秀吉派遣约十五万大军入侵朝鲜，最终目标是明朝。日军初期推进迅速，但明军援朝、义兵抗击与李舜臣水军使战事陷入僵局；1597年再度入侵，1598年秀吉死后日军撤退。

label.zh: 肥前名护屋城：出兵基地

label.en: Yi Sun-sin wins at Hansan Island

sources.title: Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail: Ming China and the First Great East Asian War, 1592–1598 (University of Oklahoma Press, 2009)
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)
Yu Seong-ryong, Jingbirok (Book of Corrections, c. 1604)
Wikipedia: Imjin War

summary.en: Admiral Yi Sun-sin lured a Japanese fleet into open water near Hansan Island and enveloped it in a "crane-wing" formation, sinking or capturing most of the ships. The victory cut Japanese sea supply along Korea's southern coast.
summary.zh: 李舜臣将日本舰队诱至闲山岛附近的开阔海域，以“鹤翼阵”合围，击沉或俘获大部分敌船。此役切断了日军沿朝鲜南海岸的海上补给线。

sources.title: Yi Sun-sin, Nanjung ilgi (War Diary, 1592–1598)
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)
Wikipedia: Battle of Hansan Island

summary.en: With only 13 warships left after the Joseon navy's disaster at Chilcheollyang, Yi Sun-sin used the fierce tidal currents of the Myeongnyang Strait to repel a Japanese fleet many times larger, halting the Japanese advance by sea.
summary.zh: 朝鲜水军在漆川梁惨败后，李舜臣仅余十三艘战船，他利用鸣梁海峡湍急的潮流，击退数倍于己的日本舰队，阻止了日军的海上推进。

sources.title: Yi Sun-sin, Nanjung ilgi (War Diary, 1592–1598)
Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail: Ming China and the First Great East Asian War, 1592–1598 (University of Oklahoma Press, 2009)
Wikipedia: Battle of Myeongnyang

name.zh: 伊斯法罕成为萨法维首都

summary.en: Shah Abbas I moved his capital from Qazvin to Isfahan and rebuilt the city around the vast Naqsh-e Jahan Square with its royal mosque, palace and bazaar. "Isfahan is half the world" became a proverb for its splendour.
summary.zh: 阿拔斯一世将首都从加兹温迁至伊斯法罕，并围绕宏大的伊玛目广场（世界图景广场）兴建王家清真寺、宫殿和巴扎。“伊斯法罕半天下”成为赞美其繁华的谚语。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Abbas I
S. Babaie, Isfahan and Its Palaces (2008)
Wikipedia: Naqsh-e Jahan Square

events.note: Uses the Naqsh-e Jahan Square item; Wikidata dates the square from 1591, while the move of the capital is usually dated 1598.

summary.en: Tokugawa Ieyasu's Eastern Army defeated the Western Army led by Ishida Mitsunari, helped by defections during the battle. The victory made Ieyasu master of Japan; he became shogun in 1603.
summary.zh: 德川家康率领的东军在战场倒戈的帮助下击败石田三成为首的西军。此役使家康成为日本实际的统治者，并于1603年就任征夷大将军。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Sekigahara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Battle of Sekigahara

image.artist: User LordAmeth on en.wikipediaCollection of The Town of Sekigahara Archive of History and Cultural Anthropology

summary.en: In two winter and summer campaigns the Tokugawa besieged Osaka Castle, the last stronghold of Toyotomi Hideyori. Its fall in 1615 destroyed the Toyotomi line and secured Tokugawa rule for two and a half centuries.
summary.zh: 德川方分冬、夏两阵围攻丰臣秀赖的最后据点大坂城。1615年城陷，丰臣氏灭亡，德川统治由此稳固了两个半世纪。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Siege of Osaka

summary.en: Beginning with the Defenestration of Prague, a revolt of Bohemian Protestants against Habsburg rule grew into a European war involving the Holy Roman Empire, Sweden, Denmark, France and Spain. The fighting devastated Germany, where perhaps a fifth or more of the population died.
summary.zh: 以布拉格掷出窗外事件为开端，波希米亚新教徒反抗哈布斯堡统治的起义演变为一场席卷欧洲的大战，神圣罗马帝国、瑞典、丹麦、法国和西班牙相继卷入。战火重创德意志地区，可能有五分之一以上的人口丧生。

sources.title: Peter H. Wilson, Europe's Tragedy: A History of the Thirty Years War (2009)
Britannica: Thirty Years' War

events.note: Placed at Prague Castle, site of the Defenestration of 23 May 1618.

summary.en: Nurhaci's Later Jin destroyed three of four converging Ming columns one after another in five days near Sarhu, shifting the balance of power in Liaodong to the Manchus.
summary.zh: 努尔哈赤“凭尔几路来，我只一路去”，五日内于萨尔浒等地各个击破明军四路中的三路，辽东攻守之势自此逆转。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷259 杨镐传
《满洲实录》卷5

summary.en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) destroyed the town of Jayakarta and built Batavia on its ruins. It became the VOC's Asian headquarters and later the capital of the Dutch East Indies.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司的扬·彼得松·库恩摧毁查雅加达城，并在废墟上兴建巴达维亚。这里成为荷兰东印度公司的亚洲总部，后来成为荷属东印度首府。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Batavia, Dutch East Indies

summary.en: Ming commander Yuan Chonghuan, using Portuguese-style cannon on the walls of Ningyuan (Xingcheng), repulsed Nurhaci's assault – his first major defeat; Nurhaci died later that year.
summary.zh: 袁崇焕凭宁远孤城与红夷大炮击退努尔哈赤，后金首遭大败，努尔哈赤同年病逝。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷259 袁崇焕传

summary.en: Shah Jahan commissioned this white-marble mausoleum at Agra for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631; built by thousands of artisans over two decades, it is the masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
summary.zh: 沙贾汗为1631年去世的皇后慕塔芝·玛哈在阿格拉修建这座白色大理石陵墓；数千名工匠历时二十余年建成，是莫卧儿建筑的巅峰之作。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Taj Mahal
Ebba Koch, The Complete Taj Mahal (2006)
Wikidata Q9141

image.artist: Taj_Mahal,_Agra,_India_edit2.jpg: Yann; edited by King of Hearts derivative work: Jbarta (talk)

summary.en: The Roman Inquisition found Galileo Galilei 'vehemently suspect of heresy' for defending Copernican heliocentrism in his Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems. He was forced to recant and spent his remaining years under house arrest near Florence.
summary.zh: 罗马宗教裁判所认定伽利略因在《关于两大世界体系的对话》中为哥白尼日心说辩护而“有强烈异端嫌疑”。他被迫公开放弃其观点，余生在佛罗伦萨附近遭软禁。

sources.title: Maurice A. Finocchiaro (ed.), The Galileo Affair: A Documentary History (1989)
Britannica: Galileo

events.note: The Wikidata item covers the whole Galileo affair (1610–1633); this record marks the sentence and abjuration at Santa Maria sopra Minerva on 22 June 1633.

summary.en: Overtaxed peasants and masterless samurai of Shimabara and Amakusa, many of them Christian, rose and held Hara Castle until it fell to a shogunal army in 1638. The revolt hardened the ban on Christianity and the exclusion of the Portuguese.
summary.zh: 岛原与天草地区不堪重税的农民和浪人（多为天主教徒）起事，据守原城，1638年被幕府大军攻陷。此后幕府更加严厉地禁教，并驱逐葡萄牙人。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Shimabara Rebellion
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Shimabara Rebellion

summary.en: A series of Tokugawa edicts in the 1630s banned Japanese from travelling abroad, expelled the Portuguese and confined Dutch trade to Dejima in Nagasaki. Controlled contacts continued with China, Korea, the Ryukyus and the Ainu until the 1850s.
summary.zh: 17世纪30年代德川幕府颁布一系列法令，禁止日本人出海、驱逐葡萄牙人，并将荷兰贸易限制在长崎出岛。与中国、朝鲜、琉球及阿伊努的有限往来则一直持续到19世纪50年代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sakoku (maritime restrictions)
Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Wikipedia: Sakoku

events.note: The term sakoku was coined only in 1801; historians debate how closed Japan really was.

summary.en: Signed near Qasr-e Shirin, the treaty ended the Ottoman–Safavid war of 1623–1639. Baghdad and Mesopotamia stayed Ottoman, and the Zagros frontier it set roughly anticipates today's Iran–Iraq and Iran–Turkey borders.
summary.zh: 条约在席林堡附近签订，结束了1623—1639年的奥斯曼—萨法维战争。巴格达和美索不达米亚归奥斯曼所有，所定的扎格罗斯边界大致与今日伊朗—伊拉克、伊朗—土耳其边界相当。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Treaty of Qasr-e Shirin
C. Finkel, Osman's Dream (2005)
Wikipedia: Treaty of Zuhab

name.en: Battle of Shanhai Pass and fall of the Ming

summary.en: Weeks after Li Zicheng took Beijing and the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself, the Ming general Wu Sangui opened Shanhai Pass to the Qing regent Dorgon; their combined forces routed Li, and the Qing moved its capital to Beijing.
summary.zh: 李自成攻破北京、崇祯帝自缢后，吴三桂开山海关降清，与多尔衮合击大顺军，清军入关，定都北京。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷4 世祖本纪一 顺治元年
张廷玉等《明史》卷24 庄烈帝纪二

summary.en: Treaties signed at Osnabrück and Münster ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch Republic. They recognised Dutch and Swiss independence, extended toleration to Calvinists and strengthened the sovereignty of the German princes.
summary.zh: 在奥斯纳布吕克与明斯特签订的一系列条约，结束了神圣罗马帝国境内的三十年战争以及西班牙与荷兰共和国之间的八十年战争。和约承认荷兰与瑞士独立，将宗教宽容扩展至加尔文派，并增强了德意志诸侯的主权。

sources.title: Instrumentum Pacis Osnabrugense and Monasteriense (1648)
Britannica: Peace of Westphalia

events.note: The Spanish–Dutch Peace of Münster was signed on 30 January 1648; the imperial treaties on 24 October 1648 (Wikidata date).

name.en: Koxinga takes Taiwan from the Dutch

summary.en: Ming loyalist Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga) landed at Luermen and besieged the Dutch East India Company's Fort Zeelandia for nine months, forcing its surrender in February 1662 and founding a Zheng regime on Taiwan.
summary.zh: 明郑延平王郑成功自鹿耳门登陆，围攻荷兰东印度公司热兰遮城九个月，1662年2月荷军投降，郑氏据台。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
江日昇《台湾外记》
Britannica: Zheng Chenggong

summary.en: When the Kangxi Emperor moved to abolish their fiefs, Wu Sangui in Yunnan and the princes in Guangdong and Fujian rebelled. After eight years of war Qing forces took Kunming in 1681.
summary.zh: 康熙帝下令撤藩，吴三桂于云南起兵，广东尚氏、福建耿氏响应；历时八年，1681年清军攻克昆明平定。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷474 吴三桂传

summary.en: A relief army of imperial, German and Polish–Lithuanian troops under King John III Sobieski routed the Ottoman forces of Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha besieging Vienna. The victory began a long Habsburg counter-offensive that recovered Hungary by 1699.
summary.zh: 由神圣罗马帝国、德意志诸邦和波兰—立陶宛军队组成、波兰国王扬三世·索别斯基统率的援军，击溃了围攻维也纳的大维齐尔卡拉·穆斯塔法帕夏的奥斯曼军队。此役开启了哈布斯堡王朝的长期反攻，至1699年收复匈牙利。

sources.title: John Stoye, The Siege of Vienna (1964)
Britannica: Siege of Vienna

name.zh: 牛顿《自然哲学的数学原理》出版

summary.en: Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, issued in London under the Royal Society's imprimatur at Edmond Halley's expense, set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation. It unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics and became a foundation of modern physics.
summary.zh: 牛顿的《自然哲学的数学原理》经皇家学会批准在伦敦出版，费用由埃德蒙·哈雷承担。书中提出运动定律和万有引力定律，统一了地面力学与天体力学，成为近代物理学的基石。

sources.title: Richard S. Westfall, Never at Rest: A Biography of Isaac Newton (1980)
Britannica: Principia

events.note: Wikidata's inception (1680) reflects when Newton began the work; publication was on 5 July 1687.

image.artist: The original uploader was Zhaladshar at English Wikisource.

summary.en: After Qing forces besieged the Russian fort of Albazin, envoys led by Songgotu signed China's first treaty with a European state at Nerchinsk, fixing the border along the Argun river and the Stanovoy range.
summary.zh: 清军两次围攻雅克萨后，索额图与俄使在尼布楚签订条约，以额尔古纳河与外兴安岭划定中俄东段边界，是中国与欧洲国家的首个条约。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷7 圣祖本纪二 康熙二十八年
Britannica: Treaty of Nerchinsk

summary.en: Peter the Great's Russian army decisively defeated Charles XII of Sweden near Poltava in the Great Northern War. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and established Russia as the dominant state of north-eastern Europe.
summary.zh: 大北方战争中，彼得大帝的俄军在波尔塔瓦附近决定性地击败瑞典国王卡尔十二世。此役终结了瑞典的强国时代，确立了俄国在东北欧的主导地位。

sources.title: Peter Englund, The Battle That Shook Europe: Poltava and the Birth of the Russian Empire (2003)
Britannica: Battle of Poltava

events.note: Wikidata gives 27 June 1709, the Julian (Old Style) date used in Russia; 8 July is the Gregorian date (28 June in the Swedish calendar).

summary.en: Nader Shah of Persia routed the far larger army of the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah, then occupied and plundered Delhi, carrying off the Peacock Throne and exposing Mughal weakness.
summary.zh: 波斯的纳迪尔沙击溃兵力远胜于己的莫卧儿皇帝穆罕默德沙的军队，随即占领并劫掠德里，掠走孔雀宝座，莫卧儿王朝的衰弱暴露无遗。

sources.title: Michael Axworthy, The Sword of Persia (2006)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nadir Shah
Wikidata Q2736986

image.file: Nadir Shah at the sack of Delhi - Battle scene with Nader Shah on horseback, possibly by Muhammad Ali ibn Abd al-Bayg ibn Ali Quli Jabbadar, mid-18th century, Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.jpg
image.artist: possibly by Muhammad Ali ibn Abd al-Bayg ibn Ali Quli Jabbadar

summary.en: On All Saints' Day a great earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands. The disaster prompted Pombal's planned rebuilding of the city and fuelled Enlightenment debate about providence, notably in Voltaire's writings.
summary.zh: 万圣节当天，一场大地震及随后的海啸和大火摧毁了里斯本大部分城区，造成数万人死亡。灾后庞巴尔侯爵主持规划重建，这场灾难也引发了以伏尔泰为代表的启蒙思想家关于天意的辩论。

sources.title: Voltaire, Poème sur le désastre de Lisbonne (1756)
Britannica: Lisbon earthquake of 1755

events.note: Wikidata's coordinates (36.0, −11.0) are the estimated offshore epicentre; this record is placed at Lisbon, the city destroyed.

summary.en: Robert Clive’s East India Company force defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, Nawab of Bengal, after his commander Mir Jafar defected; the battle made the Company the power behind the Bengal throne and began British territorial rule in India.
summary.zh: 罗伯特·克莱武率领的东印度公司军队在孟加拉纳瓦卜西拉杰·乌德·达乌拉的将领米尔·贾法尔倒戈后将其击败；公司由此操纵孟加拉政权，英国在印度的领土统治自此开始。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Plassey
P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (New Cambridge History of India II.2, 1987)
Wikidata Q203233

image.file: Lord Clive meeting with Mir Jafar after the Battle of Plassey.jpg

summary.en: Ahmad Shah Durrani’s Afghan army, with Rohilla and Awadh allies, crushed the Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau in one of the largest battles of the 18th century, halting Maratha expansion in the north.
summary.zh: 艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼的阿富汗军队联合罗赫拉人和奥德军队，击溃萨达希夫拉奥·鲍率领的马拉塔大军；这是18世纪规模最大的战役之一，遏止了马拉塔人向北扩张。

sources.title: T. S. Shejwalkar, Panipat 1761 (1946)
Stewart Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (New Cambridge History of India II.4, 1993)
Wikidata Q1259218

image.file: The Third battle of Panipat 13 January 1761.jpg

summary.en: Company troops under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II; the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) then gave the Company the revenue rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
summary.zh: 赫克托·芒罗率领的东印度公司军队击败米尔·卡西姆、奥德的舒贾·乌德·达乌拉与莫卧儿皇帝沙·阿拉姆二世的联军；1765年的《阿拉哈巴德条约》使公司获得孟加拉、比哈尔和奥里萨的财税权。

sources.title: P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (New Cambridge History of India II.2, 1987)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Buxar
Wikidata Q2355467

events.note: Standard histories date the battle 22–23 October 1764; Wikidata records 6 November 1764, which appears to be an error.

image.file: Battle of Buxar -Crown and company- Arthur Edward Mainwaring pg.144.jpg

name.en: Burmese–Siamese War and fall of Ayutthaya
name.zh: 缅暹战争与阿瑜陀耶陷落

summary.en: Konbaung Burma under Hsinbyushin invaded Siam on two fronts and, after a 14-month siege, sacked and burned Ayutthaya in April 1767, ending the 417-year-old kingdom. Taksin soon regrouped the Siamese at Thonburi.
summary.zh: 贡榜王朝孟驳王分两路入侵暹罗，经十四个月围城，于1767年4月攻陷并焚毁阿瑜陀耶，延续四百余年的王国就此灭亡。不久郑信在吞武里重整暹罗力量。

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Burmese–Siamese War (1765–1767)

summary.en: Four wars between the East India Company and Mysore under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, whose rocket corps and French ties made them the Company’s most formidable southern foe; they ended with Mysore reduced to a subsidiary state.
summary.zh: 东印度公司与海德尔·阿里和蒂普苏丹统治下的迈索尔之间的四次战争；迈索尔凭借火箭部队和与法国的联系，成为公司在南印度最强劲的对手，最终沦为附属国。

sources.title: Kate Brittlebank, Tipu Sultan’s Search for Legitimacy (1997)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mysore Wars
Wikidata Q617321

summary.en: The Qianlong Emperor's Complete Library of the Four Treasuries copied some 3,500 works into about 36,000 volumes, while the same review suppressed and destroyed thousands of books judged seditious.
summary.zh: 乾隆帝开四库全书馆，抄录典籍约三千五百种、三万六千余册；修书同时禁毁大量“违碍”书籍。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《四库全书总目》卷首 圣谕
Britannica: Siku quanshu

events.note: The first set was completed in 1782; Wikidata gives 1773–1783.

summary.en: King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, moved the capital across the Chao Phraya from Thonburi to Rattanakosin Island, setting the city pillar on 21 April 1782 and building the Grand Palace.
summary.zh: 却克里王朝开国君主拉玛一世将都城从吞武里迁至湄南河对岸的拉达那哥欣岛，于1782年4月21日立城柱，并修建大皇宫。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Rattanakosin Island

summary.en: Fiscal crisis and Enlightenment ideas led the Estates-General of 1789 to transform itself into a National Assembly; the storming of the Bastille on 14 July became the Revolution's symbol. It abolished feudal privilege and the monarchy, proclaimed the Rights of Man, and ended with Napoleon Bonaparte's coup in 1799.
summary.zh: 财政危机与启蒙思想促使1789年的三级会议转变为国民议会，7月14日攻占巴士底狱成为革命的象征。大革命废除了封建特权和君主制，发表《人权宣言》，最终以1799年拿破仑·波拿巴发动政变告终。

sources.title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (1789)
William Doyle, The Oxford History of the French Revolution (1989)
Britannica: French Revolution

events.note: Coordinates are those of the Bastille (Wikidata Q6539).

image.artist: Isidore Stanislas Helman / After Charles Monnet

summary.en: Nguyễn Huệ of the Tây Sơn, newly proclaimed Emperor Quang Trung, made a lightning march north during Tết and routed the Qing army that had occupied Thăng Long to restore the Lê, ending Qing intervention.
summary.zh: 西山朝阮惠刚称帝号光中，便于春节期间率军急行北上，击溃为扶持黎朝而占据升龙的清军，结束了清朝的干预。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Battle of Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa

events.note: Wikidata gives 1788 (the Vietnamese lunar year Mậu Thân); the decisive fighting took place on 28–30 January 1789.

image.artist: A collaboration between Chinese and European painters. The Jesuit missionaries involved in producing the drawings in Chi

summary.en: Britain's first embassy to China, led by George Macartney, was received by the Qianlong Emperor at the Chengde summer palace, but its requests for trade concessions and a permanent embassy were refused.
summary.zh: 英国首个访华使团由马戛尔尼率领，于承德避暑山庄觐见乾隆帝，其通商与驻使要求均遭拒绝。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: George Macartney
《清高宗实录》乾隆五十八年八月

summary.en: British and Hyderabad troops stormed Tipu Sultan’s island capital; Tipu was killed defending a breach, and the Company restored the Wodeyar dynasty over a reduced Mysore.
summary.zh: 英军与海得拉巴军队攻陷蒂普苏丹的河洲都城；蒂普在城墙缺口处战死，公司随后在缩小了的迈索尔恢复沃迪亚尔王朝。

sources.title: Kate Brittlebank, Tipu Sultan’s Search for Legitimacy (1997)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tippu Sultan
Wikidata Q815204

summary.en: Napoleon crossed the Niemen with some 450,000 men of the Grande Armée, won a costly victory at Borodino and entered a burning Moscow in September. Without a Russian surrender, the retreat through winter, hunger and Cossack attacks destroyed most of his army.
summary.zh: 拿破仑率领约45万人的大军渡过涅曼河，在博罗季诺付出惨重代价取胜，9月进入陷于大火的莫斯科。俄国拒不求和，大军在严寒、饥饿与哥萨克袭扰中撤退，几乎全军覆没。

label.zh: 小雅罗斯拉韦茨战役，开始撤退

sources.title: Adam Zamoyski, 1812: Napoleon's Fatal March on Moscow (2004)
Dominic Lieven, Russia Against Napoleon (2009)
Britannica: Napoleon I

events.note: Estimates of the invading force range from about 450,000 to over 600,000 including reinforcements. Event placed at Borodino.

summary.en: Diplomats of the great powers, led by Metternich, Castlereagh, Alexander I and Talleyrand, redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon's defeat. The settlement, signed in June 1815, sought a balance of power and kept general peace among the great powers for decades.
summary.zh: 以梅特涅、卡斯尔雷、亚历山大一世和塔列朗为代表的列强外交官，在拿破仑战败后重新划定欧洲版图。1815年6月签署的最后议定书追求均势，使列强之间维持了数十年的大体和平。

sources.title: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815)
Britannica: Congress of Vienna

summary.en: An Anglo-allied army under the Duke of Wellington and a Prussian army under Blücher defeated Napoleon south of Brussels. The defeat ended his Hundred Days' return to power; he abdicated again and was exiled to Saint Helena.
summary.zh: 威灵顿公爵统率的英国及其盟军与布吕歇尔统率的普鲁士军队在布鲁塞尔以南击败拿破仑。此役终结了他重掌政权的“百日王朝”，拿破仑再度退位并被流放至圣赫勒拿岛。

sources.title: Andrew Roberts, Waterloo: Napoleon's Last Gamble (2005)
Britannica: Battle of Waterloo

summary.en: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history devastated Sumbawa, killing tens of thousands directly and through famine. Its aerosols cooled the northern hemisphere, causing the "Year Without a Summer" of 1816.
summary.zh: 有记录以来规模最大的火山喷发摧毁了松巴哇岛，直接或因饥荒死亡者数以万计。喷发的气溶胶使北半球降温，导致1816年出现“无夏之年”。

sources.title: Clive Oppenheimer, "Climatic, environmental and human consequences of the largest known historic eruption: Tambora volcano (Indonesia) 1815", Progress in Physical Geography 27:2 (2003)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora

summary.en: Prince Diponegoro of Yogyakarta led a widespread rebellion against Dutch colonial rule and its Javanese allies. The war cost some 200,000 Javanese lives before Diponegoro was seized at negotiations and exiled.
summary.zh: 日惹王子蒂博尼哥罗领导了一场反抗荷兰殖民统治及其爪哇盟友的大规模起义。战争造成约二十万爪哇人死亡，最终蒂博尼哥罗在谈判中被扣押并流放。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Java War
Peter Carey, The Power of Prophecy: Prince Dipanagara and the End of an Old Order in Java, 1785–1855 (KITLV, 2007)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Java War

image.file: Nicolaas Pieneman - The Submission of Prince Dipo Negoro to General De Kock.jpg

summary.en: Ending the Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828, Qajar Iran ceded the khanates of Erivan and Nakhchivan to Russia, paid a heavy indemnity and granted Russian subjects extraterritorial rights. It fixed the Aras River frontier and marked Iran's loss of the South Caucasus.
summary.zh: 条约结束了1826—1828年俄波战争。卡扎尔伊朗将埃里温和纳希切万两汗国割让给俄国，支付巨额赔款，并给予俄国臣民治外法权。条约确定以阿拉斯河为界，标志伊朗丧失南高加索。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Treaty of Turkmenchay
F. Kazemzadeh, "Iranian relations with Russia and the Soviet Union, to 1921", Cambridge History of Iran, vol. 7 (1991)
Wikipedia: Treaty of Turkmenchay

events.note: Signed 10 February 1828 (Julian; 22 February Gregorian); only the year is given.

summary.en: Imperial commissioner Lin Zexu confiscated over 20,000 chests of British opium in Canton and destroyed it on the beach at Humen over 23 days, a confrontation that led directly to the First Opium War.
summary.zh: 钦差大臣林则徐收缴英商鸦片两万余箱，于虎门海滩历时二十三天当众销毁，直接引发第一次鸦片战争。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷369 林则徐传

summary.en: Britain sent an expeditionary force after the opium seizures; steam warships blockaded the coast, took Zhoushan, Xiamen and Zhenjiang and threatened Nanjing, forcing the Qing to sue for peace.
summary.zh: 英国以禁烟为由派远征军来华，封锁沿海，攻占定海、厦门、镇江，兵临南京，清廷被迫求和。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Opium Wars
《筹办夷务始末》道光朝

summary.en: A wave of liberal and national uprisings spread from Palermo and Paris to Vienna, Berlin, Budapest and Milan. Most were suppressed by 1849, but serfdom was abolished in the Austrian lands and the revolutions shaped later national movements.

summary.en: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, published in London by John Murray, argued that species evolve over generations through natural selection. The book transformed biology and provoked wide religious and philosophical debate.

summary.en: Led by Piedmont-Sardinia's prime minister Cavour and the volunteer campaigns of Giuseppe Garibaldi, most Italian states were united and the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in Turin in 1861 under Victor Emmanuel II. Venetia joined in 1866, and Rome, taken in 1870, became the capital in 1871.

summary.en: The Allies tried to force the Dardanelles and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. After naval attacks failed, British, ANZAC and French landings on the Gallipoli peninsula were contained by Ottoman defenders, among them Mustafa Kemal, and evacuated in January 1916.
summary.zh: 协约国企图强行打通达达尼尔海峡，迫使奥斯曼帝国退出战争。海军进攻失败后，英国、澳新军团和法国部队在加里波利半岛登陆，但被包括穆斯塔法·凯末尔在内的奥斯曼守军遏制，最终于1916年1月撤离。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Gallipoli
P. Hart, Gallipoli (2011)
Wikipedia: Gallipoli campaign

summary.en: In a secret agreement, British and French diplomats Mark Sykes and François Georges-Picot, with Russian assent, divided the Ottoman Arab provinces into zones of influence. It shaped the post-war mandates and is widely remembered in the region as a symbol of imperial partition.
summary.zh: 英法外交官马克·赛克斯和弗朗索瓦·乔治-皮科在俄国同意下秘密划分奥斯曼帝国阿拉伯诸省的势力范围。协定影响了战后的委任统治格局，在当地被普遍视为帝国主义瓜分的象征。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sykes-Picot Agreement
J. Barr, A Line in the Sand (2011)
Wikipedia: Sykes–Picot Agreement

events.note: Negotiated in London; plotted at Damascus, at the heart of the territories it divided.

summary.en: Sharif Husayn ibn Ali of Mecca, encouraged by Britain, launched a revolt against Ottoman rule in the Hejaz. Arab forces led by his son Faisal, aided by British officers including T. E. Lawrence, advanced north via Aqaba and entered Damascus in October 1918.
summary.zh: 麦加谢里夫侯赛因·本·阿里在英国鼓动下于汉志发动反抗奥斯曼统治的起义。其子费萨尔率领的阿拉伯部队在T. E. 劳伦斯等英国军官协助下经亚喀巴北上，1918年10月进入大马士革。

sources.title: E. Rogan, The Fall of the Ottomans (2015)
T. E. Lawrence, Seven Pillars of Wisdom (1926)
Wikipedia: Arab Revolt

summary.en: The Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin overthrew Russia's Provisional Government in Petrograd, seizing the Winter Palace. Their seizure of power led to civil war and to the founding of the Soviet Union in 1922.
summary.zh: 列宁领导的布尔什维克在彼得格勒推翻俄国临时政府，攻占冬宫。这次夺权引发了内战，并导致1922年苏联的建立。

sources.title: John Reed, Ten Days That Shook the World (1919)
Orlando Figes, A People's Tragedy: The Russian Revolution 1891–1924 (1996)
Britannica: Russian Revolution

events.note: Wikidata gives 25 October 1917, the Julian date then used in Russia; 7 November is the Gregorian equivalent. Coordinates: Winter Palace.

image.file: After the capture of the Winter Palace 26 October 1917.jpg

summary.en: Beijing students protested the Paris Peace Conference decision to give Germany's Shandong concessions to Japan; the demonstrations grew into a nationwide movement for science, democracy and vernacular culture.
summary.zh: 北京学生抗议巴黎和会将德国在山东权益转让日本，示威扩展为全国运动，推动了以科学、民主与白话文为旗帜的新文化运动。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Signed in the Hall of Mirrors five years to the day after the Sarajevo assassination, the treaty ended the war between Germany and the Allies. Germany lost territory and colonies and accepted limits on its armed forces and liability for reparations; the treaty also created the League of Nations.
summary.zh: 和约在萨拉热窝事件整整五年后于凡尔赛宫镜厅签署，结束了德国与协约国之间的战争。德国丧失领土和殖民地，接受军备限制并承担赔款责任；和约还创建了国际联盟。

sources.title: Margaret MacMillan, Peacemakers: The Paris Conference of 1919 and Its Attempt to End War (2001)
Britannica: Treaty of Versailles

summary.en: A Declaration of Independence was read in Seoul on 1 March 1919, sparking nationwide peaceful demonstrations against Japanese rule. Their violent suppression killed thousands, but the movement led to the Korean Provisional Government in Shanghai.
summary.zh: 1919年3月1日，《独立宣言》在汉城宣读，引发全国性反对日本统治的和平示威。运动遭血腥镇压，数千人遇难，但随后促成了上海大韩民国临时政府的成立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: March First Movement
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)

name.zh: 阿姆利则惨案（扎连瓦拉园惨案）

summary.en: Troops under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired without warning on a crowd in an enclosed garden at Amritsar, killing hundreds (379 by the official count, many more by Indian estimates); it turned many moderates against British rule.
summary.zh: 戴尔准将率部在阿姆利则一处封闭园地内不加警告地向人群开枪，造成数百人死亡（官方统计379人，印方估计远多于此），使许多温和派转而反对英国统治。

sources.title: Kim A. Wagner, Amritsar 1919: An Empire of Fear and the Making of a Massacre (2019)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre

name.en: First National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party

summary.en: Thirteen delegates, including Mao Zedong, met secretly in Shanghai's French Concession, finishing on a boat on South Lake in Jiaxing, to found the Chinese Communist Party.
summary.zh: 包括毛泽东在内的十三名代表在上海法租界秘密集会，后转至嘉兴南湖游船上闭幕，宣告中国共产党成立。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

wiki.zh: 中国共产党第一次全国代表大会

summary.en: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake beneath Sagami Bay struck at midday, and the fires that followed destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama. More than 100,000 people died, and in the chaos vigilantes massacred thousands of Koreans.
summary.zh: 一场约7.9级地震在相模湾下方于正午发生，随后的大火焚毁了东京和横滨的大部分地区，死亡逾十万人。混乱中，自警团屠杀了数千名朝鲜人。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Great Kantō earthquake

Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Great Kantō Earthquake

name.en: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

summary.en: After victory in the War of Independence and the Treaty of Lausanne, the Grand National Assembly in Ankara proclaimed the Republic of Turkey, with Mustafa Kemal (Atatürk) as its first president. The caliphate was abolished in 1924 and sweeping secularising reforms followed.
summary.zh: 独立战争胜利和《洛桑条约》签订后，安卡拉的大国民议会宣布成立土耳其共和国，穆斯塔法·凯末尔（阿塔图尔克）任首任总统。1924年哈里发制度被废除，此后推行了全面的世俗化改革。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Turkey
E.-J. Zürcher, Turkey: A Modern History (4th ed., 2017)
Wikipedia: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

summary.en: The Nationalist army under Chiang Kai-shek marched north from Guangzhou, defeating the Beiyang warlords; after the 1927 split with the Communists it took Beijing in 1928, and Zhang Xueliang's Manchuria joined the Nanjing government.
summary.zh: 蒋介石率国民革命军自广州誓师北伐，击败北洋军阀；1927年国共分裂，1928年克北京，张学良东北易帜，南京国民政府形式上统一全国。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Northern Expedition

summary.en: Gandhi and 78 followers walked about 390 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax; the march launched nationwide civil disobedience and drew world attention.
summary.zh: 甘地与78名追随者从萨巴尔马蒂修道院步行约390公里至丹迪海边自行制盐，以抗议英国的盐税；此举掀起全国性的不合作运动，引起世界关注。

label.zh: 萨巴尔马蒂修道院（3月12日）

summary.en: Japanese officers of the Kwantung Army blew up a section of railway near Mukden (Shenyang) and blamed Chinese troops, using it as pretext to occupy all of Manchuria within months.
summary.zh: 日本关东军炸毁沈阳柳条湖附近铁路并嫁祸中国军队，借机数月内侵占东北全境。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Mukden Incident

summary.en: The People's Party, a group of military officers and civilian officials, staged a bloodless coup in Bangkok that ended absolute monarchy and gave Siam its first constitution under King Prajadhipok.
summary.zh: 由军官与文官组成的民党在曼谷发动不流血政变，结束了君主专制，在巴差提勃国王治下颁布暹罗第一部宪法。

summary.en: Abdulaziz ibn Saud, who had retaken Riyadh in 1902 and conquered the Hejaz in 1924–25, united his domains as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The discovery of commercial oil in 1938 later turned it into a leading petroleum producer.
summary.zh: 1902年收复利雅得、1924—1925年征服汉志的阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·伊本·沙特，将其领地合并为沙特阿拉伯王国。1938年发现商业石油后，王国逐渐成为主要产油国。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Saudi Arabia

summary.en: Encircled in Jiangxi, the Red Army broke out and marched roughly 10,000 km through the southwest and northwest to Shaanxi. At the Zunyi Conference of January 1935 Mao Zedong gained leadership of the army.
summary.zh: 红军突破江西根据地包围，转战西南、西北约二万五千里抵达陕北；1935年1月遵义会议确立了毛泽东的领导地位。

summary.zh: 张学良、杨虎城在西安扣押蒋介石，逼其停止“剿共”、联共抗日，促成第二次国共合作。

summary.en: A clash between Japanese and Chinese troops at the Lugou (Marco Polo) Bridge near Wanping, southwest of Beiping, escalated into the full-scale Second Sino-Japanese War.
summary.zh: 日军在北平西南宛平城、卢沟桥一带向中国守军开火，中国军队奋起抵抗，全面抗日战争爆发。

name.zh: 第二次世界大战（欧洲战场）

summary.en: Germany's invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 began a war that by 1941 pitted the Axis against Britain, the Soviet Union and the United States. In Europe it ended with Germany's unconditional surrender in May 1945, after tens of millions of deaths, including some six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust.
summary.zh: 1939年9月1日德国入侵波兰，战争爆发；至1941年，轴心国已与英国、苏联和美国全面交战。欧洲战事以1945年5月德国无条件投降告终，战争造成数千万人死亡，其中包括在大屠杀中遇害的约六百万犹太人。

summary.en: At its Lahore session the All-India Muslim League under Jinnah demanded independent states for the Muslim-majority regions of north-western and eastern India—the founding demand of the Pakistan movement.
summary.zh: 全印穆斯林联盟在真纳领导下于拉合尔年会上要求在印度西北部和东部穆斯林占多数的地区建立独立国家，这成为巴基斯坦运动的纲领性诉求。

summary.en: Germany and its allies invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941 in Operation Barbarossa, opening the largest land war in history. After defeats at Moscow, Stalingrad and Kursk, the Red Army drove west and took Berlin in May 1945; Soviet deaths reached roughly 27 million.
summary.zh: 1941年6月22日，德国及其盟国发动“巴巴罗萨行动”入侵苏联，开启了史上规模最大的陆地战争。德军在莫斯科、斯大林格勒和库尔斯克相继失利后，红军一路西进，于1945年5月攻克柏林；苏联死亡人数约达2700万。

summary.en: German and Axis forces fought to take Stalingrad on the Volga in months of street fighting. A Soviet counter-offensive in November 1942 encircled the German Sixth Army, which surrendered in February 1943—a turning point of the war in Europe.
summary.zh: 德国及轴心国军队为夺取伏尔加河畔的斯大林格勒，展开了长达数月的巷战。1942年11月苏军发动反攻，包围德军第六集团军，后者于1943年2月投降，此役成为欧洲战场的转折点。

summary.en: On D-Day, American, British, Canadian and other Allied forces landed on five beaches in Normandy in the largest seaborne invasion in history. The landings opened a western front that, together with the Soviet advance in the east, led to Germany's defeat.
summary.zh: D日当天，美、英、加等盟军在诺曼底五处海滩登陆，这是史上规模最大的海上登陆作战。登陆开辟了西线战场，与东线苏军的推进一道导致德国战败。

summary.en: After Japan's surrender, the Japanese governor-general formally surrendered Taiwan and Penghu to the Republic of China in Taipei on 25 October 1945, ending fifty years of Japanese colonial rule.
summary.zh: 日本投降后，1945年10月25日台湾总督在台北向中华民国政府代表投降，结束日本五十年殖民统治。

summary.en: The US B-29 Enola Gay dropped the uranium bomb "Little Boy" on Hiroshima, the first use of a nuclear weapon in war. Around 70,000–80,000 people died instantly and many more by the end of 1945.
summary.zh: 美国B-29轰炸机“艾诺拉·盖”号在广岛投下铀弹“小男孩”，这是核武器首次用于战争。约七万至八万人当场死亡，至1945年底死亡人数大幅增加。

summary.en: Three days after Hiroshima, the plutonium bomb "Fat Man" exploded over the Urakami district of Nagasaki, killing some 40,000 people immediately. Japan announced its surrender on 15 August.
summary.zh: 广岛原爆三天后，钚弹“胖子”在长崎浦上地区上空爆炸，约四万人当场死亡。8月15日日本宣布投降。

summary.en: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta read a brief proclamation of independence at Sukarno's house in Jakarta. Four years of war and diplomacy followed before the Netherlands transferred sovereignty in 1949.
summary.zh: 日本投降两天后，苏加诺与穆罕默德·哈达在雅加达苏加诺寓所宣读简短的独立宣言。此后经过四年的战争与外交斗争，荷兰才于1949年移交主权。

summary.en: At Ba Đình Square in Hanoi, Hồ Chí Minh proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the August Revolution, quoting the US Declaration of Independence. France's return to Indochina led to war the following year.
summary.zh: 八月革命后，胡志明在河内巴亭广场宣布越南民主共和国成立，并引用了美国《独立宣言》的语句。法国重返印度支那，次年爆发战争。

summary.en: British India was divided into the dominions of India and Pakistan at midnight on 14–15 August 1947; the partition of Punjab and Bengal brought communal massacres and displaced roughly 12–15 million people.
summary.zh: 1947年8月14日至15日午夜，英属印度分为印度和巴基斯坦两个自治领；旁遮普和孟加拉的分割引发教派屠杀，约1200万至1500万人流离失所。

name.en: Discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls

summary.en: Bedouin shepherds found ancient manuscripts in a cave near Qumran by the Dead Sea; by 1956 eleven caves had yielded fragments of hundreds of scrolls. Dating from about the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE, they include the oldest known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible.
summary.zh: 贝都因牧人在死海岸边库姆兰附近的山洞中发现古代手稿；到1956年，十一个洞穴共出土数百部古卷的残片。这些文献约成于公元前3世纪至公元1世纪，包括已知最古老的希伯来圣经抄本。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dead Sea Scrolls

summary.en: Centred on Xuzhou, the largest of the three great campaigns of the Chinese Civil War destroyed the main Nationalist field armies north of the Yangtze, after the Liaoshen campaign and alongside the Pingjin campaign.
summary.zh: 以徐州为中心，是解放战争三大战役中规模最大的一役，与辽沈、平津战役一起歼灭了国民党军主力。

summary.en: Ceylon became an independent dominion within the Commonwealth under Prime Minister D. S. Senanayake; it became the Republic of Sri Lanka in 1972.
summary.zh: 锡兰在总理森那那亚克领导下成为英联邦内的独立自治领，1972年改为斯里兰卡共和国。

name.en: Declaration of the State of Israel

summary.en: As the British Mandate ended, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the State of Israel in Tel Aviv. Neighbouring Arab states intervened the next day; during the 1947–1949 war more than 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled, an event Palestinians call the Nakba ("catastrophe").
summary.zh: 英国委任统治结束之际，戴维·本-古里安在特拉维夫宣布以色列建国。次日周边阿拉伯国家出兵；在1947—1949年战争中，七十多万巴勒斯坦人逃离或被驱逐，巴勒斯坦人称之为“纳克巴”（浩劫）。

summary.zh: 珠江口大港，自汉代即为海上贸易门户；南汉都城，1757年后为“一口通商”口岸，孙中山在此建立革命政权。

summary.zh: 运河与长江交汇的名城，隋炀帝三下江都，唐代“扬一益二”最为富庶；鉴真自此东渡日本。

summary.en: Confluence of the Han and Yangtze, where the Wu fortress of Xiakou grew into the Tang–Song Ezhou and Ming–Qing Wuchang; the Wuchang Uprising of 1911 began the Xinhai Revolution.
summary.zh: 汉水入江处，孙吴筑夏口城，唐宋为鄂州，元明清称武昌；1911年武昌起义揭开辛亥革命序幕。

summary.en: Oasis at the western end of the Hexi Corridor where the Silk Road forked; the Mogao Caves preserve a millennium of Buddhist art, and the library cave yielded tens of thousands of manuscripts.
summary.zh: 河西走廊西端绿洲，丝绸之路分道之处；莫高窟保存千年佛教艺术，藏经洞出土数万件写本。

summary.zh: 塔里木盆地西缘的绿洲，丝路南北道交汇于此；班超以疏勒为据点，喀喇汗王朝时为突厥伊斯兰文化中心。

summary.zh: 松赞干布建都于此，有大昭寺与唐蕃会盟碑；后为达赖喇嘛甘丹颇章政权所在地，布达拉宫屹立其上。

summary.zh: 近拓跋代国旧都盛乐，1572年俺答汗筑库库和屯（青城），明赐名归化；清筑绥远城，二城合为归绥，今为内蒙古首府。

summary.en: Nurhaci moved his Later Jin capital here in 1625; as Mukden (Shengjing) it was the Qing capital until 1644 and kept its palace. The 1931 railway sabotage nearby launched Japan's occupation of Manchuria.
summary.zh: 1625年努尔哈赤迁都沈阳，皇太极改称盛京，为清入关前都城并存故宫；1931年九一八事变发生于城北柳条湖。

summary.zh: 北魏都城平城，城西开凿云冈石窟；辽金为西京大同府，明代为九边重镇。

summary.zh: 古称晋阳，北齐别都，李渊太原起兵建唐，唐为北都；北汉都城，979年宋灭北汉毁晋阳旧城，另筑新城。

summary.zh: 春秋吴国故都，隋开皇九年改名苏州，运河名城，以丝绸与园林著称；元末张士诚据此，1367年为朱元璋所破。

summary.zh: 福建港口，阿拉伯与欧洲旅人称之“刺桐”；1087年设市舶司后，宋元时期与亚历山大港并称世界大港。

summary.zh: 滇池之滨，南诏筑拓东城，大理称鄯阐府；元设云南行省于中庆，明清为云南府，1662年南明永历帝殒命于此。

summary.zh: 汉武帝开河西置武威郡，古称姑臧、凉州，前凉、后凉、北凉建都于此；1247年萨迦班智达与阔端在此会盟。

summary.en: Fortress on the Han River guarding the route between the Yangtze and the north; Zhuge Liang lived at nearby Longzhong, and the six-year Mongol siege that ended in 1273 opened the way to the Song heartland.
summary.zh: 汉水重镇，扼南北要冲；诸葛亮隐居城西隆中，宋元襄樊之战历时六年，1273年襄阳陷落，南宋门户洞开。

summary.en: River port at the Jialing–Yangtze confluence, known as Jiangzhou and Yuzhou, named Chongqing ("double celebration") in 1189; capital of Ming Xia and the Nationalist wartime capital during the war with Japan.
summary.zh: 嘉陵江与长江交汇处，古称江州、渝州，1189年宋光宗以“双重喜庆”升为重庆府；明夏都城，抗战时为国民政府陪都。

summary.en: A fishing village where Ōta Dōkan built Edo Castle in 1457, Edo became the seat of the Tokugawa shoguns in 1603 and one of the world's largest cities. Renamed Tokyo ("eastern capital") in 1868, it became the imperial capital.
summary.zh: 原为渔村，1457年太田道灌在此修筑江户城。1603年起成为德川将军的驻地，并发展为世界最大城市之一。1868年改称东京（“东方之京”），成为天皇所在的首都。

summary.en: Founded by Emperor Kanmu in 794 as Heian-kyō on the model of Chang'an, Kyoto was the seat of the imperial court for over a thousand years and the centre of Japanese aristocratic and religious culture until the emperor moved to Tokyo.
summary.zh: 794年桓武天皇仿照长安建立平安京。此后一千多年里，京都一直是天皇朝廷所在地和日本贵族与宗教文化的中心，直至天皇移居东京。

summary.en: The Han River basin held Baekje's first capital and was fought over by the Three Kingdoms. Joseon made Hanseong its capital in 1394; under Japanese rule it was Keijō, and since 1945 it has been Seoul, capital of South Korea.
summary.zh: 汉江流域曾是百济最早的都城所在，并为三国反复争夺。1394年朝鲜王朝定都汉城；日本殖民时期称京城，1945年后称首尔（汉语旧称汉城），为韩国首都。

summary.en: Capital of Silla for nearly a thousand years, Seorabeol was renamed Gyeongju by Goryeo after Silla's surrender in 935. Its royal tombs, temples and observatory make it an open-air museum of Silla culture.
summary.zh: 徐罗伐作为新罗都城近千年，935年新罗归降后被高丽改名为庆州。城内王陵、寺院与瞻星台使其成为新罗文化的露天博物馆。

summary.zh: 313年以前为中国乐浪郡治所，427年成为高句丽都城。高丽时期称西京，1948年起为朝鲜民主主义人民共和国首都。

summary.en: Japan's first long-lasting capital, Heijō-kyō, was laid out here in 710. After the court left in 784, its great temples—Tōdai-ji, Kōfuku-ji, Kasuga shrine—kept Nara alive as the "southern capital" of Buddhism.
summary.zh: 日本第一座长期使用的都城平城京于710年在此兴建。784年朝廷迁离后，东大寺、兴福寺、春日大社等寺社使奈良作为佛教的“南都”延续繁荣。

summary.en: Wang Geon's home town of Songak became Gaegyeong, capital of Goryeo, for almost five centuries. Lying just south of the 38th parallel, it passed to North Korean control in the Korean War.
summary.zh: 王建的故乡松岳后来成为高丽都城开京，历时近五百年。开城位于三八线以南不远，在朝鲜战争中转归朝鲜控制。

summary.en: As Naniwa it was a port and intermittent capital from the 7th century. Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle on the site of the Ishiyama Hongan-ji, and under the Tokugawa the city became Japan's commercial "kitchen".
summary.zh: 古称难波，自7世纪起即为港口，并几度成为都城。丰臣秀吉在石山本愿寺旧址修建大坂城；德川时代这里发展为日本的商业中心，号称“天下的厨房”。

summary.en: Minamoto no Yoritomo chose this coastal town, protected by hills, as his headquarters in 1180. It was Japan's political centre until the shogunate fell in 1333 and is known for the Great Buddha and Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine.
summary.zh: 1180年源赖朝选择这座三面环山、一面临海的小城作为大本营。直到1333年幕府灭亡，这里一直是日本的政治中心，以镰仓大佛和鹤冈八幡宫闻名。

summary.en: Seven islands ceded by Gujarat to Portugal in 1534 passed to England as part of Catherine of Braganza’s dowry in 1661. Reclaimed and joined, they grew into Bombay, India’s great port and financial capital, officially renamed Mumbai in 1995.
summary.zh: 这七个岛屿于1534年由古吉拉特割让给葡萄牙，1661年作为凯瑟琳公主的嫁妆转归英国。经填海连成一体后发展为孟买，成为印度最大的港口和金融中心，1995年正式更名为Mumbai。

summary.en: The East India Company acquired a coastal strip from a Vijayanagara nayaka in 1639 and built Fort St George, around which Madras grew as capital of the Madras Presidency. The city was renamed Chennai, after the neighbouring town of Chennapatnam, in 1996.
summary.zh: 东印度公司于1639年从毗奢耶那伽罗属下的纳亚克手中取得一段海岸并修建圣乔治堡，马德拉斯围绕该堡发展为马德拉斯管区首府。1996年依邻近的金奈帕特南之名改称金奈。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chennai
S. Muthiah, Madras Rediscovered (2004)
Wikidata Q1352

name.zh: 加尔各答（卡利卡塔、苏塔努蒂、戈宾德布尔）

polity.en: East India Company (capital of British India)
polity.zh: 东印度公司（英属印度首府）

summary.en: Job Charnock’s East India Company post of 1690 on the Hooghly absorbed three villages and became Calcutta, capital of British India until 1911 and centre of the Bengal Renaissance. Its Bengali name Kolkata became official in 2001.
summary.zh: 1690年约伯·查诺克在胡格利河畔设立东印度公司商站，合并三个村落形成加尔各答；该城至1911年一直是英属印度首府，也是孟加拉文艺复兴的中心。2001年正式采用孟加拉语名称Kolkata。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kolkata
P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (1987)
Wikidata Q1348

polity.zh: 托马拉王朝与乔汉王朝

summary.en: Traditionally identified with the epic Indraprastha, Delhi has been rebuilt as a succession of cities: Tomara Dhillika, the sultanate capitals, Shah Jahan’s Shahjahanabad and Lutyens’s New Delhi, capital of British India from 1911 and of the Republic of India.
summary.zh: 德里传统上被认为即史诗中的因陀罗普拉斯塔，历史上曾多次重建为不同城市：托马拉王朝的迪利卡、苏丹国诸都城、沙贾汗的沙贾汉纳巴德以及勒琴斯设计的新德里；1911年起为英属印度首都，后为印度共和国首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Delhi
Narayani Gupta, Delhi Between Two Empires 1803–1931 (1981)
Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Wikidata Q1353

places.note: The Tomara founding (traditionally 736) is uncertain; Indraprastha is legendary and is not given a date range. Shahjahanabad was built 1639–1648.

polity.en: Pala Empire and later Bihar rulers
polity.zh: 波罗王朝及其后比哈尔诸政权
苏尔王朝，后为莫卧儿帝国
莫卧儿帝国／孟加拉纳瓦卜

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Pataliputra on the Ganges was the capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires and the city where Aryabhata worked. Lying in ruins by Xuanzang’s visit, it was refounded as Patna by Sher Shah Suri in 1541 and is now capital of Bihar.
summary.zh: 恒河畔的华氏城曾是孔雀王朝和笈多王朝的都城，阿耶波多亦在此著述。玄奘到访时已成废墟，1541年舍尔沙·苏尔在此重建巴特那，今为比哈尔邦首府。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Patna
Wikidata Q80484

places.note: Polity labels before 320 and for 550–1541 are simplified; the Azimabad name (after prince Azim-us-Shan) was used alongside Patna.

polity.zh: 杜兰尼帝国／锡克米斯尔

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Capital of the later Ghaznavids, a Mughal imperial city adorned with the fort and Badshahi Mosque, and seat of Ranjit Singh’s Sikh Empire, Lahore became the capital of Punjab under the British and is Pakistan’s second-largest city.
summary.zh: 拉合尔曾是后期伽色尼王朝的都城、莫卧儿帝国的重要城市（建有拉合尔堡和巴德沙希清真寺），又为兰吉特·辛格锡克帝国的都城；英治时期为旁遮普首府，今为巴基斯坦第二大城市。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Lahore
Anna Suvorova, Lahore: Topophilia of Space and Place (2011)
Wikidata Q11739

image.file: Eye Of Lahore (Minar e Pakistan) evening.jpg

name.zh: 伊拉哈巴斯／阿拉哈巴德

summary.en: Prayaga, at the sacred confluence of the Ganges and Yamuna, hosted Harsha’s alms-giving assemblies and the Kumbh Mela. Akbar built a fort here and named it Ilahabas (1575), later Allahabad; the old name Prayagraj was restored in 2018.
summary.zh: 钵逻耶伽位于恒河与亚穆纳河的神圣交汇处，戒日王曾在此举行布施大会，也是大壶节举办地。阿克巴于1575年在此筑堡并命名为伊拉哈巴斯，后称阿拉哈巴德；2018年恢复古名普拉亚格拉杰。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Prayagraj
Abu'l-Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari (tr. H. S. Jarrett), Subah of Ilahabad
Wikidata Q162442

places.note: Akbar’s foundation is dated 1575 in most accounts, 1583 in some.

polity.en: Ghurids, then Delhi Sultanate and Jaunpur
polity.zh: 古尔王朝，后为德里苏丹国与焦恩布尔

summary.en: One of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, Kashi on the Ganges is Hinduism’s holiest city and lies near Sarnath, where the Buddha first preached. Known to the British as Benares, it officially became Varanasi in 1956.
summary.zh: 迦尸位于恒河畔，是世界上最古老的持续有人居住的城市之一，也是印度教最神圣的城市，邻近佛陀初转法轮的鹿野苑。英国人称之为贝拿勒斯，1956年正式定名瓦拉纳西。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Varanasi
Diana L. Eck, Banaras: City of Light (1982)
Wikidata Q79980

places.note: Early polity labels omitted; date of the Benares State’s founding (1737) follows conventional accounts.

image.file: Varanasi, India, Varanasi skyline in the evening.jpg

summary.en: A harbour known to Arab traders (Ibn Battuta called it Kalanpu in 1344), Colombo was fortified by the Portuguese, made the Dutch and then British capital of Ceylon, and remains Sri Lanka’s commercial capital beside the administrative capital Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
summary.zh: 科伦坡早为阿拉伯商人所知（伊本·白图泰1344年称之为卡兰普），后由葡萄牙人筑城，相继成为荷兰与英国统治下锡兰的首府；今为斯里兰卡的商业首都，行政首都为毗邻的斯里贾亚瓦德纳普拉科特。

sources.title: K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (1981)
Ibn Battuta, Rihla (tr. H. A. R. Gibb)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Colombo
Wikidata Q35381

places.note: The first name range starts at Ibn Battuta’s mention; the port is older.

polity.zh: 莫卧儿帝国（孟加拉省首府）

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Made the Mughal capital of Bengal by Islam Khan in 1610 and named Jahangirnagar after the emperor, Dhaka was famed for its muslin. It was capital of East Bengal and East Pakistan and, since 1971, of Bangladesh; the spelling Dhaka replaced Dacca in 1982.
summary.zh: 1610年伊斯兰汗将达卡定为莫卧儿孟加拉省首府，并以皇帝之名称为贾汉吉尔纳加尔，此地以细棉布闻名。后为东孟加拉和东巴基斯坦首府，1971年起为孟加拉国首都；1982年拼写由Dacca改为Dhaka。

sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier, 1204–1760 (1993)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dhaka
Wikidata Q1354

places.note: Dhaka is first securely attested in a mosque inscription of 1459; Islam Khan’s move is dated 1608 or 1610 in different sources.

summary.en: A Khmer port called Prey Nokor, settled by Vietnamese in the 17th century and organised as Gia Định in 1698. As Saigon it was the capital of French Cochinchina and of South Vietnam, and was renamed after Hồ Chí Minh in 1976.
summary.zh: 原为高棉港口波雷诺哥，17世纪越南移民迁入，1698年设嘉定府。以西贡之名先后作为法属交趾支那和南越的首府，1976年以胡志明之名命名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ho Chi Minh City
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Ho Chi Minh City

places.note: The start of Vietnamese settlement and the date of the Khmer name are approximate.

polity.zh: 唐安南都护府 / 地方自主政权
阮朝 / 法属印度支那

summary.en: On the Red River, the Tang citadel of Đại La became Thăng Long when the Lý made it their capital in 1010. Renamed Hà Nội in 1831, it was the capital of French Indochina and has been Vietnam's capital since 1945.
summary.zh: 红河畔的唐代大罗城于1010年被李朝定为都城，改名升龙。1831年改称河内，曾为法属印度支那首府，1945年起为越南首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hanoi
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long – Hanoi
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Hanoi

places.note: Hanoi was also capital of French Indochina from 1902.

polity.zh: 荷兰东印度公司 / 荷属东印度

summary.en: The pepper port of Sunda Kelapa was taken by Fatahillah in 1527 and renamed Jayakarta. The Dutch rebuilt it as Batavia in 1619; renamed Jakarta during the Japanese occupation, it became the capital of independent Indonesia.
summary.zh: 胡椒港口巽他格拉巴于1527年被法塔希拉攻占并改名查雅加达。1619年荷兰人在此重建巴达维亚；日本占领期间改称雅加达，后成为独立的印度尼西亚首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jakarta
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Jakarta

places.note: The start of Sunda Kelapa as a port is approximate; Wikidata dates the city's founding to 22 June 1527.

polity.zh: 孟族王国 / 东吁王朝

summary.en: A Mon town around the Shwedagon Pagoda, Dagon was renamed Yangon ("end of strife") by Alaungpaya in 1755. Under British rule Rangoon became the capital of Burma, which it remained until the government moved to Naypyidaw in 2005.
summary.zh: 大光原为瑞德宫大金塔周围的孟族城镇，1755年雍籍牙将其改名仰光（意为“战争终结”）。英国统治时期仰光成为缅甸首府，直至2005年政府迁往内比都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Yangon
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Yangon

places.note: Wikidata's founding date of 1035 is traditional; 1000 is used as an approximate start.

summary.en: A riverside customs and fort town on the Chao Phraya under Ayutthaya, it became the capital when Taksin settled at Thonburi in 1767 and Rama I founded the new royal city on the east bank in 1782.
summary.zh: 阿瑜陀耶时期湄南河畔的关卡与要塞小镇。1767年郑信定都吞武里，1782年拉玛一世在东岸建立新王城，曼谷由此成为都城。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Bangkok
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Bangkok

places.note: The date of the early settlement is approximate.

image.file: Temple of the Emerald of buddha or Wat Phra Kaew (cropped).jpg

summary.en: A fortified Muslim trading settlement on Manila Bay, Maynila was taken by Legazpi, who founded the Spanish city in 1571. It was the hub of the trans-Pacific galleon trade and has remained the Philippine capital.
summary.zh: 马尼拉湾畔设防的穆斯林贸易聚落，被黎牙实比攻取后于1571年建立西班牙城市。这里是跨太平洋大帆船贸易的枢纽，并一直是菲律宾的首都。

sources.title: Emma H. Blair & James A. Robertson (eds.), The Philippine Islands, 1493–1898, Vol. 3 (1903)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Manila

places.note: The pre-Hispanic polity's origins are not precisely dated.

summary.en: Founded by Parameswara around 1400, Malacca controlled the strait that bears its name and was the region's richest port. It passed to the Portuguese (1511), Dutch (1641) and British (1824), leaving a layered colonial townscape.
summary.zh: 马六甲约于1400年由拜里米苏拉建立，控制着以其命名的海峡，是区域最富庶的港口。此后相继归属葡萄牙（1511年）、荷兰（1641年）与英国（1824年），留下层叠的殖民城市风貌。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca City

places.note: British occupation 1795–1818 during the Napoleonic Wars is merged into the Dutch period.

summary.en: Named after the hill temple founded, by legend, by Lady Penh in 1372, the site at the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap became the Khmer capital after Angkor's abandonment and again under King Norodom in 1865.
summary.zh: 其名源于传说中奔夫人于1372年在山丘上建造的寺庙。此地位于湄公河与洞里萨河交汇处，吴哥被放弃后成为高棉都城，1865年诺罗敦国王再度定都于此。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Phnom Penh
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Phnom Penh

places.note: The 1372 founding and Ponhea Yat's capital dates are traditional.

summary.en: Yasovarman I founded Yasodharapura around 889, and for five centuries the Angkor region was the heart of the Khmer Empire. After 1431 the court moved south, though Angkor Wat remained a pilgrimage centre; Siam returned the province to French Cambodia in 1907.
summary.zh: 耶输跋摩一世约于889年建立耶输陀罗补罗，此后五个世纪里吴哥地区一直是高棉帝国的中心。1431年后王廷南迁，吴哥窟仍为朝圣之地；1907年暹罗将该省归还法属柬埔寨。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Angkor (Siem Reap)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Angkor

places.note: The capital moved between Angkor and nearby sites (e.g. Koh Ker, 928–944).

summary.en: Capital of the first Burmese empire, whose rulers and subjects built over 10,000 Buddhist temples and stupas on the plain beside the Irrawaddy between the 11th and 13th centuries; more than 2,000 survive.
summary.zh: 缅甸第一个帝国的都城。11至13世纪间，君主与臣民在伊洛瓦底江畔的平原上建造了一万多座佛寺与佛塔，现存两千余座。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bagan
Michael Aung-Thwin, Pagan: The Origins of Modern Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 1985)
Wikipedia: Bagan

places.note: The 849 founding date is traditional (chronicles).
