summary.en: A city sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Hadrian refounded it as Aelia Capitolina after 135; Arabic usage moved from Iliya to al-Quds ("the Holy"). Its sovereignty, especially of East Jerusalem, remains disputed between Israel and the Palestinians.
summary.zh: 犹太教、基督教和伊斯兰教共同的圣城。135年后哈德良将其重建为爱利亚加比多连；阿拉伯语称谓由“伊利亚”逐渐变为“古德斯”（意为“神圣”）。其主权，尤其是东耶路撒冷的地位，至今仍是以色列与巴勒斯坦之间的争议焦点。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jerusalem
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Aelia Capitolina
Wikipedia: Jerusalem

places.note: Frankish rule briefly returned in 1229–1244; not shown as a separate span.

polity.zh: 伊利汗国、札剌亦儿王朝、土库曼诸王朝、萨法维王朝

polity.en: British occupation and Mandate; Kingdom of Iraq from 1921
polity.zh: 英国占领与委任统治；1921年起为伊拉克王国

summary.en: Founded by al-Mansur in 762 as the round city of Madinat al-Salam near an older village called Baghdad. Capital of the Abbasid caliphate until the Mongol sack of 1258, then a provincial centre under Ilkhanid, Safavid and Ottoman rule, and capital of Iraq since 1921.
summary.zh: 762年由曼苏尔在名为“巴格达”的旧村附近建为圆城“和平之城”。在1258年蒙古攻陷前一直是阿拔斯王朝首都，此后在伊利汗国、萨法维和奥斯曼治下为地方中心，1921年起为伊拉克首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Baghdad
J. Lassner, The Topography of Baghdad in the Early Middle Ages (1970)
Wikipedia: Baghdad

places.note: Safavid control in 1508–1534 and 1624–1638 is folded into the adjacent spans.

polity.zh: 哈里发国、布韦希、塞尔柱（首都）、伊利汗国、帖木儿

polity.en: Hotaki, Afsharid, Zand and Qajar Iran
polity.zh: 霍塔克、阿夫沙尔、赞德与卡扎尔伊朗

summary.en: Known in antiquity as Aspadana and to the Sasanians as Spahan, the city was a Seljuk capital and reached its height after Shah Abbas I made it the Safavid capital in 1598, until the Afghan conquest of 1722.
summary.zh: 古称阿斯帕达纳，萨珊时期称斯帕汉，曾为塞尔柱王朝都城；1598年阿拔斯一世定都于此后达到鼎盛，直至1722年阿富汗人攻陷。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Esfahan
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Isfahan (multi-part article)
Wikipedia: Isfahan

places.note: The identification of ancient Aspadana/Gabae with Isfahan is generally accepted but approximate.

polity.zh: 第比利斯埃米尔国（哈里发治下）

polity.en: Kingdom of Georgia; Kartli and Kartli-Kakheti
polity.zh: 格鲁吉亚王国；卡特利及卡特利-卡赫季王国
格鲁吉亚苏维埃社会主义共和国
格鲁吉亚苏维埃社会主义共和国

summary.en: Founded by King Vakhtang Gorgasali in the 5th century near hot springs (Georgian tbili, "warm"). Under Arab emirs for four centuries, it was retaken by David IV in 1122. The Russian form Tiflis was officially replaced by Tbilisi in 1936.
summary.zh: 5世纪由瓦赫坦·戈尔加萨利国王在温泉附近建立（格鲁吉亚语tbili意为“温暖”）。阿拉伯埃米尔统治约四百年后，1122年被大卫四世收复。俄语名称“梯弗里斯”于1936年正式改为“第比利斯”。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tbilisi
D. Rayfield, Edge of Empires: A History of Georgia (2012)
Wikipedia: Tbilisi

places.note: Founding c. 455–479 is traditional; capital status shifted between Tbilisi and other towns at times.

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（加拉太行省首府）

polity.en: Seljuks of Rum and Turkish beyliks
polity.zh: 罗姆塞尔柱及突厥诸侯国

summary.en: Ancient Ancyra, capital of the Roman province of Galatia and site of the Monumentum Ancyranum. Under the Ottomans it was known in the West as Angora, famous for its goats' wool. Atatürk made it the base of the national movement in 1920 and the capital of the Republic in 1923.
summary.zh: 古称安基拉，罗马加拉太行省首府，存有《奥古斯都功业录》铭文。奥斯曼时期在西方称安哥拉，以安哥拉山羊毛著称。1920年阿塔图尔克以此为民族运动基地，1923年定为共和国首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ankara
C. Foss, "Late Antique and Byzantine Ankara", Dumbarton Oaks Papers 31 (1977)
Wikipedia: Ankara

places.note: Turkish control after 1073 was interrupted; the date of Ottoman capture (1354) follows the usual account. Western use of "Angora" ended after the 1930 postal law.

polity.en: Aydınid beylik (harbour castle held by the Knights Hospitaller 1344–1402)
polity.zh: 艾登侯国（港口城堡1344—1402年由医院骑士团据守）

summary.en: Ancient Smyrna was one of the great ports of Roman Asia and an early Christian centre. Contested between Turkish emirs, Byzantines and crusading knights, it became Ottoman in the 15th century and a cosmopolitan trading city; it was occupied by Greece in 1919 and largely burned in 1922.
summary.zh: 古城士麦那是罗马亚细亚行省的大港之一和早期基督教中心。曾在突厥埃米尔、拜占庭和十字军骑士之间反复易手，15世纪归入奥斯曼，成为多元的贸易城市；1919年被希腊占领，1922年大部分毁于大火。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Izmir
P. Mansel, Levant: Splendour and Catastrophe on the Mediterranean (2010)
Wikipedia: İzmir

places.note: Byzantine rule was interrupted by the emir Tzachas (c. 1081–1097); Ottoman control was definitive from c. 1426.

polity.zh: 本都王国 / 罗马帝国

summary.en: A Greek colony on the Black Sea, Trapezus was a Roman port and later a Byzantine stronghold. From 1204 it was capital of the Komnenian Empire of Trebizond, the last Byzantine successor state, until Mehmed II took it in 1461.
summary.zh: 黑海沿岸的希腊殖民城市特拉佩祖斯，曾为罗马港口和拜占庭要塞。1204年起为科穆宁家族特拉比宗帝国的首都，这是最后一个拜占庭继承国，1461年被穆罕默德二世攻占。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Trabzon
A. Bryer, The Empire of Trebizond and the Pontos (1980)
Wikipedia: Trabzon

places.note: Pontus was annexed to Rome in stages (64 CE for eastern Pontus).

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（叙利亚行省首府）
历代哈里发国与哈姆丹王朝
法国委任统治（亚历山大勒塔区）

summary.en: Founded by Seleucus I around 300 BCE, Antioch was one of the largest cities of the Roman East and the place where followers of Jesus were first called Christians. Repeatedly ruined by earthquakes and wars, it was a crusader principality capital and joined Turkey in 1939.
summary.zh: 约公元前300年由塞琉古一世建立，安条克是罗马东方最大的城市之一，耶稣的追随者在此首次被称为“基督徒”。屡遭地震和战乱摧残，曾为十字军安条克公国首都，1939年并入土耳其。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Antioch
G. Downey, A History of Antioch in Syria from Seleucus to the Arab Conquest (1961)
Wikipedia: Antakya

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国及埃米尔国

polity.en: Zengids, Ayyubids, Mongols, Mamluks, Aq Qoyunlu
polity.zh: 赞吉、阿尤布、蒙古、马穆鲁克、白羊王朝

summary.en: Edessa, capital of the kingdom of Osroene, was a cradle of Syriac Christianity. Its Arabic name al-Ruha comes from the Syriac Urhay, the root of modern Urfa. It was the first crusader state (1098–1144), and received the honorific "Şanlı" (glorious) in 1984.
summary.zh: 埃德萨是奥斯若恩王国都城，也是叙利亚语基督教的摇篮。阿拉伯语名“鲁哈”源于叙利亚语“乌尔海”，也是今名“乌尔法”的来源。它是第一个十字军国家（1098—1144年）的中心，1984年获“尚勒”（光荣）称号。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sanliurfa
J. B. Segal, Edessa: "The Blessed City" (1970)
Wikipedia: Urfa

places.note: End of Osroene's independence is dated variously 214–242; Sasanian occupation 609–628 is not shown.

name.en: Nineveh area (Ninwe; fortress opposite the ruins)
name.zh: 尼尼微一带（尼尼微遗址对岸的要塞）

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国、哈姆丹、乌盖勒、塞尔柱
伊利汗国及其后继王朝

polity.en: British occupation and Mandate of Iraq
polity.zh: 英国占领与伊拉克委任统治

summary.en: Mosul grew on the west bank of the Tigris opposite the ruins of Assyrian Nineveh. Taken by the Arabs in 641, it flourished as a Zengid capital and trading centre, gave its name to muslin, and was held by ISIS in 2014–2017.
summary.zh: 摩苏尔位于底格里斯河西岸，与亚述古都尼尼微遗址隔河相望。641年被阿拉伯人攻占，曾作为赞吉王朝都城和商贸中心而繁荣，“平纹细布”（muslin）一词即源于其名；2014—2017年被“伊斯兰国”占据。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mosul
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nineveh
Wikipedia: Mosul

places.note: The pre-Islamic settlement and its name are poorly documented; the first span is approximate.

polity.zh: 伊利汗国及其后继王朝
萨法维、阿夫沙尔与赞德伊朗

summary.en: A village near the great city of Rey, Tehran grew after the Mongols destroyed Rey in 1220. Shah Tahmasp I walled it in the 16th century, and Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar made it his capital; it has been the capital of Iran ever since.
summary.zh: 德黑兰原是大城剌夷附近的村落，1220年蒙古人毁灭剌夷后逐渐兴起。16世纪塔赫玛斯普一世为其筑城墙，阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔定都于此，此后一直是伊朗首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tehran
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Tehran
Wikipedia: Tehran

places.note: Capital from 1786 per most sources; Wikidata gives 1794 as an inception-type date.

modern.zh: 萨勒曼帕克（泰西封遗址）

polity.zh: 正统、倭马亚与阿拔斯哈里发国
阿拔斯王朝及后继诸国

summary.en: Twin city on the Tigris, with Seleucia opposite, that served as the Parthian and Sasanian capital. The Arabs called the conurbation al-Mada'in; it declined after Baghdad was founded. The great arch of the Taq-i Kisra still stands at Salman Pak, named after the companion Salman al-Farisi.
summary.zh: 泰西封与对岸的塞琉西亚组成底格里斯河畔的双城，是安息和萨珊的都城。阿拉伯人称这一城市群为“麦达因”，巴格达建立后逐渐衰落。著名的霍斯劳拱门至今矗立在以圣门弟子萨勒曼·法尔西命名的萨勒曼帕克。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ctesiphon
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Ctesiphon
Wikipedia: Ctesiphon

places.note: The modern name Salman Pak predates Iraqi independence; the 1932 boundary only marks the state change.

polity.zh: 阿拔斯、图伦、伊赫什德、法蒂玛
塞尔柱、布里德、赞吉、阿尤布

summary.en: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Damascus was the Umayyad capital from 661 to 750 and later a major centre under the Ayyubids, Mamluks and Ottomans, and has been the capital of independent Syria since 1946.
summary.zh: 世界上有人持续居住的最古老城市之一。661—750年为倭马亚王朝首都，后在阿尤布、马穆鲁克和奥斯曼治下仍是重要中心，1946年起为独立叙利亚的首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Damascus
R. Burns, Damascus: A History (2nd ed., 2019)
Wikipedia: Damascus

polity.en: Caliphates; Sharifate of Mecca from c. 967
polity.zh: 历代哈里发国；约967年起为麦加谢里夫国
奥斯曼宗主下的谢里夫国

summary.en: A caravan and pilgrimage town around the Kaaba, birthplace of Muhammad and the holiest city of Islam. Governed for nearly a millennium by sharifs descended from the Prophet under successive overlords, it passed to the Saudis in 1924–25.
summary.zh: 围绕克尔白形成的商队与朝觐城镇，穆罕默德的出生地，伊斯兰教第一圣城。近一千年间由先知后裔谢里夫在历代宗主国之下治理，1924—1925年归入沙特。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mecca
F. E. Peters, Mecca: A Literary History of the Muslim Holy Land (1994)
Wikipedia: Mecca

places.note: Mecca's pre-Islamic history is poorly documented; the first span starts at an approximate date.

polity.en: Armenian kingdoms and successive Persian, Arab and Turkic rulers
polity.zh: 亚美尼亚诸王国及历代波斯、阿拉伯、突厥统治者

polity.en: Safavid and later Persian rule (Erivan Khanate), with Ottoman interludes
polity.zh: 萨法维及其后波斯统治（埃里温汗国），间有奥斯曼统治
亚美尼亚苏维埃社会主义共和国

summary.en: Yerevan traces its origin to the Urartian fortress of Erebuni, founded by King Argishti I in 782 BCE. A modest town for centuries, it was the seat of the Persian khans of Erivan until Russia took it in 1827–28, and became capital of Armenia in 1918.
summary.zh: 埃里温起源于公元前782年乌拉尔图国王阿尔吉什提一世修建的埃里布尼要塞。数百年间规模不大，曾为波斯埃里温汗的治所，1827—1828年被俄国占领，1918年成为亚美尼亚首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Yerevan
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Erevan
Wikipedia: Yerevan

places.note: Continuity between Erebuni and medieval Erevan is assumed; the long second span lumps many rulers.

summary.en: Nicaea hosted the first (325) and seventh (787) ecumenical councils. It was briefly the first capital of the Seljuks of Rum, the seat of the Byzantine government-in-exile after 1204, and under the Ottomans became famous for İznik pottery and tiles.
summary.zh: 尼西亚曾召开第一次（325年）和第七次（787年）大公会议。它一度是罗姆塞尔柱的首个都城，1204年后为拜占庭流亡政府所在地，奥斯曼时期以伊兹尼克陶器和瓷砖闻名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Iznik
C. Foss, Nicaea: A Byzantine Capital and Its Praises (1996)
Wikipedia: İznik

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国、拉瓦德、塞尔柱、伊尔迪吉兹
札剌亦儿、黑羊、白羊王朝

polity.en: Safavid, Afsharid, Zand and Qajar Iran (seat of the crown prince under the Qajars)
polity.zh: 萨法维、阿夫沙尔、赞德与卡扎尔伊朗（卡扎尔时为王储驻地）

summary.en: The main city of Iranian Azerbaijan and a hub of the Silk Road. Tabriz was the Ilkhanid capital, then capital of the Turkmen dynasties and of the early Safavids until the court moved to Qazvin, and a cradle of the Constitutional Revolution.
summary.zh: 伊朗阿塞拜疆的首要城市和丝绸之路枢纽。大不里士曾为伊利汗国都城，后为土库曼诸王朝和早期萨法维王朝的首都，直至宫廷迁往加兹温；它也是立宪革命的摇篮之一。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tabriz
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Tabriz
Wikipedia: Tabriz

places.note: The Safavid move to Qazvin is dated 1548–1555; Ottoman occupations (e.g. 1585–1603) are not shown.

capital.zh: 坦贾武尔；恒伽贡达朱罗补罗

summary.en: An ancient Tamil lineage revived by Vijayalaya in the 9th century, the Cholas built an empire over south India and Sri Lanka, projected naval power into Southeast Asia and left monumental temples and a rich bronze tradition.
summary.zh: 朱罗是古老的泰米尔王族，9世纪由维阇耶拉耶复兴，建立起囊括南印度和斯里兰卡的帝国，海上力量远及东南亚，留下宏伟的神庙和精美的青铜造像传统。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḻas, 2nd ed. (1955)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chola dynasty
Wikidata Q151148

polities.note: The span follows Wikidata (from the Sangam-age Cholas, c. 300 BCE); the imperial Chola state ran from 848 to 1279.

name.zh: 安息帝国（阿萨息斯王朝）

summary.en: The Arsacid dynasty, from the Parni of north-eastern Iran, built an empire from the Euphrates to the borders of India. Its decentralised realm repeatedly fought Rome over Armenia and Mesopotamia until Ardashir I overthrew it in 224.
summary.zh: 源自伊朗东北部帕尔尼部落的阿萨息斯王朝建立了从幼发拉底河延伸到印度边境的帝国。这个分权的国家为争夺亚美尼亚和美索不达米亚多次与罗马交战，224年被阿尔达希尔一世推翻。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Arsacids
M. Brosius, The Persians (2006)
Wikipedia: Parthian Empire

polities.note: Reign dates of Parthian kings are reconstructed largely from coins and are approximate.

name.zh: 百乘王朝（娑多婆诃王朝）

capital.zh: 普拉蒂什塔纳（派坦）；阿默拉沃蒂

summary.en: The Satavahanas ruled the Deccan from Pratishthana and later the Krishna delta, issuing bilingual coins, patronising Buddhist sites such as Amaravati and Karla and contesting western India with the Shaka Kshatrapas.
summary.zh: 百乘王朝以普拉蒂什塔纳为中心统治德干，后期重心移至克里希纳河三角洲；他们发行双语钱币，护持阿默拉沃蒂、卡尔拉等佛教圣地，并与塞种西部总督争夺西印度。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Satavahana dynasty
Wikidata Q5257

polities.note: The “long chronology” (from c. 230 BCE, used by Wikidata) competes with a short one starting in the 1st century BCE; early reign dates are very uncertain.

image.file: Bimbisara with his royal cortege issuing from the city of Rajagriha to visit the Buddha.jpg

summary.en: First half of the Han dynasty, founded by Liu Bang with its capital at Chang'an. It consolidated the imperial system, adopted Confucian statecraft and pushed into the Western Regions before Wang Mang usurped the throne.
summary.zh: 刘邦所建汉朝前期，都长安。巩固郡县帝制、独尊儒术并经营西域，至王莽篡位而中断。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
班固《汉书》卷1–12 帝纪
Britannica: Han dynasty

image.artist: The original uploader was Kallgan at Chinese Wikipedia.

summary.en: Kingdom of southeastern Korea that allied with Tang to conquer Baekje and Goguryeo, then expelled Tang to rule most of the peninsula as Unified Silla from 668/676. It declined in the 9th century and surrendered to Goryeo in 935.
summary.zh: 朝鲜半岛东南部的王国，联合唐朝灭百济、高句丽后又驱逐唐军，自668/676年起以“统一新罗”统治半岛大部。9世纪走向衰落，935年归降高丽。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Silla
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Silla

polities.note: The 57 BCE founding is traditional. Wikidata ends Silla in 892 (start of the Later Three Kingdoms); the formal end was its surrender to Goryeo in 935.

image.file: Earthenware Funerary Objects in the Shape of a Warrior on Horseback 도기 기마인물형 명기 03.jpg

summary.en: The northernmost and largest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, spanning Manchuria and the northern peninsula. It repelled Sui and Tang invasions before falling to a Tang–Silla alliance in 668. Capitals: Jolbon, Gungnae (Ji'an), then Pyongyang from 427.
summary.zh: 朝鲜三国中最北、疆域最大的国家，地跨中国东北与朝鲜半岛北部。曾击退隋、唐的进攻，668年被唐与新罗联军所灭。都城先后为卒本、国内城（今集安），427年起迁至平壤。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Goguryeo
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Goguryeo

polities.note: The 37 BCE founding date is traditional (Samguk sagi).

summary.en: Kingdom of southwestern Korea that transmitted Buddhism, writing and craftsmen to Japan. Driven south from the Han River by Goguryeo in 475, it ruled from Ungjin and then Sabi until conquered by Tang and Silla in 660.
summary.zh: 朝鲜半岛西南部的王国，曾向日本传入佛教、文字与工匠。475年被高句丽逐出汉江流域后，先后以熊津、泗沘为都，660年被唐与新罗联军所灭。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Baekje
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Baekje Historic Areas
Wikipedia: Paekche

polities.note: The 18 BCE founding date and early reigns are traditional.

summary.en: Short-lived dynasty proclaimed by the regent Wang Mang. His land, slave and currency reforms modelled on the classics caused upheaval, and the Red Eyebrows and Lülin uprisings ended it when Chang'an fell in 23.
summary.zh: 外戚王莽代汉所建王朝。托古改制推行王田、私属与币制改革，引发动荡，赤眉、绿林起义后于23年长安城破而亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
班固《汉书》卷99 王莽传
Britannica: Wang Mang

polities.note: Jiangshan-map dates the abdication of Ruzi Ying to 8 CE; Wang Mang took the throne in the 12th month of Chushi 1, i.e. January 9 CE, which Wikidata follows.

name.zh: 亚美尼亚王国（阿萨息斯王朝）

capital.zh: 阿尔塔沙特，后为瓦加尔沙帕特、德温

summary.en: A branch of the Parthian Arsacids ruled Armenia, usually as a buffer between Rome and Iran, until the Sasanians abolished the monarchy in 428. Under Tiridates III Armenia adopted Christianity, and in this era the Armenian alphabet was created.
summary.zh: 安息阿萨息斯家族的一支统治亚美尼亚，通常作为罗马与伊朗之间的缓冲国，直至428年萨珊王朝废除其王权。梯里达底三世时亚美尼亚皈依基督教，亚美尼亚字母也创制于这一时期。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tiridates III
R. G. Hovannisian (ed.), The Armenian People from Ancient to Modern Times, vol. 1 (1997)
Wikipedia: Arsacid dynasty of Armenia

polities.note: Arsacid rule was intermittent before 66 CE; reign dates are approximate.

summary.en: Restored Han dynasty founded by Liu Xiu (Emperor Guangwu) with its capital at Luoyang. It saw the arrival of Buddhism, papermaking and Ban Chao's western campaigns, then declined amid eunuch–consort feuds and the Yellow Turban rising.
summary.zh: 光武帝刘秀复兴的汉朝，都洛阳。佛教东传、蔡伦造纸、班超经营西域皆在此期；后期外戚宦官交替专权，黄巾起义后走向分裂。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
范晔《后汉书》卷1–9 帝纪
Britannica: Han dynasty

polities.note: Wikidata starts Eastern Han in 23 (fall of Wang Mang); Jiangshan-map and the Hou Hanshu date the restoration to Liu Xiu's accession in 25 (Jianwu 1), used here.

capital.zh: 布路沙布逻（白沙瓦）；秣菟罗

summary.en: Founded by Yuezhi clans who had settled in Bactria, the Kushan Empire spanned Central Asia and north India, linked the Silk Road to the Indian Ocean trade and fostered Gandhara and Mathura Buddhist art.
summary.zh: 贵霜帝国由定居大夏的月氏部落建立，疆域横跨中亚和北印度，连接丝绸之路与印度洋贸易，并孕育了犍陀罗和秣菟罗佛教艺术。

sources.title: János Harmatta (ed.), History of Civilizations of Central Asia, vol. II (UNESCO, 1994)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kushan dynasty
Wikidata Q25979

polities.note: Kushan regnal dates depend on the debated date of Kanishka’s accession (here c. 127, after Falk 2001).

summary.en: A league of small iron-producing polities in the Nakdong River basin, closely linked by trade to the Wa of Japan. Its members were absorbed by Silla, the last, Daegaya, in 562.
summary.zh: 洛东江流域盛产铁器的小国联盟，与日本的倭国贸易往来密切。其成员先后被新罗吞并，最后的大伽倻于562年灭亡。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gaya confederacy
Iryeon, Samguk yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, c. 1281)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Kaya confederacy

polities.note: The AD 42 founding and King Suro's reign follow the legendary Garakguk-gi preserved in the Samguk yusa.

capital.zh: 特牧城（可能在巴普农附近）

summary.en: An early Indianised trading state of the lower Mekong, known chiefly from Chinese records. Its port of Óc Eo linked Indian Ocean and South China Sea commerce until Funan was eclipsed by Zhenla in the 6th century.
summary.zh: 湄公河下游早期受印度文化影响的贸易国家，主要见于中国史籍记载。其港口俄厄连接印度洋与南海贸易，6世纪被真腊取代。

name.zh: 阇耶跋摩（憍陈如阇耶跋摩）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Funan
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Michael Vickery, Society, Economics, and Politics in Pre-Angkor Cambodia (Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies, 1998)
Wikipedia: Funan

polities.note: Founding and end dates are approximate (Wikidata gives 68–550); Fan Shiman's reign dates are estimates from Chinese accounts.

summary.en: A coastal civilisation of central and southern Vietnam made up of several Hindu–Buddhist Cham principalities that thrived on maritime trade. Gradually pushed south by Đại Việt, its last remnant was annexed by the Nguyễn in 1832.
summary.zh: 越南中南部沿海由多个信奉印度教与佛教的占族邦国组成的文明，以海上贸易兴盛。占婆逐渐被大越向南挤压，最后的残余于1832年被阮朝吞并。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Champa
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Champa

polities.note: The 192 start follows the Chinese record of Lâm Ấp (Linyi); capitals shifted between Indrapura, Vijaya and Panduranga.

summary.en: Northern and strongest of the Three Kingdoms, founded when Cao Pi accepted the abdication of the last Han emperor. It introduced the nine-rank system, conquered Shu in 263, and was itself usurped by the Sima clan.
summary.zh: 三国中最强的北方政权，曹丕受汉献帝禅让而建，都洛阳。行九品官人法，263年灭蜀，终为司马氏所代。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
陈寿《三国志》卷1–4 魏书 帝纪
资治通鉴 卷69 魏纪一

polities.note: Jiangshan-map and Wikidata both end Wei in 265 (Xianxi 2, 12th month); in the Julian calendar the abdication fell in February 266.

summary.en: Three Kingdoms state in Sichuan founded by Liu Bei, who claimed the Han succession. Under chancellor Zhuge Liang it pacified the south and launched repeated northern campaigns, before surrendering to Wei forces under Deng Ai in 263.
summary.zh: 刘备于成都称帝所建，以承汉统自居。丞相诸葛亮南征北伐，263年邓艾兵临成都，后主刘禅出降。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
陈寿《三国志》卷32–33 蜀书 先主传、后主传
资治通鉴 卷69 魏纪一 黄初二年

summary.en: Three Kingdoms state of the lower Yangtze, built by the Sun family. Sun Quan ruled from Wuchang, then Jianye (Nanjing) after proclaiming himself emperor in 229; Wu developed the south and its navy before falling to Jin in 280.
summary.zh: 孙氏据江东所建政权。孙权先都武昌，229年称帝后迁建业；开发江南、经营水师，280年为西晋所灭。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
陈寿《三国志》卷47 吴书二 吴主传
资治通鉴 卷71 魏纪三 太和三年

polities.note: Sun Quan became King of Wu in 222 and emperor in 229; 222 is used as the start, following Wikidata.

summary.en: The last pre-Islamic Iranian empire, founded by Ardashir I, ruled from Mesopotamia to Central Asia. A Zoroastrian monarchy with a centralised administration, it rivalled Rome and Byzantium for four centuries before falling to the Arab conquests; Yazdegerd III, the last shah, died in 651.
summary.zh: 阿尔达希尔一世建立的最后一个前伊斯兰伊朗帝国，疆域从美索不达米亚延伸到中亚。这个奉琐罗亚斯德教、行政集中的君主国与罗马和拜占庭抗衡四百年，终亡于阿拉伯征服；末代君主伊嗣俟三世于651年身亡。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sasanian dynasty
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Sasanian dynasty
Wikipedia: Sasanian Empire

summary.en: The era in which the Yamato court in the Nara basin, at first a paramount chieftaincy that built great keyhole tombs, consolidated rule over much of Japan, adopted Buddhism and Chinese-style law, and began calling its ruler tennō.
summary.zh: 以奈良盆地为中心的大和政权时期。大和起初为修筑巨大前方后圆坟的豪族联盟首领，后逐步统一日本大部，接受佛教与中国式律令制度，并开始以“天皇”称呼君主。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Yamato period

polities.note: Start date (c. 250, the beginning of the Kofun period) is approximate; reign dates before the 6th century are traditional.

summary.en: Dynasty of the Sima clan that replaced Wei and reunified China by conquering Wu in 280. Enfeoffed princes fought the War of the Eight Princes; Xiongnu forces then sacked Luoyang (311) and Chang'an (316).
summary.zh: 司马炎代魏所建，280年灭吴统一。宗室诸王混战成八王之乱，匈奴汉赵先后攻陷洛阳（311）与长安（316）。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
房玄龄等《晋书》卷3–5 帝纪
Britannica: Jin dynasty (265–420)

polities.note: Sima Yan's accession is dated 265 (Taishi 1) by Jiangshan-map and Wikidata; in the Julian calendar it fell in February 266.

summary.en: Under Queen Zenobia, ruling for her son Vaballathus, the caravan city of Palmyra broke away from a crisis-ridden Rome and seized Egypt and much of Anatolia. Emperor Aurelian defeated her in 272 and sacked Palmyra after a revolt in 273.
summary.zh: 在为儿子瓦巴拉图斯摄政的芝诺比阿女王领导下，商队城市帕尔米拉脱离危机中的罗马，夺取埃及和安纳托利亚大部。272年奥勒良皇帝击败她，273年平定叛乱后洗劫帕尔米拉。

name.zh: 奥登纳图斯（帕尔米拉国王）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Zenobia
Zosimus, New History, Book I
Wikipedia: Palmyrene Empire

summary.en: The Pallavas of Kanchipuram dominated the Tamil north, fought long wars with the Chalukyas of Badami and pioneered Dravidian stone architecture at Mamallapuram before being supplanted by the Cholas.
summary.zh: 甘吉布勒姆的帕拉瓦王朝称雄泰米尔北部，与巴达米的遮娄其王朝长期交战，并在马马拉普拉姆开创达罗毗荼石构建筑，后被朱罗王朝取代。

name.zh: 那罗僧诃跋摩二世（罗阇僧诃）

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, 4th ed. (1975)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pallava dynasty
Wikidata Q466803

polities.note: Early Pallava chronology (3rd–6th c.) is poorly known.

summary.en: First of the Sixteen Kingdoms, founded by the Xiongnu noble Liu Yuan, who claimed the Han name. His successors captured Luoyang and Chang'an and ended the Western Jin; Liu Yao renamed the state Zhao and was destroyed by Shi Le.
summary.zh: 十六国之首，匈奴刘渊以汉为号起兵。其后攻陷洛阳、长安灭西晋；刘曜改国号赵，迁都长安，终为石勒所灭。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
房玄龄等《晋书》卷101–103 载记 刘元海、刘聪、刘曜
资治通鉴 卷85 晋纪七 永兴元年

summary.en: Jin court re-established south of the Yangtze by Sima Rui after the fall of the north, ruling from Jiankang in partnership with great émigré clans such as the Wang and Xie. It repelled Former Qin at the Fei River and was ended by Liu Yu.
summary.zh: 西晋亡后司马睿在建康重建的晋室，与王、谢等门阀共治。淝水之战击退前秦，终由刘裕代晋建宋。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
房玄龄等《晋书》卷6–10 帝纪
资治通鉴 卷90 晋纪十二 建武元年

summary.en: Sixteen Kingdoms state founded by the Jie general Shi Le, who destroyed the Han-Zhao and dominated north China. Shi Hu moved the capital to Ye; after his death the Ran Min massacre destroyed the dynasty.
summary.zh: 羯人石勒所建，灭汉赵后统一北方大部。石虎迁都邺城，其死后诸子争立，冉闵夺权诛石氏而亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
房玄龄等《晋书》卷104–107 载记 石勒、石季龙
资治通鉴 卷91 晋纪十三 太兴二年

summary.en: From Pataliputra the Guptas united most of north India; their era is remembered for Sanskrit literature (Kalidasa), mathematics (Aryabhata), temple architecture and Nalanda, before Hun invasions and regional revolts broke the empire.
summary.zh: 笈多王朝以华氏城为中心统一北印度大部，以梵语文学（迦梨陀娑）、数学（阿耶波多）、神庙建筑和那烂陀寺著称，后因嚈哒（白匈奴）入侵和地方叛离而瓦解。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gupta dynasty
Wikidata Q11774

polities.note: The end date (c. 550) is conventional; Gupta rulers persisted locally into the late 6th century.

summary.en: Di-led Sixteen Kingdoms state centred on Chang'an. Fu Jian and his minister Wang Meng unified north China by 376, but defeat at the Fei River in 383 shattered the empire.
summary.zh: 氐族苻氏所建，都长安。苻坚任王猛，376年统一北方；383年淝水惨败后迅速瓦解。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
房玄龄等《晋书》卷112–115 载记 苻洪、苻健、苻坚
资治通鉴 卷99 晋纪二十一 永和七年

polities.note: Wikidata starts Former Qin in 350 (Fu Hong's claim); the Jin shu dates Fu Jian's proclamation as Heavenly King at Chang'an to 351 (Yonghe 7), Jiangshan-map's date, used here.

summary.en: Xianbei Tuoba dynasty that reunified north China in 439, ending the Sixteen Kingdoms. Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang and pursued sinicising reforms; the Six Garrisons revolt split it into Eastern and Western Wei.
summary.zh: 鲜卑拓跋氏所建，439年统一北方，结束十六国。孝文帝迁都洛阳推行汉化；六镇之乱后分裂为东、西魏。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
魏收《魏书》卷1–11 帝纪
Britannica: Northern Wei dynasty

polities.note: Jiangshan-map ends Northern Wei in 534 when Emperor Xiaowu fled west; Wikidata uses 535, when he died and Western Wei was proclaimed.

summary.en: First of the Southern Dynasties, founded by the general Liu Yu after his northern conquests. The Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen was prosperous, but failed northern campaigns and fratricide weakened it until Xiao Daocheng seized power.
summary.zh: 南朝第一代，刘裕北伐立功后代晋所建，都建康。宋文帝元嘉之治较为繁荣；北伐失利、宗室相残，终为萧道成所代。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
沈约《宋书》卷1–10 本纪
资治通鉴 卷119 宋纪一 永初元年

summary.en: Short Southern Dynasty of the Xiao family founded by Xiao Daocheng. Purges of princes under Emperor Ming and the misrule of Xiao Baojuan led the Yongzhou governor Xiao Yan to rise at Xiangyang and found Liang.
summary.zh: 萧道成代宋所建南朝政权，都建康。齐明帝大诛宗室，东昏侯昏暴，雍州刺史萧衍起兵襄阳而代之。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
萧子显《南齐书》卷1–8 本纪
资治通鉴 卷135 齐纪一 建元元年

summary.en: Southern Dynasty founded by Xiao Yan (Emperor Wu), whose nearly fifty-year reign was a high point of southern culture and Buddhist patronage. The rebellion of Hou Jing devastated Jiankang in 548–552 and the dynasty never recovered.
summary.zh: 萧衍所建南朝政权，都建康。梁武帝在位近五十年，文教昌盛、崇信佛教；侯景之乱残破江南，梁室自此不振。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
姚思廉《梁书》卷1–6 本纪
资治通鉴 卷145 梁纪一 天监元年

polities.note: Wikidata ends the Liang in 587, counting the Western Liang rump state at Jiangling; Jiangshan-map ends it with Chen Baxian's usurpation in 557, used here.

image.file: Xiao Hui - eastern bixie, seen from S - P1070581.JPG

summary.en: Eastern successor of the divided Northern Wei, ruled in name by Emperor Xiaojing from Ye while real power lay with Gao Huan and his sons, who replaced it with Northern Qi in 550.
summary.zh: 北魏分裂后的东部政权，都邺。孝静帝在位而权归高欢父子，550年高洋代之建北齐。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
魏收《魏书》卷12 孝静纪
李百药《北齐书》卷1–2 神武纪

summary.en: Western successor of Northern Wei, dominated by Yuwen Tai from Chang'an. Its fubing militia and the Guanzhong aristocracy laid the foundations of the Sui and Tang; it seized Sichuan and Jiangling from Liang.
summary.zh: 北魏分裂后的西部政权，宇文泰掌权，都长安。创府兵制，形成关陇集团，夺取萧梁巴蜀与江陵，为隋唐奠基。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
令狐德棻等《周书》卷1–2 文帝纪
李延寿《北史》卷5 魏本纪五

summary.en: Ruling the western Deccan from Vatapi, the early Chalukyas reached their height under Pulakeshin II, who stopped Harsha on the Narmada; their temples at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal shaped Deccan architecture.
summary.zh: 早期遮娄其王朝以伐陀毗为都统治德干西部，在补罗稽舍二世时达到鼎盛，曾于讷尔默达河击退戒日王；其在艾霍莱、巴达米和帕塔达卡尔的神庙深刻影响了德干建筑。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, 4th ed. (1975)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chalukya dynasty
Wikidata Q1395011

summary.en: Dynasty of the Gao family that succeeded Eastern Wei, ruling the rich North China Plain from Ye with Jinyang as secondary capital. Court violence weakened it, and Northern Zhou conquered it in 577.
summary.zh: 高洋代东魏所建，都邺，以晋阳为别都，据华北富庶之地。宫廷屡生残杀，577年为北周所灭。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
李百药《北齐书》卷4–8 帝纪
资治通鉴 卷163 梁纪十九 大宝元年

summary.en: Dynasty of the Yuwen clan that replaced Western Wei. Emperor Wu suppressed Buddhism and Daoism to strengthen the state and conquered Northern Qi in 577; his chancellor Yang Jian took the throne in 581 as founder of Sui.
summary.zh: 宇文觉代西魏所建，都长安。周武帝禁佛道以强国，577年灭北齐；581年外戚杨坚受禅建隋。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
令狐德棻等《周书》卷3–8 帝纪
资治通鉴 卷167 陈纪一 永定元年

summary.en: Last of the Southern Dynasties, founded by Chen Baxian after he suppressed Hou Jing's rebellion. Confined to the lower Yangtze, it fell in 589 when Sui armies crossed the river and captured Chen Shubao in Jiankang.
summary.zh: 陈霸先平侯景之乱后受梁禅所建，都建康。疆域局促江南，589年隋军渡江攻入建康，俘陈后主而亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
姚思廉《陈书》卷1–6 本纪
资治通鉴 卷177 隋纪一 开皇九年

summary.en: Dynasty that reunified China in 589 after nearly three centuries of division. It created the Three Departments and Six Ministries, the first examinations and the Grand Canal, but costly Korean wars under Emperor Yang provoked its collapse.
summary.zh: 杨坚代北周所建，589年灭陈结束近三百年分裂。确立三省六部、首创科举、开凿大运河；隋炀帝三征高句丽耗尽民力而亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
魏征等《隋书》卷1–5 帝纪
Britannica: Sui dynasty

summary.en: Dynasty of the Li family whose cosmopolitan capital Chang'an was the largest city of its age. Early Tang extended protectorates across Central Asia; after the An Lushan rebellion regional governors gained power until Zhu Wen ended the dynasty in 907.
summary.zh: 李渊所建王朝，都长安，为当时世界最大都会。前期设都护府经营西域，安史之乱后藩镇割据，907年为朱温所篡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷1–20 本纪
Britannica: Tang dynasty

summary.en: Empire of the Yarlung dynasty unified by Songtsen Gampo, who married the Tang princess Wencheng. At its height it took the Tarim garrisons and the Hexi Corridor and briefly occupied Chang'an (763); it fragmented after Langdarma's death.
summary.zh: 松赞干布统一青藏高原所建王朝，与唐和亲迎娶文成公主。鼎盛时夺取安西四镇与河西，763年一度攻入长安；朗达玛死后分裂。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷196 吐蕃传
Britannica: Tibet – History

polities.note: Start (c. 618) and early reign dates are approximate; Tibetan and Chinese chronologies differ.

summary.en: The caliphate of the first four successors of Muhammad, called "rightly guided" (Rashidun) by Sunni Muslims. Its armies conquered Syria, Iraq, Egypt and Iran, while disputes over the succession led to the first civil war (656–661).
summary.zh: 穆罕默德之后前四位继承者的哈里发国，逊尼派称之为“正统”。其军队征服叙利亚、伊拉克、埃及和伊朗，而继承权之争导致了第一次内战（656—661年）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Rashidun
W. Madelung, The Succession to Muhammad (1997)
Wikipedia: Rashidun Caliphate

summary.en: A Buddhist maritime power centred on Palembang in Sumatra that controlled the Straits of Malacca and Sunda and was a centre of Buddhist learning visited by the Chinese pilgrim Yijing. Chola raids in 1025 weakened it.
summary.zh: 以苏门答腊巨港为中心的佛教海上强国，控制马六甲海峡与巽他海峡，也是佛学中心，唐代高僧义净曾在此求学。1025年朱罗王朝的袭击使其衰落。

name.zh: 达本达·希扬·室利·阇耶那沙

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Srivijaya
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce: A Study of the Origins of Śrīvijaya (Cornell University Press, 1967)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Srivijaya

polities.note: Dates are approximate; Wikidata gives 650–1377, and the later "Sanfoqi" of Chinese sources may refer to successor centres such as Jambi.

summary.en: The first hereditary caliphate, ruled from Damascus by the Umayyad clan of Quraysh. It extended Muslim rule from Iberia to the Indus, made Arabic the language of administration and built the Dome of the Rock, before falling to the Abbasid revolution.
summary.zh: 首个世袭哈里发国，由古莱什部落的倭马亚家族以大马士革为都统治。它将穆斯林统治从伊比利亚扩展到印度河，以阿拉伯语为行政语言并修建圆顶清真寺，最终被阿拔斯革命推翻。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Umayyad dynasty
H. Kennedy, The Prophet and the Age of the Caliphates (3rd ed., 2016)
Wikipedia: Umayyad Caliphate

summary.en: Interregnum of the Tang in which Wu Zetian ruled as emperor of her own Zhou dynasty, the only woman to do so in Chinese history, governing from Luoyang, renamed the Divine Capital. The Shenlong coup of 705 restored the Tang.
summary.zh: 武则天改唐为周自立为帝，以洛阳为神都，是中国历史上唯一的女皇帝。705年神龙政变后复唐国号。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷6 则天皇后本纪
资治通鉴 卷204 唐纪二十 天授元年

summary.en: A kingdom founded by Dae Jo-yeong, a former Goguryeo general, ruling Manchuria and northern Korea with Goguryeo and Mohe populations. Known to Tang as "the flourishing land in the East", it was destroyed by the Khitan Liao in 926.
summary.zh: 由原高句丽将领大祚荣建立的王国，统治中国东北与朝鲜半岛北部，居民包括高句丽人与靺鞨人。被唐朝誉为“海东盛国”，926年为契丹辽朝所灭。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Balhae
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Parhae

polities.note: Its ethnic composition and historical affiliation are debated between Korean and Chinese historiography.

summary.en: The ritsuryō state at its height, governed from Heijō-kyō under Chinese-style codes. The period produced the Kojiki, Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū and state-sponsored Buddhism centred on Tōdai-ji.
summary.zh: 律令国家的鼎盛时期，以平城京为中心依照中国式律令治国。这一时期编成了《古事记》《日本书纪》和《万叶集》，并形成以东大寺为中心的国家佛教。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nara-period Japan
Shoku Nihongi (797)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Nara period

polities.note: The court left Nara in 784 for Nagaoka-kyō; the period is conventionally closed in 794.

capital.zh: 太和城，后迁阳苴咩城（大理）

summary.en: Kingdom of the Erhai basin in Yunnan formed when Piluoge united the six zhao with Tang backing in 738. It later allied with Tibet, defeated Tang armies in the 750s and raided Sichuan and Annam before its fall in 902.
summary.zh: 唐册封皮逻阁统一六诏所建，都太和城，后迁阳苴咩城。曾附吐蕃、天宝年间大败唐军，屡掠巴蜀与安南，902年亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
欧阳修等《新唐书》卷222 南蛮传 南诏
Britannica: Nanzhao

polities.note: Piluoge reigned as a zhao chief from 728; the unified kingdom with Tang investiture dates from 738.

capital.zh: 华氏城；后为高达、蒙吉尔

summary.en: Elected king by Bengal’s chiefs around 750, Gopala founded a Buddhist dynasty that ruled Bengal and Bihar, patronised Nalanda and founded Vikramashila, and spread Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism to Tibet and Southeast Asia.
summary.zh: 约750年孟加拉诸首领推举瞿波罗为王，其建立的佛教王朝统治孟加拉与比哈尔，护持那烂陀并创建超戒寺，将大乘和金刚乘佛教传播到西藏与东南亚。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pala dynasty
Wikidata Q668412

polities.note: Pala regnal years are approximate.

summary.en: Descendants of the Prophet's uncle al-Abbas, the Abbasids moved the caliphate's centre to Iraq and founded Baghdad. Their early centuries saw a flowering of science and letters; real power later passed to Buyid and Seljuk sultans, and the Mongols ended the Baghdad caliphate in 1258.
summary.zh: 先知叔父阿拔斯的后裔将哈里发国的中心移至伊拉克并建立巴格达。王朝前期科学与文学繁荣；后来实权落入布韦希和塞尔柱苏丹之手，1258年蒙古人终结了巴格达的哈里发政权。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Abbasid caliphate
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Abbasid caliphate
Wikipedia: Abbasid Caliphate

polities.note: A line of Abbasid shadow caliphs continued under the Mamluks in Cairo until 1517.

summary.en: Overthrowing the Chalukyas in 753, the Rashtrakutas made the Deccan a great power that raided Kannauj and the Tamil south; they carved the Kailasa temple at Ellora, and Arab travellers counted their king among the world’s greatest.
summary.zh: 罗湿陀罗拘陀王朝于753年推翻遮娄其王朝，使德干成为强国，曾北袭曲女城、南侵泰米尔地区；他们开凿了埃洛拉的凯拉萨神庙，阿拉伯旅行者将其国王列为世界最伟大的君主之一。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, 4th ed. (1975)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Rashtrakuta dynasty
Wikidata Q856691

summary.en: Four centuries in which the court at Heian-kyō, dominated by Fujiwara regents and later by retired emperors, produced a refined aristocratic culture and kana literature, while provincial warrior bands grew in power.
summary.zh: 以平安京为中心的约四百年。朝廷先由藤原氏摄关、后由退位上皇（院政）主导，孕育出精致的贵族文化与假名文学，同时地方武士集团日益壮大。

name.zh: 后白河天皇（天皇及上皇）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Heian-period Japan
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 2: Heian Japan (1999)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Heian period

summary.en: Founded when Jayavarman II proclaimed himself universal monarch on Phnom Kulen in 802, the Angkorian empire dominated mainland Southeast Asia, engineered vast reservoirs and built Angkor Wat and the Bayon.
summary.zh: 802年阇耶跋摩二世在荔枝山自立为“转轮王”，吴哥帝国由此建立。它称雄东南亚大陆，修建了庞大的水利系统以及吴哥窟、巴戎寺等建筑。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
Wikipedia: Khmer Empire

polities.note: Both 802 and 1431 are conventional dates.

summary.en: The first kingdom to unite the Irrawaddy valley, under Anawrahta from 1044. It spread Theravada Buddhism and the Burmese script, filled its capital with temples, and fragmented after the Mongol invasions of the 1280s.
summary.zh: 1044年阿奴律陀即位后首次统一伊洛瓦底江流域的王国。它传播上座部佛教与缅文，都城佛塔林立，13世纪80年代蒙古入侵后分裂瓦解。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pagan Kingdom

Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom

summary.en: First of the Five Dynasties, founded when the warlord Zhu Wen forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate. It fought a long war with the Shatuo of Hedong and fell when Li Cunxu captured Kaifeng in 923.
summary.zh: 五代第一朝，朱温篡唐所建，都汴州开封。与河东沙陀晋王长期争战，923年李存勖袭破汴州而亡。

summary.en: Coastal Ten Kingdoms state of the Qian family centred on Hangzhou. Qian Liu built the Qiantang seawall and promoted trade and Buddhism; Qian Chu peacefully submitted his territory to the Song in 978.
summary.zh: 钱镠所建，都杭州。筑钱塘捍海石塘，兴商崇佛、保境安民；978年钱俶纳土归宋。

summary.en: Khitan empire founded by Abaoji that ruled Manchuria, Mongolia and the Sixteen Prefectures through a dual northern-southern administration with five capitals. The Chanyuan treaty fixed peace with Song; the Jurchen Jin destroyed it in 1125.
summary.zh: 契丹耶律阿保机所建，行南北面官制、设五京，据有东北、漠北与燕云。澶渊之盟后与宋长期和平，1125年为金所灭。

summary.en: The dynasty from which the name "Korea" derives. Goryeo reunified the peninsula in 936, fostered Buddhism, celadon and printing, endured Khitan and Mongol invasions and became a Yuan vassal before being replaced by Joseon.
summary.zh: “Korea”一名即源于高丽。高丽于936年统一半岛，崇奉佛教，青瓷与印刷术发达，历经契丹、蒙古入侵并一度成为元朝藩属，最终被朝鲜王朝取代。

summary.en: Five Dynasties regime of the Shatuo Li family, who claimed Tang descent. Li Cunxu destroyed Later Liang and Former Shu but died in a mutiny; Shi Jingtang overthrew the dynasty with Khitan help.
summary.zh: 沙陀李存勖称帝所建，以承唐统，都洛阳。灭后梁、前蜀，庄宗死于兵变；石敬瑭借契丹兵灭之。

summary.en: Five Dynasties regime founded by Shi Jingtang, who ceded the Sixteen Prefectures to the Khitan in return for their support. When his successor defied the Liao, the Khitan captured Kaifeng and ended the dynasty.
summary.zh: 石敬瑭割燕云十六州、称儿于契丹而建，都开封。出帝石重贵对契丹称孙不称臣，947年契丹攻入开封而亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

summary.en: Largest of the Ten Kingdoms, founded by Li Bian in Jinling after he replaced the Yang Wu. It annexed Min and Chu, lost Huainan to Later Zhou, and surrendered to Song in 975–976; its last ruler Li Yu is famed for his ci poetry.
summary.zh: 李昪代杨吴所建，都金陵，为十国最强。灭闽、楚，失淮南于后周；975年金陵城破，后主李煜以词名世。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
马令《南唐书》

polities.note: Jinling fell in the 11th month of Kaibao 8 (late 975); Li Yu formally surrendered at Kaifeng in early 976, the end date Wikidata uses. Jiangshan-map uses 975.

summary.en: Buddhist kingdom of the Duan family in Yunnan, founded by Duan Siping in 937 as successor to Nanzhao. It traded horses with Song and was conquered by Kublai's Mongol army, which crossed the Jinsha River in 1253.
summary.zh: 段思平所建云南政权，承南诏故地，崇信佛教，与宋互市战马。1253年忽必烈革囊渡金沙江灭之。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

polities.note: Wikidata ends Dali in 1253; Jiangshan-map uses 1254, when Duan Xingzhi was captured after the 1253 Mongol campaign. Ruler dates are approximate.

summary.en: Shortest of the Five Dynasties, founded by the Hedong governor Liu Zhiyuan after the Khitan withdrew from Kaifeng. His son Liu Chengyou provoked Guo Wei into rebellion and was killed in 951.
summary.zh: 河东节度使刘知远乘契丹北撤而建，都开封，为五代最短。隐帝刘承祐猜忌郭威，951年兵变身死。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
薛居正等《旧五代史》卷99–103 汉书

summary.en: Last of the Five Dynasties, founded by Guo Wei. His adopted son Chai Rong (Shizong) reformed the army, took the Huainan lands from Southern Tang and attacked the Liao, preparing the way for Song reunification.
summary.zh: 郭威所建，都开封。养子周世宗柴荣整军、三征南唐取江北淮南、北伐契丹，为宋朝统一奠基。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
薛居正等《旧五代史》卷110–120 周书
资治通鉴 卷290 后周纪一 广顺元年

summary.en: First half of the Song dynasty, founded by Zhao Kuangyin at Kaifeng. It reunified China proper, subordinated the military to civil officials, and saw printing, paper money and an urban economic boom before the Jurchen sacked Kaifeng in 1127.
summary.zh: 赵匡胤陈桥兵变所建，都东京开封。统一中原与江南，重文抑武；印刷术、交子与城市经济繁荣，1127年靖康之变亡于金。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

capital.zh: 库塔伊西，1122年起为第比利斯

summary.en: Unified under Bagrat III in 1008, the Bagrationi kingdom became the leading Christian power of the Caucasus. Its golden age under David IV and Queen Tamar was ended by Khwarazmian and Mongol invasions; after a revival under George V it split into rival kingdoms in the late 15th century.
summary.zh: 1008年在巴格拉特三世治下统一，巴格拉季昂尼王朝的王国成为高加索首要的基督教强国。大卫四世和塔玛尔女王的黄金时代被花剌子模和蒙古入侵终结；经格奥尔基五世复兴后，15世纪末分裂为数个对立王国。

sources.title: D. Rayfield, Edge of Empires: A History of Georgia (2012)
Kartlis Tskhovreba (The Georgian Chronicles)
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Georgia

summary.en: The first long-lived Vietnamese dynasty, which founded Thăng Long, named the state Đại Việt (1054), patronised Buddhism, set up the Temple of Literature (1070) and defeated a Song invasion in 1077.
summary.zh: 越南第一个长期统治的王朝。李朝建都升龙，1054年定国号大越，崇奉佛教，1070年兴建文庙，并于1077年击退宋军入侵。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Lý dynasty

capital.zh: 内沙布尔、剌夷，后为伊斯法罕

summary.en: An Oghuz Turkic dynasty that conquered Iran, entered Baghdad in 1055 as protector of the Abbasid caliph and defeated Byzantium at Manzikert. Under the vizier Nizam al-Mulk it sponsored madrasas and a Sunni revival; it fragmented after 1092, and the last sultan in Iraq fell in 1194.
summary.zh: 乌古斯突厥王朝，征服伊朗，1055年以阿拔斯哈里发保护者身份进入巴格达，并在曼齐刻尔特击败拜占庭。在宰相尼扎姆·穆勒克主持下兴办经学院、推动逊尼派复兴；1092年后分裂，1194年伊拉克的末代苏丹败亡。

sources.title: A. C. S. Peacock, The Great Seljuk Empire (2015)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Saljuqs
Wikipedia: Seljuk Empire

summary.en: Tangut state proclaimed by Li Yuanhao at Xingqing, controlling the Ordos and the Hexi Corridor. It created its own script, fought and traded with Song, Liao and Jin, and was destroyed by the Mongols in 1227.
summary.zh: 党项李元昊于兴庆府称帝所建，据河套与河西走廊。创制西夏文，与宋、辽、金或战或和，1227年为蒙古所灭。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
脱脱等《宋史》卷485–486 夏国传
Britannica: Xi Xia

summary.en: A Seljuk branch that ruled much of Anatolia after Manzikert, first from Nicaea and from 1097 from Konya. Its 13th-century peak saw caravanserais and Persianate culture flourish; after defeat by the Mongols at Köse Dağ in 1243 it became an Ilkhanid vassal and dissolved by c. 1307.
summary.zh: 塞尔柱的一支，曼齐刻尔特之战后统治安纳托利亚大部，先都尼西亚，1097年起都科尼亚。13世纪鼎盛时商队客栈和波斯化文化繁荣；1243年在克塞山败于蒙古后沦为伊利汗国附庸，约1307年解体。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sultanate of Rum
C. Cahen, The Formation of Turkey (2001)
Wikipedia: Sultanate of Rum

name.zh: 奇里乞亚亚美尼亚王国

summary.en: Founded by Armenian lords who settled in Cilicia after the Seljuk conquest of Greater Armenia, it became a kingdom in 1198. Allied with the crusaders and later the Mongols, it was a centre of Armenian culture until the Mamluks captured Sis in 1375.
summary.zh: 塞尔柱征服大亚美尼亚后，迁居奇里乞亚的亚美尼亚贵族建立此国，1198年升格为王国。它先后与十字军和蒙古结盟，是亚美尼亚文化中心，直至1375年马穆鲁克攻陷都城西斯。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Little Armenia
R. G. Hovannisian (ed.), The Armenian People from Ancient to Modern Times, vol. 1 (1997)
Wikipedia: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia

polities.note: Principality from 1080, kingdom from 1198.

summary.en: A crusader state founded after the capture of Jerusalem in 1099. After Saladin's victory at Hattin in 1187 it lost Jerusalem and survived as a coastal kingdom centred on Acre until the Mamluks took Acre in 1291.
summary.zh: 1099年攻占耶路撒冷后建立的十字军国家。1187年萨拉丁在哈丁获胜后失去耶路撒冷，此后以阿卡为中心作为沿海王国延续，直到1291年阿卡被马穆鲁克攻陷。

name.zh: 布永的戈弗雷（圣墓守护者）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kingdom of Jerusalem
S. Runciman, A History of the Crusades (1951–54)
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Jerusalem

polities.note: Jerusalem itself was briefly held again in 1229–1244.

summary.en: Jurchen dynasty founded by Wanyan Aguda, which destroyed the Liao in 1125 and the Northern Song in 1127, then ruled north China from Zhongdu. Mongol attacks drove it to Kaifeng, and it fell at Caizhou in 1234.
summary.zh: 女真完颜阿骨打所建，1125年灭辽、1127年灭北宋，迁都中都统治华北。蒙古进攻下南迁汴京，1234年亡于蔡州。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)

Britannica: Jin dynasty (1115–1234)

summary.en: Song court re-established in the south by Zhao Gou after the Jingkang disaster, with Lin'an as its "temporary" capital. Despite military pressure from Jin and then the Mongols, its commercial economy and Neo-Confucian scholarship flourished until defeat at Yamen in 1279.
summary.zh: 靖康之变后赵构在南方重建的宋室，以临安为行在。虽受金、蒙古压迫，商业与理学繁盛，1279年崖山海战后灭亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
脱脱等《宋史》卷24–47 本纪
Britannica: Song dynasty

summary.en: Kurdish dynasty founded by Saladin, who ended the Fatimid caliphate in Egypt in 1171 and united Egypt and Syria. It recaptured Jerusalem from the crusaders in 1187; after 1250 power in Egypt passed to the Mamluks, though Ayyubid princes held Hama until 1341.
summary.zh: 萨拉丁建立的库尔德王朝。他于1171年终结埃及的法蒂玛哈里发政权，统一埃及和叙利亚，1187年从十字军手中收复耶路撒冷；1250年后埃及政权落入马穆鲁克之手，但阿尤布家族在哈马的支系延续到1341年。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Ayyubids
R. S. Humphreys, From Saladin to the Mongols (1977)
Wikipedia: Ayyubid dynasty

polities.note: Capital point shown at Damascus, the dynasty's Syrian seat; Cairo was the main seat of the sultans of Egypt.

summary.en: Japan's first warrior government, founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo and later run by the Hōjō regents. It repelled the Mongol invasions but was overthrown in 1333 by Emperor Go-Daigo's supporters.
summary.zh: 日本第一个武家政权，由源赖朝创建，后由北条氏执权掌控。它击退了蒙古入侵，1333年被后醍醐天皇一方推翻。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kamakura shogunate
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)

summary.en: Five successive dynasties—Mamluk, Khalji, Tughluq, Sayyid and Lodi—ruled from Delhi, resisting the Mongols and at their height under Muhammad bin Tughluq reaching almost the whole subcontinent, until Babur’s victory at Panipat.
summary.zh: 马穆鲁克、卡尔吉、图格鲁克、赛义德和洛迪五个王朝相继以德里为都，抵御了蒙古人的进攻，在穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克时疆域几乎覆盖整个次大陆，直至巴布尔在帕尼帕特获胜。

sources.title: Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Delhi sultanate
Wikidata Q229411

summary.en: Successor to the Lý through a marriage engineered by Trần Thủ Độ, the Trần repelled three Mongol–Yuan invasions and fostered the Trúc Lâm school of Vietnamese Zen before being usurped by Hồ Quý Ly.
summary.zh: 经陈守度安排的联姻继承李朝的王朝。陈朝三次击退蒙元入侵，倡导越南禅宗竹林派，后被胡季犛篡夺。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Trần dynasty
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Trần dynasty

summary.en: An early Tai kingdom in the upper Chao Phraya basin, traditionally regarded as the first Thai state. Under Ram Khamhaeng it expanded and adopted Theravada Buddhism; it later became a vassal and then part of Ayutthaya.
summary.zh: 湄南河上游早期的泰族王国，传统上被视为第一个泰国国家。兰甘亨在位时向外扩张并奉行上座部佛教，后沦为阿瑜陀耶的藩属，最终被并入。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sukhothai Kingdom

summary.en: Mongol khanate founded by Hulagu in Iran and Iraq. Its rulers converted to Islam under Ghazan in 1295 and patronised Persian historiography, science and art, notably Rashid al-Din's universal history; the state disintegrated after Abu Sa'id died without an heir in 1335.
summary.zh: 旭烈兀在伊朗和伊拉克建立的蒙古汗国。1295年合赞汗时皈依伊斯兰教，汗廷赞助波斯史学、科学和艺术，尤以拉施特的《史集》著称；1335年不赛因无嗣而终后国家瓦解。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Il-Khanid dynasty
P. Jackson, The Mongols and the Islamic World (2017)
Wikipedia: Ilkhanate

summary.en: Mongol dynasty proclaimed by Kublai Khan in 1271, which conquered the Southern Song and ruled all China from Dadu with Shangdu as summer capital. It created the branch-secretariat provinces and was driven north by the Ming in 1368.
summary.zh: 忽必烈1271年定国号大元，灭南宋统一全国，以大都、上都为两都，创行省制度。1368年明军攻克大都，元廷北迁。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
宋濂等《元史》卷1–47 本纪
Britannica: Yuan dynasty

summary.en: A Hindu–Buddhist kingdom of East Java founded by Raden Wijaya after the Yuan invasion. Under Hayam Wuruk and Gajah Mada it claimed tribute from much of the archipelago, as celebrated in the Nāgarakṛtāgama, before declining amid the rise of Muslim coastal states.
summary.zh: 元军入侵后由罗登·威查耶在东爪哇建立的印度教—佛教王国。在哈奄·武禄与加查·马达治下，它向群岛大部分地区索取朝贡，《爪哇史颂》对此多有颂扬；后在沿海穆斯林国家兴起中衰落。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Majapahit
Mpu Prapañca, Deśawarṇana (Nāgarakṛtāgama, 1365), trans. Stuart Robson (KITLV, 1995)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Majapahit

polities.note: The end date (c. 1527, fall to Demak) is debated; the extent of its "empire" is likely overstated in court poetry.

capital.zh: 索于特、布尔萨、埃迪尔内；1453年起为君士坦丁堡/伊斯坦布尔

summary.en: From a small frontier principality in north-western Anatolia, the Ottoman dynasty built an empire spanning south-east Europe, Anatolia, the Arab lands and North Africa, with Constantinople as capital from 1453. After 19th-century reforms and territorial losses it collapsed after World War I; the sultanate was abolished in 1922.
summary.zh: 奥斯曼王朝从安纳托利亚西北部的边境小公国起家，建立起横跨东南欧、安纳托利亚、阿拉伯地区和北非的帝国，1453年起以君士坦丁堡为都。经历19世纪改革与领土丧失后，帝国在一战后崩溃，苏丹制于1922年被废除。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ottoman Empire
C. Finkel, Osman's Dream: The History of the Ottoman Empire (2005)
Wikipedia: Ottoman Empire

polities.note: Osman I died c. 1323/24 (Wikidata gives 1326).

summary.en: The shogunate of the Ashikaga family, based in Kyoto's Muromachi district. It flourished under Yoshimitsu, who reunited the rival courts and traded with Ming China, but lost real power after the Ōnin War; Oda Nobunaga ended it in 1573.
summary.zh: 足利氏的幕府，设于京都室町。足利义满时期最为鼎盛，统一南北朝并与明朝开展勘合贸易；应仁之乱后实权丧失，1573年被织田信长终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Muromachi (Ashikaga) shogunate
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Ashikaga shogunate

summary.en: Founded by the brothers Harihara and Bukka on the Tungabhadra, Vijayanagara dominated south India for two centuries; its capital at Hampi astonished Persian and Portuguese visitors before the defeat at Talikota in 1565.
summary.zh: 毗奢耶那伽罗由诃里诃罗与布迦兄弟在栋格珀德拉河畔建立，称雄南印度两百年；其都城亨比曾令波斯与葡萄牙访客惊叹，1565年塔利科塔之败后衰落。

name.zh: 萨达湿婆·罗耶（摄政罗摩·罗阇）

sources.title: Burton Stein, Vijayanagara (New Cambridge History of India I.2, 1989)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Group of Monuments at Hampi
Wikidata Q167639

summary.en: Created by a revolt of Deccan nobles against Muhammad bin Tughluq, the Bahmani Sultanate ruled the northern Deccan, fought Vijayanagara and, after the minister Mahmud Gawan’s execution, split into five successor sultanates.
summary.zh: 巴赫曼尼苏丹国由德干贵族反叛穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克而建立，统治德干北部，与毗奢耶那伽罗长期交战；宰相马哈茂德·加万被处死后分裂为五个继承苏丹国。

sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, A Social History of the Deccan, 1300–1761 (2005)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Bahmani sultanate
Wikidata Q374521

name.zh: 阿瑜陀耶王朝（大城王朝）

summary.en: A Siamese kingdom founded by U Thong on an island in the Chao Phraya. For four centuries it was one of Asia's great trading capitals, absorbing Sukhothai and sacking Angkor, until the Burmese destroyed it in 1767.
summary.zh: 乌通王在湄南河中的岛上建立的暹罗王国。四个世纪里它是亚洲重要的贸易都城之一，兼并素可泰并攻陷吴哥，1767年被缅军摧毁。

name.zh: 乌通王（拉玛铁菩提一世）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ayutthaya Kingdom
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya, trans. Richard D. Cushman (Siam Society, 2000)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic City of Ayutthaya
Wikipedia: Ayutthaya Kingdom

polities.note: Wikidata gives 1350; the traditional founding date is 1351.

summary.en: Han Chinese dynasty founded by Zhu Yuanzhang at Nanjing; the Yongle Emperor moved the capital to Beijing and sent Zheng He's fleets abroad. The Ming rebuilt the Great Wall and fell when Li Zicheng took Beijing in 1644.
summary.zh: 朱元璋于应天所建，永乐帝迁都北京并遣郑和下西洋。修筑九边长城，1644年李自成攻陷北京而亡。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
张廷玉等《明史》卷1–24 本纪
Britannica: Ming dynasty

image.artist: Říše Ming.png: Michal Klajban derivative work: Jann translator: Manlleus (ca)

summary.en: Korea's longest-ruling dynasty, founded by Yi Seong-gye. A Neo-Confucian state with a literati bureaucracy, it created Hangul, survived the Japanese and Manchu invasions, and was opened by unequal treaties before becoming the Korean Empire in 1897.
summary.zh: 由李成桂建立，是朝鲜半岛历时最长的王朝。以性理学立国、实行两班文官统治，创制了训民正音，历经壬辰倭乱与丙子胡乱，近代被迫签订不平等条约，1897年改称大韩帝国。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Joseon
Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Joseon

capital.zh: 迈索尔；斯里兰加帕特纳

summary.en: A Wodeyar kingdom that began as a Vijayanagara vassal, Mysore became a major military power under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan; after 1799 the restored Wodeyars ruled it as a princely state until it joined India.
summary.zh: 迈索尔原为毗奢耶那伽罗属下的沃迪亚尔王国，在海德尔·阿里和蒂普苏丹时期成为军事强国；1799年后复辟的沃迪亚尔王室以土邦形式统治，直至并入印度。

name.zh: 克里希纳罗阇·沃迪亚尔三世

sources.title: Kate Brittlebank, Tipu Sultan’s Search for Legitimacy (1997)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mysore
Wikidata Q266923

polities.note: The 1399 founding is traditional; the state was integrated into India in 1947–1950.

summary.en: A Malay maritime state that grew from Parameswara's settlement into the dominant entrepôt of the Straits. Its rulers adopted Islam, received Zheng He's fleets, and set the model of Malay kingship before the Portuguese conquest of 1511.
summary.zh: 由拜里米苏拉的聚落发展而来的马来海上国家，成为海峡地区首要的转口贸易港。其君主皈依伊斯兰教，接待郑和船队，奠定了马来王权的典范，1511年被葡萄牙征服。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Malacca Sultanate
Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals), trans. C. C. Brown (1952)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca Sultanate

summary.en: Founded by Lê Lợi after expelling the Ming, it reached its height under Lê Thánh Tông, who conquered Vijaya in 1471 and issued the Hồng Đức code. Later the Lê emperors were figureheads under the Mạc, Trịnh and Nguyễn lords until the Tây Sơn ended the dynasty.
summary.zh: 黎利驱逐明军后建立的王朝，在黎圣宗时期臻于鼎盛：1471年攻取毗阇耶，颁布《洪德法典》。后期黎帝成为莫氏、郑主和阮主控制下的傀儡，最终被西山朝终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Later Lê dynasty
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Later Lê dynasty early period

polities.note: Interrupted by the Mạc dynasty (1527–1533/92); the restored Lê (1533–1789) were largely nominal rulers.

image.file: Map of Later Lê dynasty during the reign of Lê Thánh Tông (1460-1497).png

capital.zh: 大不里士、加兹温，1598年起为伊斯法罕

summary.en: Founded by Shah Ismail I from a Sufi order of Ardabil, the Safavid state made Twelver Shi'ism Iran's official religion and fought the Ottomans for two centuries. It peaked under Abbas I at Isfahan; the Afghan capture of Isfahan in 1722 ended effective Safavid rule.
summary.zh: 由阿尔达比勒苏非教团出身的伊斯玛仪一世建立，萨法维王朝定十二伊玛目什叶派为伊朗国教，与奥斯曼争战两百年。阿拔斯一世在伊斯法罕时达到鼎盛；1722年阿富汗人攻陷伊斯法罕，萨法维的实际统治告终。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Safavid dynasty
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Safavids
Wikipedia: Safavid Iran

polities.note: Nominal Safavid shahs reigned under Nader's control until 1736.

summary.en: Rising from the small principality of Toungoo, Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung reunited Burma and built a vast but short-lived empire. A restored Toungoo state ruled from Ava until Mon rebels sacked it in 1752.
summary.zh: 东吁王朝从小邦东吁崛起，莽瑞体与莽应龙重新统一缅甸，建立了庞大但短暂的帝国。复兴后的东吁王朝以阿瓦为都，直至1752年被孟族起义军攻破。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Toungoo dynasty
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Toungoo dynasty

polities.note: Wikidata starts the dynasty in 1485 (Mingyi Nyo's accession as a vassal ruler); 1510 marks Toungoo's independence from Ava.

capital.zh: 阿格拉；法塔赫布尔西格里；拉合尔；德里（沙贾汉纳巴德）

summary.en: Founded by the Timurid Babur, the Mughal Empire ruled most of South Asia by 1700, combining Persianate court culture with a vast revenue system; after Aurangzeb it fragmented, and the British deposed the last emperor in 1857.
summary.zh: 莫卧儿帝国由帖木儿后裔巴布尔创建，至1700年已统治南亚大部，融合波斯化宫廷文化与庞大的税收体系；奥朗则布之后帝国分崩离析，1857年英国废黜末代皇帝。

sources.title: John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mughal dynasty
Wikidata Q33296

polities.note: Humayun was in exile 1540–1555 during the Sur interregnum.

image.artist: TRAJAN 117 This bitmap image was created with Windows Paint.

capital.zh: 哥打格德，后迁卡尔塔苏拉

summary.en: The last great Javanese kingdom before Dutch dominance. Sultan Agung conquered most of Java and twice besieged Batavia (1628–29); later succession wars drew in the VOC, and the 1755 Treaty of Giyanti split it into Yogyakarta and Surakarta.
summary.zh: 荷兰称霸前爪哇最后一个强大王国。苏丹阿贡征服爪哇大部，并两度围攻巴达维亚（1628—1629年）；此后的王位继承战争引来荷兰东印度公司介入，1755年《吉扬蒂条约》将其分裂为日惹与梭罗。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Mataram Sultanate

summary.en: The military government founded by Tokugawa Ieyasu that gave Japan some 250 years of peace through a balance between the shogun and some 260 domains, strict status order and controlled foreign relations, until it returned power to the emperor in 1867.
summary.zh: 德川家康建立的武家政权，通过将军与约二百六十个藩的平衡、严格的身份秩序以及受控的对外关系，使日本维持了约二百五十年的和平，1867年大政奉还天皇。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tokugawa shogunate
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Tokugawa shogunate

summary.en: Manchu dynasty proclaimed by Hong Taiji in 1636 as successor to Nurhaci's Later Jin. It entered Beijing in 1644, expanded to Xinjiang, Tibet and Taiwan under Kangxi and Qianlong, then faced Western wars and rebellion until the 1911 revolution.
summary.zh: 皇太极1636年改后金为大清，1644年入关定都北京。康雍乾时期版图扩至新疆、西藏与台湾，近代屡遭列强侵略与内乱，1912年清帝退位。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷1–25 本纪
Britannica: Qing dynasty

polities.note: The dynastic name Qing dates from 1636 (Hong Taiji), which Wikidata uses; Jiangshan-map's Qing period begins with the entry into Beijing in 1644.

capital.zh: 赖格尔；萨塔拉；浦那（佩什瓦）

summary.en: From Shivaji’s hill-fort kingdom the Marathas expanded under the Peshwas into a confederacy dominating much of India in the 18th century, until defeat at Panipat (1761) and the Anglo-Maratha wars ended their power in 1818.
summary.zh: 马拉塔人从希瓦吉的山堡王国起家，在佩什瓦领导下扩张为18世纪称雄印度大部的联盟，1761年帕尼帕特之败及其后的英马战争使其势力于1818年终结。

name.zh: 马达夫拉奥一世（佩什瓦）

sources.title: Stewart Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (New Cambridge History of India II.4, 1993)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Maratha confederacy
Wikidata Q83618

summary.en: Dynasty founded by Nader Shah, a Turkmen of the Afshar tribe who expelled the Afghans and Ottomans and was crowned on the Mughan plain in 1736. His campaigns reached Delhi, but after his assassination in 1747 the realm fragmented and his successors held only Khorasan until 1796.
summary.zh: 阿夫沙尔部落的土库曼人纳迪尔沙驱逐阿富汗人和奥斯曼人，1736年在穆甘草原加冕，建立此王朝。其征战远及德里，但1747年他遇刺后国家分裂，继承者仅保有呼罗珊至1796年。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Nader Shah
M. Axworthy, The Sword of Persia (2006)
Wikipedia: Afsharid dynasty

polities.note: Shahrukh's rule over Khorasan was interrupted and largely nominal.

capital.zh: 曼德勒（1857年起）；此前为阿瓦、阿摩罗补罗

summary.en: Founded by Alaungpaya, the last Burmese dynasty destroyed Ayutthaya, repelled Qing invasions and expanded into Arakan, Manipur and Assam, before losing three wars to Britain; Thibaw was deposed in 1885.
summary.zh: 由雍籍牙建立的缅甸末代王朝。它摧毁阿瑜陀耶、击退清军入侵，并向若开、曼尼普尔与阿萨姆扩张，后在三次英缅战争中战败，1885年锡袍王被废黜。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Konbaung dynasty
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Wikipedia: Konbaung dynasty

name.zh: 拉达那哥欣王朝（暹罗曼谷王朝）

summary.en: The Chakri kingdom founded by Rama I at Bangkok. Mongkut and Chulalongkorn modernised the state and ceded border territories, keeping Siam the only Southeast Asian country never colonised, until the 1932 revolution ended absolute monarchy.
summary.zh: 拉玛一世在曼谷建立的却克里王朝。蒙固王与朱拉隆功推行现代化改革并割让部分边地，使暹罗成为东南亚唯一未被殖民的国家，直至1932年革命结束君主专制。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Rattanakosin Kingdom (1782–1932)

polities.note: Prajadhipok reigned until 1935; his entry is truncated at the end of absolute monarchy.

summary.en: Turkmen dynasty founded by Agha Mohammad Khan, who made Tehran the capital and reunified Iran. In the 19th century it lost the Caucasus to Russia and faced growing British and Russian influence; the Constitutional Revolution limited royal power, and Reza Khan deposed the last shah in 1925.
summary.zh: 阿迦·穆罕默德汗建立的土库曼王朝，定都德黑兰并重新统一伊朗。19世纪将高加索领土割让给俄国，并受到英俄日益加深的影响；立宪革命限制了王权，1925年礼萨汗废黜末代国王。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Qajar dynasty
A. Amanat, Iran: A Modern History (2017)
Wikipedia: Qajar Iran

polities.note: Agha Mohammad Khan dominated Iran from 1789 but was crowned only in 1796.

summary.en: Ranjit Singh unified the Sikh misls into a Punjab state stretching from the Khyber Pass to Kashmir; after his death succession struggles weakened it, and two wars with the British ended in annexation in 1849.
summary.zh: 兰吉特·辛格将锡克各米斯尔统一为从开伯尔山口延伸至克什米尔的旁遮普国家；他死后王位之争削弱了国力，与英国的两次战争后于1849年被吞并。

sources.title: J. S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (New Cambridge History of India II.3, 1990)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ranjit Singh
Wikidata Q83572

polities.note: Dated from Ranjit Singh’s capture of Lahore (1799); Wikidata’s inception of 1733 refers to earlier Sikh confederacies.

summary.en: Founded by Gia Long after defeating the Tây Sơn, it ruled a unified Vietnam from Huế and named the country Việt Nam. France conquered it between 1858 and 1885, after which the emperors reigned under French protection until Bảo Đại abdicated in 1945.
summary.zh: 嘉隆帝击败西山朝后建立的王朝，以顺化为都统治统一的越南，并定国号“越南”。1858至1885年间被法国征服，此后皇帝在法国保护下名义在位，直至1945年保大帝退位。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nguyễn dynasty
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Complex of Hué Monuments
Wikipedia: Nguyễn dynasty

summary.en: Rebel theocratic state led by Hong Xiuquan, who claimed to be Christ's younger brother. Rising at Jintian in Guangxi, it held the lower Yangtze from Nanjing for over a decade before the Xiang Army took Tianjing in 1864.
summary.zh: 洪秀全以拜上帝会起事所建，1851年金田起义，1853年定都天京，据长江中下游十余年，1864年天京陷于湘军。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Taiping Rebellion
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷475 洪秀全传

summary.en: After the 1857 rebellion the British Crown took over the East India Company’s territories, ruling directly or through some 560 princely states until independence and partition in 1947.
summary.zh: 1857年起义后英国王室接管东印度公司领地，通过直接统治或约560个土邦进行间接统治，直至1947年印巴独立与分治。

name.zh: 维多利亚女王（1876年起兼印度女皇）

sources.title: Barbara D. Metcalf & Thomas R. Metcalf, A Concise History of Modern India, 3rd ed. (2012)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: British raj
Wikidata Q129286

summary.en: The modern imperial state created by the Meiji Restoration. It industrialised rapidly, won wars against China (1895) and Russia (1905), colonised Taiwan and Korea, and expanded across Asia until its defeat in 1945; the 1947 constitution replaced it.
summary.zh: 明治维新后建立的近代帝国。它迅速实现工业化，先后战胜清朝（1895年）与俄国（1905年），殖民台湾与朝鲜，并在亚洲各地扩张，1945年战败，1947年新宪法施行后终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Empire of Japan
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Wikipedia: Empire of Japan

polities.note: Hirohito reigned until 1989; his entry is truncated at the 1947 end of the Empire.

summary.en: King Gojong proclaimed himself emperor in 1897 to assert Korea's independence from Qing China. Despite modernising reforms, the empire became a Japanese protectorate in 1905 and was annexed in 1910.
summary.zh: 1897年高宗称帝，宣示朝鲜脱离清朝而独立。尽管推行了光武改革，大韩帝国仍于1905年沦为日本保护国，1910年被日本吞并。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Korean Empire

name.zh: 日本殖民统治时期的朝鲜

summary.en: Korea was governed as the colony of Chōsen by a Japanese Governor-General from 1910 until Japan's defeat in 1945. The period saw industrial development for Japanese ends, forced assimilation policies and wartime labour mobilisation.
summary.zh: 1910年至1945年日本战败期间，朝鲜作为日本殖民地“朝鲜”由朝鲜总督统治。这一时期出现了服务于日本的工业开发、强制同化政策与战时劳动力征用。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Korea under Japanese rule
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)

summary.en: Kingdom proclaimed by Abdulaziz ibn Saud in 1932 after three decades of conquest across central Arabia and the Hejaz. As custodian of Mecca and Medina and, from 1938, a major oil producer, it became one of the most influential states of the Middle East; it remains an absolute monarchy.
